text_mt: He rams it all around three times with the staff of the Maitrāvaruṇa with: "Make firm the sacred word!"

sanskrit_iast: samam bhūmi kṛtvādbhir upasicya viṣṇoḥ karmāṇi \\ iti vācayati yūpam anvārabdham //
meaning: समम् भूमि कृत्वाद्भिर् उपसिच्य विष्णोः कर्माणि \\ इति वाचयति यूपम् अन्वारब्धम् //
text_mt: Having made the ground level and having sprinkled it with water, he makes [the sacrificer], holding onto the post, recite: "The deeds of Viṣṇu..."
And as he looks at the head-ring: "That [highest step] of Viṣṇu..."
He prompts [the Hotṛ to recite] for [the post] being girded.

sanskrit_iast: triguṇā trivyāmā kauśī raśanā tayā nābhimātre trivṛtaṃ parivyayati parivīr asi \\ iti //
meaning: त्रिगुणा त्रिव्यामा कौशी रशना तया नाभिमात्रे त्रिवृतं परिव्ययति परिवीर् असि \\ इति //
text_mt: A three-stranded girdle made of kuśa grass, three fathoms long—with it he girds [the post] three times around at navel height with the formula: "A girdle art thou!"
Joining [the ends], he inserts the end into one [of the coils].

sanskrit_iast: yūpaśakalam asyām avagūhaty uttareṇāgniṣṭhām \\ divaḥ sūnur asi \\ iti //
meaning: यूपशकलम् अस्याम् अवगूहत्य् उत्तरेणाग्निष्ठाम् \\ दिवः सूनुर् असि \\ इति //
text_mt: He tucks a chip of the sacrificial post into it north of the Agniṣṭha face with [the formula], "You are the son of heaven."

sanskrit_iast: upāvīr asi \\ iti tṛṇam ādāya tena paśum upaspṛśati \\ upa devān iti //
meaning: उपावीर् असि \\ इति तृणम् आदाय तेन पशुम् उपस्पृशति \\ उप देवान् इति //
text_mt: Taking a blade of grass with [the formula], "You are the approacher," he touches the sacrificial animal with it, [saying,] "Go near to the gods."
At the sprinkling, [the deity is specified] according to the words of the mantra;
He churns the fire and performs [the rites] up to the offering;

sanskrit_iast: dviguṇaraśanayā dvivyāmayā kauśyā pāśaṃ kṛtvāntarāśṛṅgam abhidakṣiṇaṃ badhnāti \\ ṛtasya tvā \\ iti //
meaning: द्विगुणरशनया द्विव्यामया कौश्या पाशं कृत्वान्तराशृङ्गम् अभिदक्षिणं बध्नाति \\ ऋतस्य त्वा \\ इति //
text_mt: Having made a noose with a two-stranded, two-fathom kuśa rope, he ties [it] between the horns clockwise with [the formula], "[I bind] you [with the cord] of truth."
[The animal] is dedicated to Indra-Agni, to Sūrya, or to Prajāpati,

sanskrit_iast: adbhyas tvā \\ iti paśuṃ prokṣaṇībhiḥ prokṣati //
meaning: अद्भ्यस् त्वा \\ इति पशुं प्रोक्षणीभिः प्रोक्षति //
text_mt: He sprinkles the sacrificial animal with the sprinkling waters with [the formula], "[I sprinkle] you for the waters."

sanskrit_iast:
apāṃ perur ity āsya upagṛhṇāti //
āpo devīr ity adhastād upokṣati //
meaning:
अपां पेरुर् इत्य् आस्य उपगृह्णाति //
आपो देवीर् इत्य् अधस्ताद् उपोक्षति //
text_mt: He holds [water] under its mouth with [the formula], "The drinker of waters..."; / he sprinkles beneath [its body] with [the formula], "Divine waters..."
He performs [the rites] beginning with the call for the fuel bundle up to the fore-offerings.

sanskrit_iast: uttarāghāram āghārya paśuṃ pūrvam̐ samanakti lalāṭām̐saśroṇiṣu saṃ te \\ iti pratimantram //
meaning: उत्तराघारम् आघार्य पशुं पूर्वम्̐ समनक्ति ललाटाम्̐सश्रोणिषु सं ते \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: Having made the northern Āghāra libation, he first anoints the sacrificial animal on the forehead, the shoulders, and the hips, with the respective mantras: "May your [breath unite with breath]..."

sanskrit_iast: pravṛtya hotāram āśrāvyāha \\ agnir ha daivīnāṃ viśāṃ puraetā \\ ayaṃ yajamāno manuṣyāṇām̐ sunvann iti sutye tayor asthūri gārhapatyaṃ dīdayachatam̐ himā dvā yū \ rādhām̐sīt sampṛñcānāv asampṛñcānau tanvas \\ iti //
meaning: प्रवृत्य होतारम् आश्राव्याह \\ अग्निर् ह दैवीनां विशां पुरएता \\ अयं यजमानो मनुष्याणाम्̐ सुन्वन्न् इति सुत्ये तयोर् अस्थूरि गार्हपत्यं दीदयछतम्̐ हिमा द्वा यू \ राधाम्̐सीत् सम्पृञ्चानाव् असम्पृञ्चानौ तन्वस् \\ इति //
text_mt: Having chosen the Hotṛ and having caused [the Agnīdh] to announce, he says: "Agni is the leader of the divine subjects; this sacrificer, pressing [soma]—[if it is] at a soma feast—[is the leader] of human subjects; may their Gārhapatya fire shine unshared for a hundred winters; may the two [sacrificers]... combining their wealth, not combining their bodies..."

sanskrit_iast: maitrāvaruṇāya daṇḍaṃ prayachati mitrāvaruṇayos tvā praśāstroḥ praśiṣā prayachāmi \\ iti //
meaning: मैत्रावरुणाय दण्डं प्रयछति मित्रावरुणयोस् त्वा प्रशास्त्रोः प्रशिषा प्रयछामि \\ इति //
text_mt: He gives the staff to the Maitrāvaruṇa with [the formula], "Under the direction of Mitra and Varuṇa, the directors, I hand [it] over to you."
[The staff should be] of udumbara wood, reaching up to the sacrificer's mouth;

sanskrit_iast: samaitrāvaruṇe preṣya \\ ity āha yajasthāne vacane //
meaning: समैत्रावरुणे प्रेष्य \\ इत्य् आह यजस्थाने वचने //
text_mt: In a rite with the Maitrāvaruṇa, he says "Prompt [the Hotṛ]" where the word "Offer" occurs.

sanskrit_iast: daśeṣṭvā prayājān āha śāsam āhara \\ iti //
meaning: दशेष्ट्वा प्रयाजान् आह शासम् आहर \\ इति //
text_mt: Having offered ten fore-offerings, he says, "Bring the slaughtering knife."

sanskrit_iast: svarum ādāyāktvobhau juhvagre tābhyāṃ paśor lalāṭam upaspṛśati ghṛtenāktau \\ iti //
meaning: स्वरुम् आदायाक्त्वोभौ जुह्वग्रे ताभ्यां पशोर् ललाटम् उपस्पृशति घृतेनाक्तौ \\ इति //
text_mt: Taking the chip of the sacrificial post and anointing both it and the tip of the Juhū, he touches the forehead of the sacrificial animal with the two, with [the formula], "Anointed with ghee..."

sanskrit_iast: svarum avaguhyāsiṃ prayachann āha \\ eṣā te prajñātāśrir astu \\ iti //
meaning: स्वरुम् अवगुह्यासिं प्रयछन्न् आह \\ एषा ते प्रज्ञाताश्रिर् अस्तु \\ इति //
text_mt: Having tucked away the chip of the post, handing over the slaughtering knife, he says, "May this be your well-known edge."
Having placed down the two ladles, he marks out [the ground] for the Śāmitra fire north of the Cātvāla pit.
He makes [the Hotṛ] recite for [the animal] being carried around with fire.

sanskrit_iast: āhavanīyolmukam ādāyāgnīt triḥ samantaṃ paryeti paśvājyaśāmitradeśayūpacātvālāhavanīyān //
meaning: आहवनीयोल्मुकम् आदायाग्नीत् त्रिः समन्तं पर्येति पश्वाज्यशामित्रदेशयूपचात्वालाहवनीयान् //
text_mt: Taking a firebrand from the Āhavanīya, the Agnīdh walks around three times entirely enclosing the animal, the ghee, the place of the Śāmitra fire, the sacrificial post, the Cātvāla pit, and the Āhavanīya;
Throwing back the firebrand, he walks around in the reverse direction for as long.
Taking [it] up again, he proceeds northward,
The Pratiprasthātṛ touches it from behind with two omentum-cooking spits made of kārṣmarya wood, one forked and one unforked.

sanskrit_iast: veditṛṇe adhvaryur ādāyāśrāvyāha \\ upapreṣya hotar havyā devebhyas \\ iti //
meaning: वेदितृणे अध्वर्युर् आदायाश्राव्याह \\ उपप्रेष्य होतर् हव्या देवेभ्यस् \\ इति //
text_mt: Taking two blades of grass from the altar and causing [the Agnīdh] to announce, the Adhvaryu says: "Hotṛ, prompt [the deities] to the oblations for the gods."
He makes [the sacrificer] recite: "O wealthy one, in the sacrificer..."
He deposits the fire in the Śāmitra place;

sanskrit_iast: paścāt tṛṇam upāsyati varṣo varṣīyasi \\ iti //
meaning: पश्चात् तृणम् उपास्यति वर्षो वर्षीयसि \\ इति //
text_mt: He casts a blade of grass behind [the fire] with [the formula], "O highest one, upon the higher..."
Upon that [grass] they kill it, with its head to the west and its feet to the north,
Having seized its mouth, they suffocate it without letting it cry out,
Having gone [back], they sit facing away from the Āhavanīya.
He should only say, "Quiet [the animal]; it has departed."
He makes an offering with [the formula], "Svāhā to the gods!"

sanskrit_iast: saṃjñaptaḥ paśur iti prokte śetāṃ nu muhūrtam ity āhāsome //
meaning: संज्ञप्तः पशुर् इति प्रोक्ते शेतां नु मुहूर्तम् इत्य् आहासोमे //
text_mt: When it is announced, "The animal is quieted," he says, "Let it lie for a moment," [in a rite] other than a soma sacrifice.
He makes an offering with [the formula], "To the gods, svāhā!"

sanskrit_iast: vapāśrapaṇībhyāṃ niyojanīṃ cātvāle prāsyati māhir bhūs \\ iti //
meaning: वपाश्रपणीभ्यां नियोजनीं चात्वाले प्रास्यति माहिर् भूस् \\ इति //
text_mt: With the two omentum-cooking spits he throws the tethering cord into the Cātvāla pit with [the formula], "Do not become a serpent!"
He says, "Pratiprasthātṛ, bring up the wife [of the sacrificer]!"

sanskrit_iast: pānnejanahastāṃ vācayati nayan namas ta ātāna \\ iti //
meaning: पान्नेजनहस्तां वाचयति नयन् नमस् त आतान \\ इति //
text_mt: Leading [her], who has water for washing feet in her hand, he makes her recite: "Homage to you, who are stretched out..."
The wife purifies the vital breaths of the animal.

sanskrit_iast: mukhaṃ nāsike cakṣuṣī karṇau nābhiṃ meḍhraṃ pāyuṃ pādānt saṃhṛtya vācaṃ te śundhāmi \\ iti pratimantam //
meaning: मुखं नासिके चक्षुषी कर्णौ नाभिं मेढ्रं पायुं पादान्त् संहृत्य वाचं ते शुन्धामि \\ इति प्रतिमन्तम् //
text_mt: Bringing together the mouth, the two nostrils, the two eyes, the two ears, the navel, the penis, the anus, [and] the feet, with a mantra for each: "I purify your speech..."
With the remainder, she and the sacrificer sprinkle along [the body], beginning from the head:
"What of you is raw..." — [upon] the limbs;

sanskrit_iast: śam ahobhyas \\ iti paścāt paśor niṣiñcataḥ //
meaning: शम् अहोभ्यस् \\ इति पश्चात् पशोर् निषिञ्चतः //
text_mt: "Peace from the days..." — they pour out [the remaining water] behind the animal.

sanskrit_iast: uttānaṃ paśuṃ kṛtvāgreṇa nābhiṃ tṛṇaṃ nidadhāti \\ oṣadhe \\ iti //
meaning: उत्तानं पशुं कृत्वाग्रेण नाभिं तृणं निदधाति \\ ओषधे \\ इति //
text_mt: Having placed the animal supine, he lays a blade of grass in front of the navel: "O herb!"

sanskrit_iast: svadhite \\ iti prajñātayābhinidhāya chittvāgram̐ savye kṛtvā dakṣiṇena mūlam ubhayato 'nakti lohitena rakṣasām iti //
meaning: स्वधिते \\ इति प्रज्ञातयाभिनिधाय छित्त्वाग्रम्̐ सव्ये कृत्वा दक्षिणेन मूलम् उभयतो ऽनक्ति लोहितेन रक्षसाम् इति //
text_mt: Having placed [the knife] down [upon the grass] with its recognizable [blade], saying: "O knife!", and having cut the tip, having placed it in the left [hand], he anoints the base on both sides with the right [hand] with blood, saying: "Of the Rakṣases..."
The sacrificer steps upon [it], saying: "Here I [step upon]..."

sanskrit_iast: vapām utkhidya vapāśrapaṇyau prorṇauti ghṛtena dyāvāpṛthivī iti //
meaning: वपाम् उत्खिद्य वपाश्रपण्यौ प्रोर्णौति घृतेन द्यावापृथिवी इति //
text_mt: Having extracted the omentum, he wraps the two omentum-cooking spits [with it], saying: "With clarified butter, O Heaven and Earth!"
Having trimmed [it] and having washed it down at the Cātvāla pit, he heats it over the Śāmitra fire.
The Agnīdh priest throws a portion of the Śāmitra fire into the Āhavanīya fire.
And the Adhvaryu [throws] the tip of the grass [into the Āhavanīya], saying: "For Vāyu, the bird..."

sanskrit_iast: uttaratas tiṣṭhan pratapya vapām antarā yūpāgnī hṛtvā dakṣiṇataḥ pratiprasthātā śrapayati parītya //
meaning: उत्तरतस् तिष्ठन् प्रतप्य वपाम् अन्तरा यूपाग्नी हृत्वा दक्षिणतः प्रतिप्रस्थाता श्रपयति परीत्य //
text_mt: Standing on the north side and having heated the omentum, having carried it between the sacrificial post and the fire, having walked around, the Pratiprasthātṛ cooks it on the south.
He bastes the omentum with the sruva, saying: "Agni [has accepted] of the clarified butter..."

sanskrit_iast: śṛtāyām \\ śṛtā pracara \\ ity āha pratiprasthātā //
meaning: शृतायाम् \\ शृता प्रचर \\ इत्य् आह प्रतिप्रस्थाता //
text_mt: When it is cooked, the Pratiprasthātṛ says: "It is cooked; proceed!"
[He commands:] "Prompt [the Hotṛ] for the Svāhākṛti offerings!"
Having offered the omentum, he bastes it with clotted butter.
First [he bastes] the Dhruvā ladle, if the two portions of clarified butter [are offered here].

sanskrit_iast: vapayā cariṣyann upastīrya hiraṇyam avadhāya vapām avadyann āha \\ indrāgnibhyāṃ chāgasya vapāyai medaso 'nubrūhi \\ iti
meaning: वपया चरिष्यन्न् उपस्तीर्य हिरण्यम् अवधाय वपाम् अवद्यन्न् आह \\ इन्द्राग्निभ्यां छागस्य वपायै मेदसो ऽनुब्रूहि \\ इति
text_mt: About to proceed with the omentum, having spread under [clarified butter], having deposited gold, while cutting off the omentum, he says: "Recite [the invitatory verse] for Indra and Agni, for the omentum and fat of the goat!"
In a soma sacrifice, having deposited gold, there is a double basting.

sanskrit_iast:
āśrāvyāha \\ indrāgnibhyāṃ chāgasya vapāṃ medaḥ preṣya \\ iti //
(6.6.26) prasthitam iti ca prasute //
meaning:
आश्राव्याह \\ इन्द्राग्निभ्यां छागस्य वपां मेदः प्रेष्य \\ इति //
(6.6.26) प्रस्थितम् इति च प्रसुते //
text_mt: Having called for the response, he says: "Prompt [the Hotṛ] for Indra and Agni for the omentum and fat of the goat!" And in a pressed-soma rite: "...set forth!"

sanskrit_iast: hutvā vapāśrapaṇyāv anuprāsyati prācīṃ viśākhāṃ pratīcīm itarām \\ svāhākṛte iti //
meaning: हुत्वा वपाश्रपण्याव् अनुप्रास्यति प्राचीं विशाखां प्रतीचीम् इतराम् \\ स्वाहाकृते इति //
text_mt: Having offered [it], he throws the two omentum-cooking spits after: the forked one pointing east, the other pointing west, saying: "O Svāhākṛti offerings!"

sanskrit_iast: cātvāle mārjayante sapatnīkās \\ idam āpaḥ pravahata \\ iti //
meaning: चात्वाले मार्जयन्ते सपत्नीकास् \\ इदम् आपः प्रवहत \\ इति //
text_mt: Together with the wife, they purify themselves at the Cātvāla pit, saying: "O waters, wash away this..."
Or [he may be] one of the officiating priests, because of not being prescribed for the Śāmitra fire;
However, the soma-seller is another person, because of connection with a Śūdra.
He cuts off the limbs without breaking [bones]:

sanskrit_iast: hṛdayaṃ jihvāṃ kroḍam̐ savyasakthipūrvanaḍakaṃ pārśve yakṛdvṛkkau gudamadhyaṃ dakṣiṇā śroṇir iti jauhavāni //
meaning: हृदयं जिह्वां क्रोडम्̐ सव्यसक्थिपूर्वनडकं पार्श्वे यकृद्वृक्कौ गुदमध्यं दक्षिणा श्रोणिर् इति जौहवानि //
text_mt: The heart, the tongue, the breast, the front shank of the left thigh, the two flanks, the liver, the two kidneys, the middle of the rectum, [and] the right buttock: these are the portions for the Juhū ladle.

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇasakthipūrvanaḍakaṃ gudatṛtīyāṇiṣṭham̐ savyā śroṇir ity aupabhṛtāni //
meaning: दक्षिणसक्थिपूर्वनडकं गुदतृतीयाणिष्ठम्̐ सव्या श्रोणिर् इत्य् औपभृतानि //
text_mt: The front shank of the right thigh, the third and lowest part of the rectum, [and] the left buttock: these are the portions for the Upabhṛt ladle.
The largest [portion of the rectum] is for the Upayaj offerings.
The division occurs at the time of the cutting off [of portions].
And he cuts off the entrails and the hindquarters.
And if he wishes, the lungs, spleen, supra-udder flesh, and pericardium.

meaning: उदरमेदो ऽवशिष्टं गुदे प्रास्यति कृशश् चेत् //
text_mt: If [the animal] is lean, he throws the remaining abdominal fat into the rectum.

sanskrit_iast: śvabhra ūvadhyam avadhāya tasmin lohitam̐ rakṣasām iti //
meaning: श्वभ्र ऊवध्यम् अवधाय तस्मिन् लोहितम्̐ रक्षसाम् इति //
text_mt: Having deposited the undigested food of the stomach in a pit, [he throws] the blood into it, saying: "Of the Rakṣases..."
Having pierced the heart on a spit, he cooks it over the Śāmitra fire;
For the animal's deity, there is a sacrificial cake on eleven potsherds.
Or it belongs to Agni and Soma, because of the specific prescription.
The invocation of the preparer of the oblation is right here, because the sacrifice is one.
While cutting off [the cake-portion], he says: "Recite [the invitatory verse] for Indra and Agni for the sacrificial cake!"
And he cuts off [a portion] into the Upabhṛt ladle, as in the case of the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.
He prompts [the Hotṛ] with: "...the sacrificial cake for Indra and Agni!"
Having offered, having brought together [the clarified butter], and having given [it] to Agni;
In the place of the modified deity, the unmodified [deity Agni] is the modification for all, because of unity.
Or as traditionally recited, because of the difference of utterance.
There is non-performance of the other [cake-offering], because they serve the same purpose.

sanskrit_iast: paśur dakṣiṇā dhenur varo vā mārjite //
meaning: पशुर् दक्षिणा धेनुर् वरो वा मार्जिते //
text_mt: When [the vessel] is cleaned, the sacrificial gift is an animal, a milch-cow, or an excellent object.

sanskrit_iast: śamitāram̐ śāsti triḥ pracyāvayatāt \ triḥ pracyutasya hṛdayam uttamaṃ kurutāt \ yat tvā pṛchāchṛtam̐ haviḥ śamitā3r iti śṛtam ity eva brūtān na śṛtaṃ bhagavo na śṛtaṃ hi \\ iti //
meaning: शमितारम्̐ शास्ति त्रिः प्रच्यावयतात् \ त्रिः प्रच्युतस्य हृदयम् उत्तमं कुरुतात् \ यत् त्वा पृछाछृतम्̐ हविः शमिता3र् इति शृतम् इत्य् एव ब्रूतान् न शृतं भगवो न शृतं हि \\ इति //
text_mt: He instructs the slaughterer: "Cause [the cooking pot] to be moved three times; of what has been moved three times, place the heart at the very top; when one asks you: 'Is the oblation cooked, O slaughterer?', say only: 'Cooked!', not: 'Cooked, sir!', for it is indeed cooked!"
When it has been moved three times, having pulled out the heart, he places it on the very top;

sanskrit_iast: juhvā pṛṣadājyasyādāyopaniṣkramya pṛcchati śṛtam̐ haviḥ śamitā3r iti trir abhikrāmam //
meaning: जुह्वा पृषदाज्यस्यादायोपनिष्क्रम्य पृच्छति शृतम्̐ हविः शमिता3र् इति त्रिर् अभिक्रामम् //
text_mt: Taking clotted ghee with the Juhū and stepping out, he asks, stepping forward three times: "Is the oblation cooked, O slaughterer?"
When it has been announced, he says in a low voice: "[It is] for the gods."

sanskrit_iast: saṃ te manas \\ iti hṛdayam abhighārya sarvam //
meaning: सं ते मनस् \\ इति हृदयम् अभिघार्य सर्वम् //
text_mt: Having basted all the heart with the mantra: "May your mind [unite with mind]..."

sanskrit_iast: paśvasī vapāvad dhṛtvā dakṣiṇataḥ pratiprasthātā vedyāṃ plakṣaśākhāsv avadyati //
meaning: पश्वसी वपावद् धृत्वा दक्षिणतः प्रतिप्रस्थाता वेद्यां प्लक्षशाखास्व् अवद्यति //
text_mt: having grasped [the organs] as [was done] with the omentum with the mantra: "You are an animal...", the Pratiprasthātṛ priest portions them out on the vedi upon plakṣa branches on the south.
He spreads under [clarified butter] in the Juhū and Upabhṛt ladles, and in the ladle for offering the fat and in the dish.

sanskrit_iast: manotāyai haviṣo 'vadīyamānasyānubrūhi \\ ity ukte srucor avadyati yathoktaṃ dvirdviḥ //
meaning: मनोतायै हविषो ऽवदीयमानस्यानुब्रूहि \\ इत्य् उक्ते स्रुचोर् अवद्यति यथोक्तं द्विर्द्विः //
text_mt: When it is said: "Recite [the invitatory verse] for Manotā while the oblation is being portioned out", he portions out twice into each of the two ladles as prescribed.

sanskrit_iast: reḍ asi \\ iti vasāṃ gṛhītvā dvir abhighārya prayutam iti pārśvena sam̐sṛjaty asinā vā //
meaning: रेड् असि \\ इति वसां गृहीत्वा द्विर् अभिघार्य प्रयुतम् इति पार्श्वेन सम्̐सृजत्य् असिना वा //
text_mt: Having taken the fat with the mantra: "You are bright...", having basted it twice, he stirs it with the rib or with the knife, [reciting]: "[United with] the mixed..."

sanskrit_iast: śeṣam iḍāpātryām āsicya kroḍam anasthīni ca prāsyati śroṇivarjam //
meaning: शेषम् इडापात्र्याम् आसिच्य क्रोडम् अनस्थीनि च प्रास्यति श्रोणिवर्जम् //
text_mt: Having poured the remainder into the iḍā-dish, he throws in the breast-meat and the boneless parts, with the exception of the rump.

sanskrit_iast: jāghanīgudaṃ nidhāyāha \\ indrāgnibhyāṃ chāgasya haviṣo 'nubrūhi \\ iti //
meaning: जाघनीगुदं निधायाह \\ इन्द्राग्निभ्यां छागस्य हविषो ऽनुब्रूहि \\ इति //
text_mt: Having placed down the tail and rectum, he says: "Recite [the invitatory verse] for Indra and Agni for the oblation of the goat."

sanskrit_iast: āśrāvyāha \\ indrāgnibhyāṃ chāgasya haviḥ preṣya \\ iti //
meaning: आश्राव्याह \\ इन्द्राग्निभ्यां छागस्य हविः प्रेष्य \\ इति //
text_mt: Having called for recitation, he says: "Prompt [the Hotṛ to recite the offering verse] for Indra and Agni for the oblation of the goat."
And when he has been impelled, [he adds]: "...set forth."

sanskrit_iast: ardharcāntare yājyāyai vasaikadeśaṃ juhoti ghṛtaṃ ghṛtapāvānas \\ iti //
meaning: अर्धर्चान्तरे याज्यायै वसैकदेशं जुहोति घृतं घृतपावानस् \\ इति //
text_mt: At the interval between the two half-verses of the offering verse, he offers a portion of the fat with the mantra: "Ghee, O ghee-drinkers..."

sanskrit_iast: daivatam̐ hutvā pradakṣiṇam āvṛtya juhvā pṛṣadājyasyopaghnann āha vanaspataye 'nubrūhi \\ iti //
meaning: दैवतम्̐ हुत्वा प्रदक्षिणम् आवृत्य जुह्वा पृषदाज्यस्योपघ्नन्न् आह वनस्पतये ऽनुब्रूहि \\ इति //
text_mt: Having offered the primary oblation to the deity, having turned clockwise, drawing up clotted butter with the Juhū ladle, he says: "Recite [the invitatory verse] for Vanaspati."
Having called for recitation, he says: "Prompt [the Hotṛ to recite the offering verse] for Vanaspati."
Having offered, having brought together [the portions], [he offers the oblation] to Agni Sviṣṭakṛt.

sanskrit_iast: pratyetya vā diśo vyāghārayati vasāśeṣeṇa vājinavat //
meaning: प्रत्येत्य वा दिशो व्याघारयति वसाशेषेण वाजिनवत् //
text_mt: Or having returned, he sprinkles the quarters with the remainder of the fat, like the vājina.
He touches the animal with the mantra: "The breath belonging to Indra..."
Or having portioned out the iḍā before the offering.
When it has been invoked, [he gives] the entrails to the Agnīdh priest.

sanskrit_iast: mārjite preṣyati \\ agnīd aupayajān aṅgarān āhara \\ upayayaṣṭar upasīda \ brahman prasthāsyāmi \ samidham ādhāyāgnim agnīt saṃmṛḍḍhi \\ iti //
meaning: मार्जिते प्रेष्यति \\ अग्नीद् औपयजान् अङ्गरान् आहर \\ उपययष्टर् उपसीद \ ब्रह्मन् प्रस्थास्यामि \ समिधम् आधायाग्निम् अग्नीत् संमृड्ढि \\ इति //
text_mt: When they have cleansed themselves, he summons: "Agnīdh, bring the embers for the upayaj-offerings; Upayaj-offerer, sit down; Brahman, I shall proceed; having placed fuel on the fire, Agnīdh, cleanse [the fire]!"

sanskrit_iast: śāmitrād aṅgārān āhṛtya vediśroṇyāṃ nivapaty uttarasyām //
meaning: शामित्राद् अङ्गारान् आहृत्य वेदिश्रोण्यां निवपत्य् उत्तरस्याम् //
text_mt: Having brought the embers from the Śāmitra fire, he scatters them on the northern hip of the vedi.
Or in the soma sacrifice, from the Āgnīdhra fire onto the Hotṛ's hearth.

sanskrit_iast: pratiprasthātopayajati gudatṛtīyasya prachedam anuyājeṣu samudraṃ gacha \\ iti pratimantram //
meaning: प्रतिप्रस्थातोपयजति गुदतृतीयस्य प्रछेदम् अनुयाजेषु समुद्रं गछ \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: During the after-offerings, the Pratiprasthātṛ priest offers the upayaj-oblations of severed pieces of the third part of the rectum, each with its mantra: "Go to the ocean..."

sanskrit_iast: prativaṣaṭkāram̐ hutvā mano me \\ iti mukhopasparśanam //
meaning: प्रतिवषट्कारम्̐ हुत्वा मनो मे \\ इति मुखोपस्पर्शनम् //
text_mt: After each vaṣaṭ-call, having offered, there is the touching of the mouth with the mantra: "My mind..."

sanskrit_iast: anuyājānte svaruṃ juhoti divaṃ te dhūmas \\ iti //
meaning: अनुयाजान्ते स्वरुं जुहोति दिवं ते धूमस् \\ इति //
text_mt: At the end of the after-offerings, he offers the chip of the sacrificial post with the mantra: "May your smoke [reach] the sky..."
The unyoking of the ladles is for the deity of the animal and for Vanaspati.
The offerings to the wives of the gods are performed with the tail.
Turning it supine, he portions out [a piece] for the wives of the gods.
Turning it over, [he portions out] for Agni Gṛhapati.
Or all [are performed] with the tail, because there is no distinction.
Having offered the sacrificial grass, taking the heart-spit, they go to the water.
Or having stood by the Āhavanīya fire, if [it is the time of] the observance and the like.

sanskrit_iast: abhyavetya śuṣkārdrasaṃdhau hṛdayaśūlam upagūhati śug asi \ tam abhiśoca yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmas \\ māpo mauṣadhīr iti ca //
meaning: अभ्यवेत्य शुष्कार्द्रसंधौ हृदयशूलम् उपगूहति शुग् असि \ तम् अभिशोच यो ऽस्मान् द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्मस् \\ मापो मौषधीर् इति च //
text_mt: Having descended [into the water], he buries the heart-spit at the junction of the dry and the wet, with the mantras: "You are sorrow; inflict sorrow upon him who hates us and whom we hate" and "Neither the waters nor the plants..."

sanskrit_iast: glāyann udapātraṃ niṣicya pūrveṇa yūpaṃ yathoktam upagūhati //
meaning: ग्लायन्न् उदपात्रं निषिच्य पूर्वेण यूपं यथोक्तम् उपगूहति //
text_mt: If exhausted, having poured out a jar of water to the east of the sacrificial post, he buries it as prescribed.

sanskrit_iast: dhāmnodhāmnaḥ \ sumitriyā nas \\ ity upaspṛśanty apaḥ //
meaning: धाम्नोधाम्नः \ सुमित्रिया नस् \\ इत्य् उपस्पृशन्त्य् अपः //
text_mt: They touch water with the mantras: "From abode to abode..." and "May [the waters be] friendly to us..."
Or the former [mantra] is the conclusion of the burying rite.
Or the consecration [of the water] is with the latter [mantra].
Not in the soma sacrifice, with the exception of the Anūbandhyā cow.
The placing of the fuel stick is like that in the Varuṇapraghāsa rites.
Having discharged the observance, [there is an offering] of four ladlings in the eastern of the western fires, like the offering to the sacrificial post.
Or [the fire is] produced by churning or re-ascended [from the churning sticks].
He should give [dakṣiṇā] in this rite according to his ability.

sanskrit_iast: agniṃ praṇīya sadohavirdhānāgnīdhrahotṛdhiṣṇyān yathoktaṃ gṛhītvājyāny āgnīdhrapraṇayanam agnīṣomīyadarśanāt //
meaning: अग्निं प्रणीय सदोहविर्धानाग्नीध्रहोतृधिष्ण्यान् यथोक्तं गृहीत्वाज्यान्य् आग्नीध्रप्रणयनम् अग्नीषोमीयदर्शनात् //
text_mt: Having brought forward the fire, having taken the sadas, the havirdhāna shed, and the Āgnīdhra and Hotṛ hearths as prescribed, and the clarified butters, the bringing forward of the Āgnīdhra fire [takes place], because it is seen in the Agnīṣomīya animal sacrifice.
Spoon-offerings have the characteristics of the Full-Moon sacrifice, because the term 'juhoti' is without distinction.
those that originate in an alien procedure are merely juhoti-offerings.
In cooked-food sacrifices, there is no offering of the whole of the portioned portion;

sanskrit_iast: agnihotre tad asya pākayajñasyeva \\ iti śruteḥ //
meaning: अग्निहोत्रे तद् अस्य पाकयज्ञस्येव \\ इति श्रुतेः //
text_mt: because of the Vedic text concerning the Agnihotra: 'Indeed, this is like his cooked-food sacrifice.'

sanskrit_iast: vapām̐ hutvā trīṇi pañca sarvāṇi vāvadyati //
meaning: वपाम्̐ हुत्वा त्रीणि पञ्च सर्वाणि वावद्यति //
text_mt: Having offered the omentum, he cuts off three, five, or all portions;
if all [parts] are not [offered], the Sviṣṭakṛt [offering is made] from the remainder.
The offering is [made] together with the boiled-rice mess.
Because of the Vedic text: 'Having sacrificed with the New- and Full-Moon sacrifices, one should sacrifice with another [rite].'
Or with soma, if the soma is arranged, because of the primacy of soma in the establishment of the fires;
One whose family has not drunk soma for two generations, having immolated a set-free [heifer] for Indra and Agni, [performs it].

He chooses sixteen officiating priests: Brahman, Udgātṛ, Hotṛ, Adhvaryu, Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, Prastotṛ, Maitrāvaruṇa, Pratiprasthātṛ, Potṛ, Pratihartṛ, Acchāvāka, Neṣṭṛ, Agnīdh, Subrahmaṇya, Grāvastut, and Unnetṛ;
the others are their assistants according to their Veda.
The Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, the Agnīdh, and the Potṛ belong to the Brahman.
They select the sacrificial site:
equal in measure on all sides to a sacrificial ground;
whatever [site] officiating priests learned [in the Veda choose].
On the western edge, where the roots of plants have been dug out, they erect a shed;

sanskrit_iast: dīkṣāprabhṛti śuklapakṣe pañcamīm̐ saptamīṃ vā prasutaḥ //
meaning: दीक्षाप्रभृति शुक्लपक्षे पञ्चमीम्̐ सप्तमीं वा प्रसुतः //
text_mt: Starting from the consecration, the soma pressing takes place on the fifth or the seventh [day] in the bright half of the month.
If the time has passed, the prescribed rite [takes place] because its time has arrived;
On an auspicious day take place the consecration, the purchase [of soma], the pressing, and the concluding rite;
if there is a conflict between the beginning and the concluding rite;

sanskrit_iast: dīkṣāsu yūpachedanaṃ yūpāhutiṃ prāg ghutvā yūpānte vāgniṃ mathitvā dīkṣitasyāgnihomapratiṣedhaśruteḥ //
meaning: दीक्षासु यूपछेदनं यूपाहुतिं प्राग् घुत्वा यूपान्ते वाग्निं मथित्वा दीक्षितस्याग्निहोमप्रतिषेधश्रुतेः //
text_mt: During the consecration days, the cutting of the sacrificial post [takes place] after having first offered the oblation for the sacrificial post, or after churning the fire near the sacrificial post, because of the Vedic prohibition against offering into the fire for one who is consecrated;
or both, the oblation and the cutting, [take place] at the time of erection, because of proximity.

sanskrit_iast: samārohyāgnī śālāstambhaṃ pūrvārdhyaṃ gṛhītvāraṇipāṇir āha \\ edam aganma \\ iti śālāyām //
meaning: समारोह्याग्नी शालास्तम्भं पूर्वार्ध्यं गृहीत्वारणिपाणिर् आह \\ एदम् अगन्म \\ इति शालायाम् //
text_mt: Having caused the fires to ascend into himself, taking hold of the eastern post of the hall, with fire-churning sticks in hand, he says in the hall: 'We have come hither;'
he deposits King [Soma], if he has been fetched.

sanskrit_iast: prāk krayād annam upaharanty asmai haviṣyam amām̐sam agniṃ vihṛtya //
meaning: प्राक् क्रयाद् अन्नम् उपहरन्त्य् अस्मै हविष्यम् अमाम्̐सम् अग्निं विहृत्य //
text_mt: Before the purchase [of soma], having distributed the fire, they serve him food fit for an oblation, free from meat;
at seven paces, and [at the distance of] half a fathom in a sacrifice with the piling of the fire altar.

sanskrit_iast: kratvartham apadiśyāny asmā uttare parivṛta udakumbhavaty apsudīkṣā //
meaning: क्रत्वर्थम् अपदिश्यान्य् अस्मा उत्तरे परिवृत उदकुम्भवत्य् अप्सुदीक्षा //
text_mt: Having assigned [food] for another for the sake of the sacrifice, in the northern enclosure with a water-pot, the consecration in water [takes place].

sanskrit_iast: nāpita upatiṣṭhati nakhāni nikṛntaty aṅguṣṭhyaprabhṛtīni dakṣiṇahastasya prathamam //
meaning: नापित उपतिष्ठति नखानि निकृन्तत्य् अङ्गुष्ठ्यप्रभृतीनि दक्षिणहस्तस्य प्रथमम् //
text_mt: The barber attends [him]; he pares the nails, beginning with the thumb, of the right hand first.

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇaṃ godānaṃ vitāryonatti \\ imā āpas \\ iti //
meaning: दक्षिणं गोदानं वितार्योनत्ति \\ इमा आपस् \\ इति //
text_mt: Having parted the right lock of hair on the side of the head, he moistens it with the mantra: 'These waters...'.
And laying [it] down with the razor and cutting [it], he throws it into a vessel of water.
He hands the razor to the barber.
With it, he shaves his hair and beard.

sanskrit_iast: āpo asmān iti snātvā \\ ud id ābhyas \\ ity utkrāmaty uttarapūrvārdham //
meaning: आपो अस्मान् इति स्नात्वा \\ उद् इद् आभ्यस् \\ इत्य् उत्क्रामत्य् उत्तरपूर्वार्धम् //
text_mt: Having bathed with the mantra: 'May the waters [purify] us...', he steps out towards the north-eastern quarter with the mantra: 'Up indeed from them...'.

sanskrit_iast: niṣpeṣṭavai brūyād ahataṃ ced adbhir abhyukṣya //
meaning: निष्पेष्टवै ब्रूयाद् अहतं चेद् अद्भिर् अभ्युक्ष्य //
text_mt: If it is unwashed, he should tell [someone] to beat it out, having sprinkled it with water.
Or [it may be] a garment suitable for bathing, washed with cow's urine.
Its threads combed and its fringes stretched out, with the mantra: 'Of consecration and ascetic toil...'.
In the same way, the Pratiprasthātṛ [attends to] the wife in the western enclosure, silently,
He should not eat the flesh of a milch cow or an ox.
Or it is a universal human rule, because [eating them] is impossible [to sustain].
Having entered, [an offering of a cake] on eleven potsherds to Agni and Viṣṇu [is made].
He performs [the sacrifice] up to before the samiṣṭayajus offering.
Or excluding the samiṣṭayajus.
They act in a low voice before the Agni-Soma animal sacrifice.
Or [he recites] the Dīkṣaṇīyā offering with the end of his voice; the others [the Upasads] more and more softly.

sanskrit_iast: śālāṃ pūrveṇa tiṣṭhann abhyaṅkte kuśeṣu navanītena śīrṣṇo 'dhyanulomam̐ sapādakas \\ mahīnāṃ payo 'si \\ iti //
meaning: शालां पूर्वेण तिष्ठन्न् अभ्यङ्क्ते कुशेषु नवनीतेन शीर्ष्णो ऽध्यनुलोमम्̐ सपादकस् \\ महीनां पयो ऽसि \\ इति //
text_mt: Standing to the east of the hall on kuśa grasses, down to the feet, he anoints himself with butter from the head downward along the hair, with the mantra: 'You are the milk of the great ones...'.

sanskrit_iast: vṛtrasya \\ ity akṣyāv anakti traikakudāñjanenābhāve 'nyad dvir dakṣiṇaṃ trir uttaraṃ parāk sakṛtsakṛnmantraḥ śareṣīkayā sāgrayā //
meaning: वृत्रस्य \\ इत्य् अक्ष्याव् अनक्ति त्रैककुदाञ्जनेनाभावे ऽन्यद् द्विर् दक्षिणं त्रिर् उत्तरं पराक् सकृत्सकृन्मन्त्रः शरेषीकया साग्रया //
text_mt: With the mantra: 'Of Vṛtra...', he anoints both eyes with salve from Mount Trikakud; in its absence, another; twice the right, three times the left, outward, once each with the mantra, using a reed stalk having its tip.

sanskrit_iast: kuśapavitrais \\ citpatir mā \\ iti pāvayati saptabhiḥsaptabhiḥ pratimantram achidreṇa \\ iti sarvatra dvir uparinābhyunmṛjya pradakṣiṇam̐ sakṛd avāṅ //
meaning: कुशपवित्रैस् \\ चित्पतिर् मा \\ इति पावयति सप्तभिःसप्तभिः प्रतिमन्त्रम् अछिद्रेण \\ इति सर्वत्र द्विर् उपरिनाभ्युन्मृज्य प्रदक्षिणम्̐ सकृद् अवाङ् //
text_mt: With kuśa purifiers, he purifies [him] with the mantra: 'May the lord of thought [purify] me...', each time with seven, per mantra; with the mantra: 'with the flawless...', everywhere wiping upward twice above the navel, clock-wise, and once downward.
He makes him recite: 'To you, O gods...'.

sanskrit_iast: svāhā yajñam ity aṅgulī acate nānā hastayoḥ //
meaning: स्वाहा यज्ञम् इत्य् अङ्गुली अचते नाना हस्तयोः //
text_mt: With the mantra: 'Svāhā to the sacrifice!', he bends his fingers, severally on the two hands.
In the same manner, the remainder, mantra by mantra.

sanskrit_iast: uttamena muṣṭī kṛtvā svāhā \\ ity uktvā vāgyataḥ //
meaning: उत्तमेन मुष्टी कृत्वा स्वाहा \\ इत्य् उक्त्वा वाग्यतः //
text_mt: Having made fists with the last [formula], and having said: 'Svāhā!', he restrains his speech.
He leaves free the thumbs and [the fingers] adjoining them.
between the Āhavanīya and the Gārhapatya.
That is his movement-path until the Soma pressing.
In the same way, the Pratiprasthātṛ [attends to] the wife, anointing and so on, silently.
Or he leads her to enter behind [the Gārhapatya].

sanskrit_iast: audgrabhaṇāni juhoti sthālyāḥ sruveṇa \\ ākūtyai \\ iti pratimantram //
meaning: औद्ग्रभणानि जुहोति स्थाल्याः स्रुवेण \\ आकूत्यै \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: He offers the audgrabhaṇa oblations from the pot with the dipping spoon, with the mantras: 'To intention...', mantra by mantra.

sanskrit_iast: pañcamaṃ juhvāṃ dhrauvam āsicya dviś ca sthālyāḥ sruveṇa tṛtīyam̐ sruvam abhipūrayati viśvo devasya \\ iti //
meaning: पञ्चमं जुह्वां ध्रौवम् आसिच्य द्विश् च स्थाल्याः स्रुवेण तृतीयम्̐ स्रुवम् अभिपूरयति विश्वो देवस्य \\ इति //
text_mt: Having poured the fifth from the dhruvā ladle into the Juhū ladle, and twice with the dipping spoon from the pot, he fills the dipping spoon a third time, with the mantra: 'Every [mortal] of the divine...'.
Or he may offer this [Juhū ladle] full.

sanskrit_iast: āhavanīyaṃ dakṣiṇena kṛṣṇājine mām̐sasahite syūtānte tardmasu paścādāsañjanavatī nidadhāti //
meaning: आहवनीयं दक्षिणेन कृष्णाजिने माम्̐ससहिते स्यूतान्ते तर्द्मसु पश्चादासञ्जनवती निदधाति //
text_mt: South of the Āhavanīya, he spreads out two black-antelope skins having their fleshy parts together, sewn at the edges, having ties at the holes behind.
If [there is only] one, the rear part is folded double.
Having bent his right knee, he sits behind the two.
He touches the junction of the white and black [hairs] with the mantra: 'Of the Ṛg and the Sāman...'.
He steps onto it with his right knee with the mantra: 'You are shelter...'.

sanskrit_iast: mekhalāṃ badhnīte veṇiṃ trivṛtam̐ śaṇamuñjamiśrām antarāṃ vāsasas \\ ūrg asi \\ iti //
meaning: मेखलां बध्नीते वेणिं त्रिवृतम्̐ शणमुञ्जमिश्राम् अन्तरां वाससस् \\ ऊर्ग् असि \\ इति //
text_mt: He binds the girdle—a three-strand braid of hemp mixed with muñja grass—underneath the garment, with the mantra: 'You are strength...'.
He makes a tuck with the mantra: 'The tuck of Soma...'.
He covers his head with the mantra: 'The shelter of Viṣṇu...'.

sanskrit_iast: kṛṣṇaviṣāṇāṃ trivaliṃ pañcavaliṃ vottānāṃ daśāyāṃ badhnīte //
meaning: कृष्णविषाणां त्रिवलिं पञ्चवलिं वोत्तानां दशायां बध्नीते //
text_mt: He binds a black buck's horn having three or five curves, turned upwards, to the fringe [of his garment].

sanskrit_iast: upaspṛśaty enayā dakṣiṇasya bhruva upari \\ indrasya yonir iti //
meaning: उपस्पृशत्य् एनया दक्षिणस्य भ्रुव उपरि \\ इन्द्रस्य योनिर् इति //
text_mt: With it, he touches above his right eyebrow with the mantra: 'The womb of Indra...'.
And he scratches the ground with the mantra: 'Of good crops...'.
He hands him a staff of udumbara wood measuring up to his mouth.
With [the mantra]: 'Raise yourself upright' (ŚB 3.2.1.33), he raises it upright.
He places it to the south [of himself].
Or here [take place] the clenching of the fists and the restraint of speech.

sanskrit_iast: evaṃ pratiprasthātā ptanīṃ tūṣṇīṃ yugapan mekhalādi //
meaning: एवं प्रतिप्रस्थाता प्तनीं तूष्णीं युगपन् मेखलादि //
text_mt: In the same way, the Pratiprasthātṛ [invests] the wife silently, simultaneously, [with the rites] beginning with the girdle;
or a net [wound] three times around her head;
[and gives her] a broad-tipped peg of sacrificial wood for scratching.
If [it begins] from the furrowing, he performs [the rites] beginning with the girdle;
if [it begins] from the black antelope skin, [he performs them] ending with the staff.

sanskrit_iast: anyo dīkṣitas \\ ayaṃ brāhmaṇas \\ ity āha trir uccaiḥ //
meaning: अन्यो दीक्षितस् \\ अयं ब्राह्मणस् \\ इत्य् आह त्रिर् उच्चैः //
text_mt: Another [priest] says aloud three times: 'The consecrated one is this Brāhmaṇa!'

sanskrit_iast: brāhmaṇas \\ ity eva vaiśyarājanyayor api śruteḥ //
meaning: ब्राह्मणस् \\ इत्य् एव वैश्यराजन्ययोर् अपि श्रुतेः //
text_mt: [He says] 'Brāhmaṇa' indeed even for a Vaiśya and a Rājanya, because of the Vedic text.
He restrains his speech until sunset.

sanskrit_iast: astamite dīkṣita vācaṃ visṛjasva \ patni vācaṃ visṛjasva \\ iti trir āha //
meaning: अस्तमिते दीक्षित वाचं विसृजस्व \ पत्नि वाचं विसृजस्व \\ इति त्रिर् आह //
text_mt: When [the sun] has set, [the priest] says three times: 'Consecrated one, release speech! Wife, release speech!'

sanskrit_iast: agnim abhyāvṛtya vrataṃ kṛṇuta \\ iti vāgvisarjanaṃ trir uktvā \\ agnir brahmā \\ iti ca sakṛt //
meaning: अग्निम् अभ्यावृत्य व्रतं कृणुत \\ इति वाग्विसर्जनं त्रिर् उक्त्वा \\ अग्निर् ब्रह्मा \\ इति च सकृत् //
text_mt: Turning towards the fire, having uttered three times the release of speech with: 'Prepare the fast-food!' (ŚB 3.2.2.22), and once with: 'Agni is the Brahman';

sanskrit_iast: ata ūrdhvam ā muṣṭivisargād anastamite 'nudite ca trir āha dīkṣita vācaṃ yacha \ patni vācaṃ yacha \\ iti //
meaning: अत ऊर्ध्वम् आ मुष्टिविसर्गाद् अनस्तमिते ऽनुदिते च त्रिर् आह दीक्षित वाचं यछ \ पत्नि वाचं यछ \\ इति //
text_mt: Henceforth, until the unclenching of the fists, before sunset and before sunrise, [the priest] says three times: 'Consecrated one, restrain speech! Wife, restrain speech!'
The two have milk for their fast-food.
At the first fast-food [preparation], he tosses in either rice or barley.
And some [prescribe] all herbs and all fragrant substances.
The cooking of the consecrated one's [food] is on the Gārhapatya fire;
He offers the fast-food without letting it spill over.
In the latter part of the night [he takes] the evening milking;
With: 'The divine thought...' [he performs] sipping [of water] for the fast-food in his own seat.
With: 'Whichever deities...' he consumes the fast-food from an earthen vessel.
With: 'The invigorating [waters] have been drunk...', he touches his navel.

sanskrit_iast: mekṣyan kṛṣṇaviṣāṇayā loṣṭaṃ kiṃcid vādatte \\ iyaṃ te \\ iti //
meaning: मेक्ष्यन् कृष्णविषाणया लोष्टं किंचिद् वादत्ते \\ इयं ते \\ इति //
text_mt: When about to urinate, he takes up a clod of earth or something with the black antelope horn, with: 'This is thy...'
With: 'Be united with the earth', he puts down what was taken up.

sanskrit_iast: agne tvam ity uktvā svapity adhaḥ prāṅ dakṣiṇataḥ //
meaning: अग्ने त्वम् इत्य् उक्त्वा स्वपित्य् अधः प्राङ् दक्षिणतः //
text_mt: Having said: 'O Agni, thou...', he sleeps on the ground, facing east, to the south [of the fire].

sanskrit_iast: agnim abhyāvṛttaṃ vibuddham asvapsyantam \\ punar manas \\ iti vācayati //
meaning: अग्निम् अभ्यावृत्तं विबुद्धम् अस्वप्स्यन्तम् \\ पुनर् मनस् \\ इति वाचयति //
text_mt: When he has turned towards the fire, has awakened, and is not going to sleep again, [the priest] makes him recite: 'May mind [return] to me...'
If he becomes angry, he says: 'Thou, O Agni...'
Touching whatever has been obtained [as a gift], he makes him recite: 'Give so much...'
He should avoid the entrance of a Śūdra, conversation [with a Śūdra], rising to greet [anyone], paying homage, entering into water, and [being rained on by] rain, until the final bath (avabhṛtha).
speech containing [words ending in] '-vicakṣaṇa' and '-canasita'.
Remaining in the hall and not sleeping [are observed] at the two twilight hours;
There is no expiation in case of a transgression [among participants in a sacrificial session];
or they may seek mutual permission from one another.
He portions out a caru offering to Aditi.

sanskrit_iast: ājyabhāgāv iṣṭvājyena devatāś catasro yajati pathyām̐ svastim agnim̐ somam̐ savitāraṃ ca //
meaning: आज्यभागाव् इष्ट्वाज्येन देवताश् चतस्रो यजति पथ्याम्̐ स्वस्तिम् अग्निम्̐ सोमम्̐ सवितारं च //
text_mt: Having offered the two butter portions, he performs yajati-offerings with clarified butter to four deities: Pathyā Svasti, Agni, Soma, and Savitṛ.
He keeps the caru pot, the stirring stick, and the sacrificial grass for the Udayanīyā offering.
The caru pot with the remnants sticking to it, [and] the stirring stick wiped clean;
[If the previous rite] is declared to terminate [with a certain item], the earlier [possibility applies], because the general rule of obtaining it lacks specific distinction.
Or rather, the latter [possibility applies], on account of the preservation of the archetype rite and the prohibition of the after-offerings (anuyājas).
The prohibition of the after-offerings is a restatement of what is already regular.

sanskrit_iast: uparavadeśe pratiprasthātā rohite carmaṇy ānaduhe somaṃ nivapati //
meaning: उपरवदेशे प्रतिप्रस्थाता रोहिते चर्मण्य् आनदुहे सोमं निवपति //
text_mt: In the place of the Uparavas, the Pratiprasthātṛ pours out the soma onto a red bull's hide.
and a water-jar is placed in front.

sanskrit_iast: śālādvārāṇy apidhāya dhrauvaṃ juhvāṃ catur vigṛhṇāti //
meaning: शालाद्वाराण्य् अपिधाय ध्रौवं जुह्वां चतुर् विगृह्णाति //
text_mt: Having closed the doors of the hall, he divides four portions [of clarified butter] from the Dhruvā ladle into the Juhū ladle.

sanskrit_iast: barhistṛṇena hiraṇyaṃ baddhvāvadadhāti \\ eṣā te \\ iti //
meaning: बर्हिस्तृणेन हिरण्यं बद्ध्वावदधाति \\ एषा ते \\ इति //
text_mt: Having tied a piece of gold with a blade of sacrificial grass, he puts it into [the butter] with the mantra: 'This is thy [seat]...'

sanskrit_iast: śuram asi \\ iti hiraṇyam uddhṛtya vedyāṃ tṛṇaṃ nidadhāti //
meaning: शुरम् असि \\ इति हिरण्यम् उद्धृत्य वेद्यां तृणं निदधाति //
text_mt: Having taken out the gold with the mantra: 'Thou art bold...', he places the blade of grass on the altar.
He ties the piece of gold with a string.

sanskrit_iast: caturgṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā \\ anvārabhasva yajamāna \\ ity āha //
meaning: चतुर्गृहीतं गृहीत्वा \\ अन्वारभस्व यजमान \\ इत्य् आह //
text_mt: Having taken four portions [of clarified butter], he says: 'Sacrificer, take hold [of me] from behind!'
The two go out through the open door.

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇena dvāram̐ somakrayaṇī tiṣṭhaty alakṣitāvyaṅgāpravītārajjubaddhā babhruḥ piṅgalā piṅgalābhāve 'ruṇāruṇābhāve rohiṇy aśyetākṣī //
meaning: दक्षिणेन द्वारम्̐ सोमक्रयणी तिष्ठत्य् अलक्षिताव्यङ्गाप्रवीतारज्जुबद्धा बभ्रुः पिङ्गला पिङ्गलाभावे ऽरुणारुणाभावे रोहिण्य् अश्येताक्षी //
text_mt: South of the door stands the soma-cow, unmarked, unmaimed, unblemished by breeding, untied by a rope, brown, reddish-brown; in the absence of a reddish-brown one, red; in the absence of a red one, dark-red with white eyes.
He addresses her with the mantra: 'Thou art thought...'

sanskrit_iast: udīcīṃ nīyamānām anugachatas \\ vasvy asi \\ iti //
meaning: उदीचीं नीयमानाम् अनुगछतस् \\ वस्व्य् असि \\ इति //
text_mt: As she is being led toward the north, the two follow her with the mantra: 'Thou art excellent...'
Having passed six footprints, they sit down around the seventh.

sanskrit_iast: hiraṇyam asmin nidhāyābhijuhoti \\ adityās tvā \\ iti //
meaning: हिरण्यम् अस्मिन् निधायाभिजुहोति \\ अदित्यास् त्वा \\ इति //
text_mt: Having placed the piece of gold upon it, he pours an oblation over it with the mantra: 'On Aditi's [head]...'

sanskrit_iast: sphyena padaṃ triḥ parilikhati \\ asme ramasva \\ iti //
meaning: स्फ्येन पदं त्रिः परिलिखति \\ अस्मे रमस्व \\ इति //
text_mt: With the wooden sword he traces around the footprint three times with the mantra: 'Delight in us...'

sanskrit_iast: samuddhṛtya padam̐ sthālyām āvapati \\ asme te bandhur iti //
meaning: समुद्धृत्य पदम्̐ स्थाल्याम् आवपति \\ अस्मे ते बन्धुर् इति //
text_mt: Having taken up [the earth of] the footprint, he pours it into an earthen pot with the mantra: 'With us is thy kin...'

sanskrit_iast: apa sthāne niṣicya yajamānāya padaṃ prayachati tve rāyas \\ iti //
meaning: अप स्थाने निषिच्य यजमानाय पदं प्रयछति त्वे रायस् \\ इति //
text_mt: Having poured water into the place [of the footprint], he hands the footprint to the sacrificer with the mantra: 'In thee be riches!'
With the mantra: 'In me be riches!', the sacrificer receives it.

sanskrit_iast: mā vayam ity adhvaryur ātmānam̐ sam̐spṛśati //
meaning: मा वयम् इत्य् अध्वर्युर् आत्मानम्̐ सम्̐स्पृशति //
text_mt: The Adhvaryu touches himself with the mantra: 'May we not [be destitute]...'
Having carried it, he hands the footprint to the wife [of the sacrificer].
The Neṣṭṛ makes her recite the mantra: 'May the father [protect thee]...'
And while she is being looked at by the soma-cow, [she recites]: 'I have beheld [thee]...'
Having washed his hands, he ties the piece of gold onto his ring finger.
And [he ties it likewise] at the swellings, the pressings, and the Am̐śu and Adābhya cups.

sanskrit_iast: preṣyati ca somopanahanam āhara \ somaparyāṇahanam āhara \\ uṣṇīṣam āhara \\ iti //
meaning: प्रेष्यति च सोमोपनहनम् आहर \ सोमपर्याणहनम् आहर \\ उष्णीषम् आहर \\ इति //
text_mt: And he calls out: 'Bring the soma-wrapper! Bring the somaparyāṇahana-cloth! Bring the turban!'
The soma-wrapper must be a fine one.
In the absence of a turban, he cuts off [a strip] of two or three finger-breadths from the somaparyāṇahana-cloth for a turban.
The Adhvaryu or the sacrificer carries the soma-wrapper;

sanskrit_iast: prāṅ upaviśya \\ asmāko 'si \\ iti somam ālabhate //
meaning: प्राङ् उपविश्य \\ अस्माको ऽसि \\ इति सोमम् आलभते //
text_mt: Sitting down facing east, he touches the soma with the mantra: 'Thou art ours...'
Some hold that the casting away of grass and wood [is done now].

sanskrit_iast: somopanahanaṃ dviguṇaṃ caturguṇaṃ vā stṛṇāti prāgdaśam udag vā //
meaning: सोमोपनहनं द्विगुणं चतुर्गुणं वा स्तृणाति प्राग्दशम् उदग् वा //
text_mt: He spreads out the soma-wrapper double or fourfold, with fringes pointing east or north.

sanskrit_iast: tasmin somaṃ mimīte daśakṛtvas \\ abhi tyam iti //
meaning: तस्मिन् सोमं मिमीते दशकृत्वस् \\ अभि त्यम् इति //
text_mt: On it he measures out the soma ten times with the mantra: 'Towards that [well-formed god]...'
and with each subsequent measure leaving out one [finger] beginning with the thumb;
Or [the measuring is done in] another [manner], because of the Vedic statement about pouring upon [the measured stalks].

sanskrit_iast: antānt saṃgṛhyoṣṇīṣeṇa badhnāti prajābhyas tvā \\ iti //
meaning: अन्तान्त् संगृह्योष्णीषेण बध्नाति प्रजाभ्यस् त्वा \\ इति //
text_mt: Gathering the ends together, he ties it with the turban with the mantra: 'For the offspring thee...'

sanskrit_iast: aṅgulyā madhye vivṛṇoti prajās tvānuprāṇantu \\ iti //
meaning: अङ्गुल्या मध्ये विवृणोति प्रजास् त्वानुप्राणन्तु \\ इति //
text_mt: He opens it in the middle with a finger with the mantra: 'May offspring breathe after thee...'
He hands it to the seller.
Five times he bargains for the soma.

sanskrit_iast: sa āha somavikrayin krayyas te somo rājā3 iti //
meaning: स आह सोमविक्रयिन् क्रय्यस् ते सोमो राजा3 इति //
text_mt: He says: 'O soma-seller, is thy King Soma for sale?'
'He is for sale,' says the soma-seller.
'Buy him!' says the soma-seller.

sanskrit_iast: bhūyo vā ataḥ somo rājārhati \\ iti somavikrayī //
meaning: भूयो वा अतः सोमो राजार्हति \\ इति सोमविक्रयी //
text_mt: "King Soma is worth much more than that," says the Soma-seller.

sanskrit_iast: bhūya evātaḥ somo rājārhati mahāṃs tv eva gor mahimā \\ ity adhvaryur gor vai pratidhuk tasyai śṛtaṃ tasyai śaras tasyai dadhi tasyai mastu tasyā ātañcanaṃ tasyai navanītaṃ tasyai ghṛtaṃ tasyā āmikṣā tasyai vājinam iti //
meaning: भूय एवातः सोमो राजार्हति महांस् त्व् एव गोर् महिमा \\ इत्य् अध्वर्युर् गोर् वै प्रतिधुक् तस्यै शृतं तस्यै शरस् तस्यै दधि तस्यै मस्तु तस्या आतञ्चनं तस्यै नवनीतं तस्यै घृतं तस्या आमिक्षा तस्यै वाजिनम् इति //
text_mt: "King Soma is indeed worth much more than that, but great indeed is the greatness of the cow," [says] the Adhvaryu: "From the cow indeed comes fresh milk, from her boiled milk, from her cream, from her curds, from her whey, from her curd-starter, from her fresh butter, from her clarified butter, from her curd mixture, from her curd water!"

sanskrit_iast: bhūya eva \\ ity ataḥprabhṛti catur āvartayati //
meaning: भूय एव \\ इत्य् अतःप्रभृति चतुर् आवर्तयति //
text_mt: From "[King Soma is] indeed worth much more" onwards, he repeats [this dialogue] four times.
At the end [of each], he bargains with each [fraction in succession]: with a hoof [an eighth], with a quarter, with a half, with a cow.

sanskrit_iast: krītaḥ somo rājā \\ ity ante vayām̐si prabrūhi \\ ity āha somavikrayī //
meaning: क्रीतः सोमो राजा \\ इत्य् अन्ते वयाम्̐सि प्रब्रूहि \\ इत्य् आह सोमविक्रयी //
text_mt: At the end [the Adhvaryu says], "King Soma has been bought"; "Declare the items!" says the Soma-seller.

sanskrit_iast: sa āha candraṃ te vastraṃ te chāgā te dhenus te mithunau te gāvau tisras te 'nyās \\ iti //
meaning: स आह चन्द्रं ते वस्त्रं ते छागा ते धेनुस् ते मिथुनौ ते गावौ तिस्रस् ते ऽन्यास् \\ इति //
text_mt: He says: "Gold for you, a cloth for you, a she-goat for you, a milch-cow for you, a pair of cattle for you, three other [cows] for you."

sanskrit_iast: śukraṃ tvā \\ iti hiraṇyam ālambhya vācayati //
meaning: शुक्रं त्वा \\ इति हिरण्यम् आलम्भ्य वाचयति //
text_mt: Touching the gold, he has [the sacrificer] recite: "Thee, bright..."
With "Unto the friendly...", he shakes the gold towards the Soma-seller.
With "Unto us for thee...", he places it down together with the sacrificer.
The Soma-seller takes this [gold].

sanskrit_iast: ajāṃ pratyaṅmukhīm ālambhya vācayati tapasas tanūr iti //
meaning: अजां प्रत्यङ्मुखीम् आलम्भ्य वाचयति तपसस् तनूर् इति //
text_mt: Touching the she-goat facing west, he has [the sacrificer] recite: "The body of austerity..."

sanskrit_iast: savyenājāṃ prayachan mitro nas \\ iti dakṣiṇena somam //
meaning: सव्येनाजां प्रयछन् मित्रो नस् \\ इति दक्षिणेन सोमम् //
text_mt: Giving the she-goat with his left hand, [he takes] the Soma with his right hand with: "Friend to us..."
Having taken it, he either comes up or stands up.

sanskrit_iast: dīkṣitorau dakṣiṇe pratyuhya vāso nidadhāti \\ indrasyorum iti //
meaning: दीक्षितोरौ दक्षिणे प्रत्युह्य वासो निदधाति \\ इन्द्रस्योरुम् इति //
text_mt: Tucking up the garment on the consecrated sacrificer's right thigh, he places [the Soma] down with: "The thigh of Indra..."

sanskrit_iast: svāna bhrāja \\ iti japati somavikrayiṇam īkṣamāṇaḥ //
meaning: स्वान भ्राज \\ इति जपति सोमविक्रयिणम् ईक्षमाणः //
text_mt: Looking at the Soma-seller, he mutters: "O Svāna, O Bhrāja..."
The consecrated sacrificer uncovers his head.
Or, having snatched away the gold by force, he strikes [the Soma-seller] with a spotted strap piece.
He has [the sacrificer], who has taken the Soma, recite: "Around me, O Agni..."

sanskrit_iast: śīrṣṇi somaṃ kṛtvā pāṇim antardhāya prati panthām ity ano 'bhyeti dakṣiṇatas tiṣṭhacchannam̐ samaṅgi dhautam //
meaning: शीर्ष्णि सोमं कृत्वा पाणिम् अन्तर्धाय प्रति पन्थाम् इत्य् अनो ऽभ्येति दक्षिणतस् तिष्ठच्छन्नम्̐ समङ्गि धौतम् //
text_mt: Placing the Soma on his head and holding his hand under it, he approaches the cart on the south, which is standing covered, well-jointed, and washed, with: "Along the path..."
And the two front sideboards are raised from the pole.

sanskrit_iast: kṛṣṇājinam asminn āstṛṇāti \\ adityās tvag iti //
meaning: कृष्णाजिनम् अस्मिन्न् आस्तृणाति \\ अदित्यास् त्वग् इति //
text_mt: In it he spreads a black antelope skin with: "The skin of Aditi..."

sanskrit_iast: tasmint somaṃ nidadhāti \\ adtyai sadas \\ iti //
meaning: तस्मिन्त् सोमं निदधाति \\ अद्त्यै सदस् \\ इति //
text_mt: On it he places the Soma with: "The seat of Aditi..."

sanskrit_iast: astabhnād dyām iti somam ālambhya vācayati //
meaning: अस्तभ्नाद् द्याम् इति सोमम् आलम्भ्य वाचयति //
text_mt: Touching the Soma, he has [the sacrificer] recite: "He propped the sky..."

sanskrit_iast: vaneṣu vy antarikṣam iti somaparyāṇahanena paritatya kṛṣṇājinaṃ purastād āsajati sūryasya cakṣur ity āsanayor anyatarat //
meaning: वनेषु व्य् अन्तरिक्षम् इति सोमपर्याणहनेन परितत्य कृष्णाजिनं पुरस्ताद् आसजति सूर्यस्य चक्षुर् इत्य् आसनयोर् अन्यतरत् //
text_mt: Wrapping it around with the Soma-wrapper with "Across the atmosphere in the trees...", he attaches a black antelope skin in front, or either of the two seats, with: "The eye of the sun..."
If it is one [skin], having cut off the neck-portion.
He yokes the two draft-oxen with: "Come, ye two bright ones..."
Simultaneously, because of its dual phrasing.
In case of separate [yoking], repetition of the mantra [occurs], because of its direct application to the act.
Standing on the ground between the shafts, the Subrahmaṇya drives [them] forward with a palāśa branch.
Having gone around behind and taken hold of the tail-board, he calls for the recitation for the bought Soma;
And the consecrated sacrificer takes hold from behind.

sanskrit_iast: triruktāyāṃ prāṅ yātvā dakṣiṇāvartya śālāṃ gachanti //
meaning: त्रिरुक्तायां प्राङ् यात्वा दक्षिणावर्त्य शालां गछन्ति //
text_mt: When [the verse] has been recited three times, having driven eastwards and turned to the right, they go to the hall.

sanskrit_iast: subrahmaṇyāṃ cāhvayati subrahmaṇyo3m̐ subrahmaṇyo3m iti trir uktvā sakṛn nigadaṃ yāvad ahe sutyā bhavati tathāha //
meaning: सुब्रह्मण्यां चाह्वयति सुब्रह्मण्यो3म्̐ सुब्रह्मण्यो3म् इति त्रिर् उक्त्वा सकृन् निगदं यावद् अहे सुत्या भवति तथाह //
text_mt: And he calls out the Subrahmaṇyā formula: having said "O Subrahmaṇya! O Subrahmaṇya!" three times, he pronounces the nigada once according to the day on which the pressing takes place.

sanskrit_iast: śālāṃ pūrveṇa pratiprasthātāgnīṣomīyaṃ paśum ādāya tiṣṭhati kṛṣṇasāraṅgaṃ medhyam abhāve lohitasāraṅgam //
meaning: शालां पूर्वेण प्रतिप्रस्थाताग्नीषोमीयं पशुम् आदाय तिष्ठति कृष्णसारङ्गं मेध्यम् अभावे लोहितसारङ्गम् //
text_mt: To the east of the hall, the Pratiprasthātṛ stands holding the Agnīṣomīya victim, which is black-spotted and fit for sacrifice, or, in its absence, red-spotted.

sanskrit_iast: namo mitrasya \\ ity enam ālambhya vācayati //
meaning: नमो मित्रस्य \\ इत्य् एनम् आलम्भ्य वाचयति //
text_mt: Touching it, he has [the sacrificer] recite: "Homage to Mitra's..."
While the victim is moving, only the recitation [takes place].
According to some, having fetched a firebrand from the Āhavanīya fire.
Having brought the cart to a halt near [the hall], he props it up with a prop with: "The support of Varuṇa..."
And he pulls out the two yoke-pins with: "The releasers of Varuṇa's yoke-pin..."

sanskrit_iast: audumbarīm āsandīṃ nābhidaghnām aratnimātrāṅgīmūtām āharanti catvāraḥ //
meaning: औदुम्बरीम् आसन्दीं नाभिदघ्नाम् अरत्निमात्राङ्गीमूताम् आहरन्ति चत्वारः //
text_mt: Four men bring an udumbara chair, navel-high, its limbs measuring a cubit, and woven.

sanskrit_iast: abhimṛśaty enām \\ varuṇasya ṛtasadany asi \\ iti //
meaning: अभिमृशत्य् एनाम् \\ वरुणस्य ऋतसदन्य् असि \\ इति //
text_mt: He touches it with: "Thou art Varuṇa's seat of truth..."

sanskrit_iast: kṛṣṇājinam asyām āstṛṇāti varuṇasya ṛtasadanam asi \\ iti //
meaning: कृष्णाजिनम् अस्याम् आस्तृणाति वरुणस्य ऋतसदनम् असि \\ इति //
text_mt: He spreads a black antelope skin on it with: "Thou art Varuṇa's seat of truth..."

sanskrit_iast: tasmint somaṃ nidadhāti varuṇasya ṛtasadanam āsīda \\ iti //
meaning: तस्मिन्त् सोमं निदधाति वरुणस्य ऋतसदनम् आसीद \\ इति //
text_mt: On it he places the Soma with: "Sit upon Varuṇa's seat of truth..."
They bring [the chair with Soma] into the hall by the passage of the consecrated sacrificer.
They place it south of the Āhavanīya fire.
Some pour out a vessel of water near it.
Touched from behind by the wife, he quickly portions out [the rice] for a nine-pot-sherd [cake] dedicated to Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast: nirvapet \\ agnes tanūr iti pañcakṛtvaḥ pratimantram //
meaning: निर्वपेत् \\ अग्नेस् तनूर् इति पञ्चकृत्वः प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: He portions it out with "Agni's body..." five times, each time with a mantra.
The Sāvitra [offerings] are omitted on account of Vedic text and conflict.

The adding of fuel to the sacred fires, undertaking the vow, eating wild forest foods, giving gifts, and choosing the Brahman priest [are not repeated] from the Dīkṣaṇīyā offering onwards until before the Udavasānīyā offering, because they have already been performed for the Soma sacrifice.
And the girding of the wife [is omitted], since she is already wearing the girdle.
And the sacrificer’s portion [is omitted], because consumption is prohibited.
He places the Upasarjanī waters on the fire, and the Madantī waters, just as in the rite of the vow.
The purpose of water up to the opening of the fists is [served] by that [Madantī water].
The enclosing sticks are made of kārṣmarya wood.
This very set of four is used also in the Agnīṣomīya and the Upasad rites.
Having placed [the oblations], he performs the churning of the fire until the oblation [is offered].
At the time of offering the vow, he takes [clarified butter] from the Dhruvā ladle with [the mantra], "To the lord of fall..."

sanskrit_iast: dviś ca sthālyāḥ sruveṇa tanūnaptre śākvarāya \\ iti śakvana ojiṣṭhāya \\ iti //
meaning: द्विश् च स्थाल्याः स्रुवेण तनूनप्त्रे शाक्वराय \\ इति शक्वन ओजिष्ठाय \\ इति //
text_mt: And twice from the pot with the dipping spoon with [the mantras], "To Tanūnapāt the mighty..." and "To the powerful, the strongest..."
[The word] 'I take' [is supplied] everywhere, because of syntactic expectancy.

sanskrit_iast: pratipuruṣaṃ ca grahaṇam ājyāni gṛhṇānā iti śruteḥ //
meaning: प्रतिपुरुषं च ग्रहणम् आज्यानि गृह्णाना इति श्रुतेः //
text_mt: And there is a taking for each person, on account of the Vedic text: 'taking the portions of clarified butter.'

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇasyāṃ vediśroṇau nidhāyāvamṛśanty ṛtvijo yajamānaś ca \\ anādhṛṣṭam iti //
meaning: दक्षिणस्यां वेदिश्रोणौ निधायावमृशन्त्य् ऋत्विजो यजमानश् च \\ अनाधृष्टम् इति //
text_mt: Having deposited it on the southern hip of the altar, the officiating priests and the sacrificer touch it with [the mantra], "Unassailable..."

sanskrit_iast: adrohas tebhyo na satānūnaptriṇe drogdhavyam iti śruteḥ //
meaning: अद्रोहस् तेभ्यो न सतानूनप्त्रिणे द्रोग्धव्यम् इति श्रुतेः //
text_mt: There is no betrayal among them, on account of the Vedic text: 'One should not betray a fellow participant in the Tānūnaptra.'
Having moved it around, he deposits it, covering it with a non-earthen vessel.
In the afternoon, he gives it mixed with the vow-food to the consecrated [sacrificer].

sanskrit_iast: agne vratapās \\ ity āhavanīye samidham ādhāya madantīr upaspṛśya gāḍhataraṃ muṣṭimekhalaṃ kurute //
meaning: अग्ने व्रतपास् \\ इत्य् आहवनीये समिधम् आधाय मदन्तीर् उपस्पृश्य गाढतरं मुष्टिमेखलं कुरुते //
text_mt: Having placed a fuel-stick on the Āhavanīya fire with [the mantra], "O Agni, guardian of vows...", and having touched the Madantī waters, he makes the fists and the girdle firmer.
And the wife [does so] at the Gārhapatya fire silently.

sanskrit_iast: madantīr upaspṛśya yajamānaṣaṣṭhāḥ somam āpyāyayanti \\ am̐śuram̐śur iti //
meaning: मदन्तीर् उपस्पृश्य यजमानषष्ठाः सोमम् आप्याययन्ति \\ अम्̐शुरम्̐शुर् इति //
text_mt: Having touched the Madantī waters, they, six with the sacrificer as the sixth, make the Soma swell with [the mantra], "Shoot by shoot..."
Desiring to touch the Soma, he should touch water after having touched clarified butter.

sanskrit_iast: pratyetya prastare nihnuvata uttānahastā dakṣiṇottānā vā \\ eṣṭā rāyas \\ iti //
meaning: प्रत्येत्य प्रस्तरे निह्नुवत उत्तानहस्ता दक्षिणोत्ताना वा \\ एष्टा रायस् \\ इति //
text_mt: Having returned, they make obeisance over the prastara bundle with palms upward, or with the right [palm] upward, with [the mantra], "Sought are the riches..."
Some [do so] after having performed the shifting [of grass] and the anointing of the enclosing sticks.

sanskrit_iast: samullupya prastaram aktvā paridhīṃś cādāyāha \\ agnīn madanty āpā3 iti //
meaning: समुल्लुप्य प्रस्तरम् अक्त्वा परिधींश् चादायाह \\ अग्नीन् मदन्त्य् आपा3 इति //
text_mt: Having pulled out [a blade], anointed the prastara bundle, and taken the enclosing sticks, he says: "O Agnīdh, are the waters boiling?"

sanskrit_iast: tābhir ehi \\ iti bruvann adhyadhy āhavanīyam̐ hṛtvābhyukṣyāgnīdhe prayachati nidhānāya //
meaning: ताभिर् एहि \\ इति ब्रुवन्न् अध्यध्य् आहवनीयम्̐ हृत्वाभ्युक्ष्याग्नीधे प्रयछति निधानाय //
text_mt: Saying "Come with them", carrying [the vessel] over the Āhavanīya fire and sprinkling it, he hands it to the Agnīdh to set down.

sanskrit_iast: subrahmaṇyāṃ ca preṣyati subrahmaṇye subrahmaṇyām āhvaya \\ iti //
meaning: सुब्रह्मण्यां च प्रेष्यति सुब्रह्मण्ये सुब्रह्मण्याम् आह्वय \\ इति //
text_mt: And he prompts for the Subrahmaṇyā litany: "O Subrahmaṇya, call the Subrahmaṇyā!"
From this point are the Pravargya and the Upasad rites.
Or the Upasad alone when there is no Pravargya.
After calling the maker of the oblation (haviṣkṛt), there is no beating [of grains] when there is no grinding, because [beating] is for the purpose of crushing.
Or it should take place, because it is merely a ritual duty.

Having performed the spreading around [of grass], setting down of vessels, sprinkling, pouring out of clarified butter, and placing [it] on the fire, he performs the rites beginning with the wooden sword.
He takes away the cut-off root of the sacrificial grass.
Or he prompts: "[Bring] the Madantī waters!"
He cleans the ladles, with the dipping spoon as the third.
Eight ladlefuls in the Juhū ladle, four in the Upabhṛt ladle.
The clarified butter pot serves the purpose of the Dhruvā ladle.

sanskrit_iast: sruvāghāram āghārya saṃmṛṣṭe \\ āśrāvya sīda hotar ity eva brūyāt //
meaning: स्रुवाघारम् आघार्य संमृष्टे \\ आश्राव्य सीद होतर् इत्य् एव ब्रूयात् //
text_mt: Having offered the foundation oblation with the dipping spoon, when [the ladles] are cleansed, having called for the śrauta call, he should simply say: "Sit down, Hotṛ priest."
Having been impelled, stepping across, he causes [the Hotṛ] to recite the puronuvākyā for Agni.
Having deposited the two ladles, [the rites] from the swelling of Soma up to the prompt for the Subrahmaṇyā [are performed].

sanskrit_iast: aktvā prastaram upasadaṃ juhoti sruveṇa yā te \\ ity ayaḥśayām anvārabdhe //
meaning: अक्त्वा प्रस्तरम् उपसदं जुहोति स्रुवेण या ते \\ इत्य् अयःशयाम् अन्वारब्धे //
text_mt: Having anointed the prastara bundle, while being touched from behind, he offers the Upasad oblation with the dipping spoon with [the mantra], "That iron-dwelling body of yours..."

sanskrit_iast: evam itare anvaham̐ rajaḥśayām̐ hariśayāṃ ca //
meaning: एवम् इतरे अन्वहम्̐ रजःशयाम्̐ हरिशयां च //
text_mt: Likewise the others on each day: the silver-dwelling (rajaḥśayā) and the gold-dwelling (hariśayā).
He has [the cow] milked from three teats on the first [day].
Or in reverse order, if there is no piling of the fire altar.
Thus in the case of increase [of days], he should divide equally.

sanskrit_iast: aupavasathyāt pūrve 'hani paurvāhṇikyā pracarya vediṃ mimīte //
meaning: औपवसथ्यात् पूर्वे ऽहनि पौर्वाह्णिक्या प्रचर्य वेदिं मिमीते //
text_mt: On the day before the fast day, having performed the morning rite, he measures out the sacrificial ground.

sanskrit_iast: pūrvārdhyāt stambhāt purastāt triṣu prakrameṣu śaṅkuṃ nihanti so 'ntaḥpātyaḥ //
meaning: पूर्वार्ध्यात् स्तम्भात् पुरस्तात् त्रिषु प्रक्रमेषु शङ्कुं निहन्ति सो ऽन्तःपात्यः //
text_mt: East of the eastern post, at [a distance of] three strides, he drives in a peg; that is the antaḥpātya.
East of that, at thirty-six [strides, he fixes a peg].
And the southern and northern [corners of the rear], at fifteen [strides each from the central line].
And [the two eastern corners] from the eastern [peg], at twelve [strides] each.
Having stretched the cord along the spine line, he performs the rites beginning with the wooden sword, up to covering with khadira wood.
From the place of the sound-holes, he takes the earth-and-grass [with the wooden sword].
One and a half paces west of the northern shoulder [is] the Cātvāla pit.
In the morning, having combined the two Upasad rites,
[and] having performed the morning rite, he gives half the fast-milk.

sanskrit_iast: ubhābhyāṃ carite pravargyam utsādayati yathoktaṃ kuryāc cet //
meaning: उभाभ्यां चरिते प्रवर्ग्यम् उत्सादयति यथोक्तं कुर्याच् चेत् //
text_mt: When both [Upasad rites] are performed, he removes the Pravargya rite, if he should perform it according to the rule.

sanskrit_iast: opanivapanāt kṛtvā havirdhāne sthāpayati pṛṣṭhyām ubhayato dvyaratnyantare prakṣālite prācī ubhayataḥ śālām āvartya //
meaning: ओपनिवपनात् कृत्वा हविर्धाने स्थापयति पृष्ठ्याम् उभयतो द्व्यरत्न्यन्तरे प्रक्षालिते प्राची उभयतः शालाम् आवर्त्य //
text_mt: Having performed [the rites] up to the scattering [of earth on the mound], he places the two Havirdhāna carts on both sides of the spine line at an interval of two cubits, washed, facing east, having turned the shed on both sides.
Over both he places a thatched roof.
In front, on the forehead-piece, he attaches a reed mat.
A thatch enclosing with two side-posts.
He offers four ladlings into the Śālādvārya fire with: "They yoke…"

sanskrit_iast: aparaṃ dakṣiṇe vartmani dakṣiṇasyānaso hiraṇyaṃ nidhāyābhijuhoti \\ idaṃ viṣṇur iti //
meaning: अपरं दक्षिणे वर्त्मनि दक्षिणस्यानसो हिरण्यं निधायाभिजुहोति \\ इदं विष्णुर् इति //
text_mt: Having placed a piece of gold in the southern wheel-track of the southern cart, he pours another offering over it with: "Through this Viṣṇu…"

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇayā dvārānītā patnī pāṇibhyām̐ śeṣaṃ pratigṛhyākṣadhurāv anakti parāg devaśrutau \\ iti //
meaning: दक्षिणया द्वारानीता पत्नी पाणिभ्याम्̐ शेषं प्रतिगृह्याक्षधुराव् अनक्ति पराग् देवश्रुतौ \\ इति //
text_mt: The wife, brought through the southern door, having taken the remainder with both hands, anoints the axle-pins turning away with: "Ye who hear the gods…"
Simultaneously, because the mantra mentions [both] in the dual.
In case of separation, there is repetition of the mantra, because it is an auxiliary act.

sanskrit_iast: sruksthālyau pratigṛhya pratiprasthātottarasya \\ irāvatī iti pūrvavat //
meaning: स्रुक्स्थाल्यौ प्रतिगृह्य प्रतिप्रस्थातोत्तरस्य \\ इरावती इति पूर्ववत् //
text_mt: The Pratiprasthātṛ, having taken the ladle and the pot, [anoints the axle-pins] of the northern [cart] with: "Full of food…", as before.
And the wife, having gone around west of the fires, anoints [the axle-pins] of the northern [cart] as before.
He causes [the Hotṛ] to recite while the two Havirdhāna carts are being rolled forward.
When [the verse] has been recited three times, the rolling stops, as if lifted up.
He makes [the sacrificer] recite: "Go forward, eastward…"
And when it creaks: "… to your own stall!"

sanskrit_iast: paścād uttaravedes triṣu prakrameṣu matyā vā nabhyasthe abhimantrayate \\ atra ramethām iti //
meaning: पश्चाद् उत्तरवेदेस् त्रिषु प्रक्रमेषु मत्या वा नभ्यस्थे अभिमन्त्रयते \\ अत्र रमेथाम् इति //
text_mt: Three strides west of the high altar, or at discretion, when they stand on their hubs, he addresses them with: "Rest here…"

sanskrit_iast: uttareṇa parikramya dakṣiṇam upastabhnāti viṣṇor nu kam iti //
meaning: उत्तरेण परिक्रम्य दक्षिणम् उपस्तभ्नाति विष्णोर् नु कम् इति //
text_mt: Having walked around by the north, he props up the southern [cart] with: "Now indeed of Viṣṇu…"

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇata sthūṇām upanihanti viṣṇave tvā \\ iti //
meaning: दक्षिणत स्थूणाम् उपनिहन्ति विष्णवे त्वा \\ इति //
text_mt: He drives in a prop post on the south with: "For Viṣṇu, thee!"
The Pratiprasthātṛ [props] the northern [cart] with: "Or of heaven…"
A prop post on the north as before.

sanskrit_iast: yad u ca mānuṣe \\ iti śruteḥ //
meaning: यद् उ च मानुषे \\ इति श्रुतेः //
text_mt: Because of the Vedic text: "And what in the human manner…"

sanskrit_iast: pra tad viṣṇur iti vācayati madhyamaṃ chadir ālambhya //
meaning: प्र तद् विष्णुर् इति वाचयति मध्यमं छदिर् आलम्भ्य //
text_mt: Touching the middle roof-thatch, he makes [the sacrificer] recite: "Forth that Viṣṇu…"
With: "The forehead of Viṣṇu", [he touches] the forehead-piece.
With: "Ye are the mouth-corners of Viṣṇu", the two side-posts.
The roof-thatches have their ends pointing north, because of the subsequent scriptural statement.

sanskrit_iast: dvāryāḥ pariṣīvyati laspūjanipratihṛtayā rajjvā viṣṇoḥ syūr asi \\ iti //
meaning: द्वार्याः परिषीव्यति लस्पूजनिप्रतिहृतया रज्ज्वा विष्णोः स्यूर् असि \\ इति //
text_mt: He sews round the door-frame with a cord passed through by means of a needle with: "Thou art the sewing of Viṣṇu."

meaning: विष्णोर् ध्रुवो ऽसि \\ इति ग्रन्थिं करोति //
text_mt: With: "Thou art the knot of Viṣṇu", he ties a knot.

sanskrit_iast: prāgvam̐śam̐ havirdhānaṃ niṣṭhāpya vaiṣṇavam asi \\ ity ālabhate //
meaning: प्राग्वम्̐शम्̐ हविर्धानं निष्ठाप्य वैष्णवम् असि \\ इत्य् आलभते //
text_mt: Having completed the Havirdhāna shed with its ridge-pole pointing east, he touches it with: "Thou art belonging to Viṣṇu."
And they should not take meals or consume food in this [shed].

sanskrit_iast: advāreṇa sadohavirdhāne prekṣamāṇaṃ brūyāt \\ mā prekṣathās \\ iti //
meaning: अद्वारेण सदोहविर्धाने प्रेक्षमाणं ब्रूयात् \\ मा प्रेक्षथास् \\ इति //
text_mt: To one looking at the Sadas and Havirdhāna sheds through other than the entrance, he should say: "Do not look!"
The two doorposts are on both sides of the spinal cord (pṛṣṭhyā).
Beneath the fore-part of the southern cart, he digs the resounding holes (uparavas).
He performs [the actions] starting from [taking] the spade up to the drawing of the outlines, as in the case of a pit.
Four [holes], diagonally, as in the sprinkling (vyāghāraṇa).
Or the north-western one first.
The north-eastern one, however, is the last.
A span in size, with [an interval of a span] between them.
With 'Thou art great,' he digs according to the outline.

sanskrit_iast: idam aham ity utkirati yathākhātaṃ pratimantram //
meaning: इदम् अहम् इत्य् उत्किरति यथाखातं प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: With 'Here I cast out,' he casts out [the earth] as it is dug, according to each mantra.
With 'I cast out the charm,' to the west from all [the holes].
With 'Self-ruler,' he causes [the hole] to be touched, as dug, according to each mantra.
The Adhvaryu and the sacrificer touch each other's hands [underground].
The Adhvaryu in the south-eastern [hole], the sacrificer in the north-western.

sanskrit_iast: adhvaryuḥ pṛchati yajamāna kim atra \\ iti //
meaning: अध्वर्युः पृछति यजमान किम् अत्र \\ इति //
text_mt: The Adhvaryu asks: 'O sacrificer, what is here?'

sanskrit_iast: tan nau saha \\ ity adhvaryur upām̐śu //
meaning: तन् नौ सह \\ इत्य् अध्वर्युर् उपाम्̐शु //
text_mt: 'May that be for us together,' the Adhvaryu [says] in a whisper.
Then again, the Adhvaryu in the south-western [hole], the sacrificer in the north-eastern.

sanskrit_iast: yajamānaḥ pṛchati \\ adhvaryo kim atra \\ iti //
meaning: यजमानः पृछति \\ अध्वर्यो किम् अत्र \\ इति //
text_mt: The sacrificer asks: 'O Adhvaryu, what is here?'

sanskrit_iast: bhadram iti prokte tan me \\ iti yajamānaḥ //
meaning: भद्रम् इति प्रोक्ते तन् मे \\ इति यजमानः //
text_mt: When 'Auspiciousness' is spoken, the sacrificer [says]: 'May that be mine.'
He sprinkles them with 'Slayers of Rakṣases.'
In case of separation, there is repetition of the mantra, because it is an act directly affecting the object.
And the pouring in of water and the strewing [of grass are done] as for a pit, with 'Slayers of Rakṣases…', 'Slayers of Rakṣases…'

sanskrit_iast: tanūn upari kuśān kṛtvādhiṣavaṇe phalake dvyaṅgulāntare prakṣālite prācī aratnimātre saṃtṛṇṇe vopadadhāti paryūhati ca rakṣohaṇau \ rakṣohaṇau \\ iti //
meaning: तनून् उपरि कुशान् कृत्वाधिषवणे फलके द्व्यङ्गुलान्तरे प्रक्षालिते प्राची अरत्निमात्रे संतृण्णे वोपदधाति पर्यूहति च रक्षोहणौ \ रक्षोहणौ \\ इति //
text_mt: Having placed slender kuśa grasses on top, he sets down the two pressing-boards (adhiṣavaṇa-phalaka), two fingers apart, washed clean, pointed eastward, a cubit long, or perforated, and covers them around with 'Slayers of Rakṣases,' 'Slayers of Rakṣases.'

sanskrit_iast: tayoś carmādhiṣavaṇaṃ parikṛttam̐ sarvarohitaṃ nidadhāti vaiṣṇavam asi \\ iti //
meaning: तयोश् चर्माधिषवणं परिकृत्तम्̐ सर्वरोहितं निदधाति वैष्णवम् असि \\ इति //
text_mt: On them he places the pressing-hide (adhiṣavaṇa-carman), cut around and entirely red, with 'Thou art Viṣṇu's.'

sanskrit_iast: tasmin grāvṇaḥ pañca vaiṣṇavā stha \\ iti //
meaning: तस्मिन् ग्राव्णः पञ्च वैष्णवा स्थ \\ इति //
text_mt: On it, the five pressing stones with 'Ye are Viṣṇu's.'

sanskrit_iast: kharaṃ purastāt karoty uddhatāvokṣite sikatopakīrṇaṃ caturaśram //
meaning: खरं पुरस्तात् करोत्य् उद्धतावोक्षिते सिकतोपकीर्णं चतुरश्रम् //
text_mt: He makes the mound (khara) in front, on ground raised and sprinkled, strewn with sand, [and] quadrangular.

sanskrit_iast: antaḥpātyāt ṣaṭ prakramān prāṅ yātvā dakṣiṇā saptamaṃ mahāntam //
meaning: अन्तःपात्यात् षट् प्रक्रमान् प्राङ् यात्वा दक्षिणा सप्तमं महान्तम् //
text_mt: Having gone six steps eastward from the antaḥpātya peg, a seventh large [step] to the south:
There he erects the Audumbarī pillar, as tall as the sacrificer.
He performs [the rites] beginning with [taking] the spade up to the strewing [of grass].

sanskrit_iast: paryūhaṇādy opasecanāt kṛtvā dhruvāsi \\ iti vācayaty audumbarīm ālambhya //
meaning: पर्यूहणाद्य् ओपसेचनात् कृत्वा ध्रुवासि \\ इति वाचयत्य् औदुम्बरीम् आलम्भ्य //
text_mt: Having performed [the acts] from banking up earth up to moistening with water, he makes [the sacrificer] recite while holding the Audumbarī pillar: 'Thou art firm.'

sanskrit_iast: prajayā bhūyāt \\ iti paśubhir iti vā //
meaning: प्रजया भूयात् \\ इति पशुभिर् इति वा //
text_mt: 'May I abound in offspring,' or 'in cattle.'

sanskrit_iast: sruveṇa viśākhe juhoti ghṛtena dyāvāpṛthivī iti //
meaning: स्रुवेण विशाखे जुहोति घृतेन द्यावापृथिवी इति //
text_mt: With the dipping spoon (sruva) he offers into the fork [of the pillar] with 'Heaven and Earth with ghee…'
When [the stream of ghee] reaches the ground, he pronounces 'svāhā.'
Everywhere [in rites] having mantras, because of the instruction [to perform] an offering (juhoti).
And because there is no prohibition handed down in scripture.

sanskrit_iast: sadasaḥ prānteṣūccatvaṃ bhavati na nābhimātraniyamaḥ śākhāntarāt / udagvam̐śam //
meaning: सदसः प्रान्तेषूच्चत्वं भवति न नाभिमात्रनियमः शाखान्तरात् / उदग्वम्̐शम् //
text_mt: At the outer edges of the Sadas there is height; there is no restriction to navel-height alone, according to another school. Its beam runs northwards.

sanskrit_iast: vaṃśo madhyavalaḥ so 'trodagāyato bhavati tenodagāyatam / aṣṭādaśāratni //
meaning: वंशो मध्यवलः सो ऽत्रोदगायतो भवति तेनोदगायतम् / अष्टादशारत्नि //
text_mt: The beam is the central ridge-pole; that here runs northwards, thus [the Sadas] is elongated toward the north. It is eighteen cubits [in length].

sanskrit_iast: tiryakpramāṇasya vakṣyamāṇatvāt idaṃ dairghyapramāṇam ucyate / ekavim̐śatiś caturvim̐śatir vā //
meaning: तिर्यक्प्रमाणस्य वक्ष्यमाणत्वात् इदं दैर्घ्यप्रमाणम् उच्यते / एकविम्̐शतिश् चतुर्विम्̐शतिर् वा //
text_mt: Because the transverse measurement will be stated, this measure of length is stated: or twenty-one, or twenty-four,
cubits, according to another school. Nine [cubits] across.

sanskrit_iast: triṣv api pakṣeṣu navāratnayas tiryakpramāṇaṃ bhavati / ardhāyāmo vā //
meaning: त्रिष्व् अपि पक्षेषु नवारत्नयस् तिर्यक्प्रमाणं भवति / अर्धायामो वा //
text_mt: In all three options, the transverse measure is nine cubits. Or half its length.

sanskrit_iast: indrasya chadir iti madhyamaṃ chadir āropyāparapūrve ca //
meaning: इन्द्रस्य छदिर् इति मध्यमं छदिर् आरोप्यापरपूर्वे च //
text_mt: Having mounted the middle roof-mat with 'Indra's roof,' [he mounts] the western and eastern ones.

sanskrit_iast: pari tvā \\ iti parivārya pariṣīvaṇagranthyabhimarśanāny aindraiḥ //
meaning: परि त्वा \\ इति परिवार्य परिषीवणग्रन्थ्यभिमर्शनान्य् ऐन्द्रैः //
text_mt: Having enclosed it with 'Around thee…', the enclosing, stitching, knotting, and touching [are done] with [mantras] dedicated to Indra.

sanskrit_iast: havirdhānāparāntam uttareṇāgnīdhram agnyagāradvāram antarvedyardhaṃ bhūyaḥ sarvaṃ vā //
meaning: हविर्धानापरान्तम् उत्तरेणाग्नीध्रम् अग्न्यगारद्वारम् अन्तर्वेद्यर्धं भूयः सर्वं वा //
text_mt: To the north of the western end of the Havirdhāna shed, having the door of the fire-hall [facing it], half within the altar, more, or entirely, is the Āgnīdhra shed.
Having finished it, he touches it with 'Thou art of the Viśvedevas.'

sanskrit_iast:
dhiṣṇyān nivapaty uddhatāvokṣite purīṣaṃ nivapati sphenānvārabdha udaṅṅ upaviśya vibhūr asi \\ iti pratimantram //
āgnīdhrīyaṃ pūrvam //
meaning:
धिष्ण्यान् निवपत्य् उद्धतावोक्षिते पुरीषं निवपति स्फेनान्वारब्ध उदङ्ङ् उपविश्य विभूर् असि \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
आग्नीध्रीयं पूर्वम् //
text_mt: He heaps up the dhiṣṇya hearths: on ground raised and sprinkled, he heaps up loose earth; having touched [it] with the wooden sword, seated facing north, with 'Thou art all-pervading,' according to each mantra. The Āgnīdhrīya hearth is first.
And sand on top, with [the mantra] addressed to Rudra—thus everywhere.
Facing west, west of the door, is the Hotṛ's [dhiṣṇya].
To the south-east of the Audumbarī [post is the hearth] of the Maitrāvaruṇa.
To the north of the Hotṛ's hearth [he prepares] four [hearths] equidistant from each other, for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, Potṛ, Neṣṭṛ, and Acchāvāka.

sanskrit_iast: āgnīdhrād dakṣiṇam̐ samprati vedyante dakṣiṇāmukho mārjālīyam //
meaning: आग्नीध्राद् दक्षिणम्̐ सम्प्रति वेद्यन्ते दक्षिणामुखो मार्जालीयम् //
text_mt: Directly south from the Āgnīdhra [hearth], at the edge of the altar, facing south, [he prepares] the Mārjālīya [hearth].

sanskrit_iast: sadodvāraṃ pūrveṇa tiṣṭhann anudiśaty āhavanīyabahiṣpavamānadeśacātvālaśāmitraudumbaribrahmāsanaśālādvāryaprājahitānt samrāḍ asi \\ iti pratimantram //
meaning: सदोद्वारं पूर्वेण तिष्ठन्न् अनुदिशत्य् आहवनीयबहिष्पवमानदेशचात्वालशामित्रौदुम्बरिब्रह्मासनशालाद्वार्यप्राजहितान्त् सम्राड् असि \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: Standing to the east of the door of the Sadas, he addresses each [sacred area] with its respective mantra beginning with 'Thou art sovereign': the Āhavanīya, the place of the Bahiṣpavamāna, the Cātvāla pit, the Śāmitra [shed], the Audumbarī [post], the Brahman's seat, the Śālādvārya [fire], and the Prājahita [fire].
