And he throws in roasted grains with: "The roasted grains of the two bay steeds..."

sanskrit_iast: unnetānuvācayati mūrdhani kṛtvā dhānāsomebhyo 'nubrūhi \\ ity āśrāvyāha dhānāsomān prasthitān preṣya \\ iti //
meaning: उन्नेतानुवाचयति मूर्धनि कृत्वा धानासोमेभ्यो ऽनुब्रूहि \\ इत्य् आश्राव्याह धानासोमान् प्रस्थितान् प्रेष्य \\ इति //
text_mt: Having placed [the vessel] on his head, the Unnetṛ causes [the Hotṛ] to recite: "Recite for the soma with roasted grains"; and having called for the response, he says: "Prompt for the soma with roasted grains set out!"

sanskrit_iast: uttaravedau vā nidhāya vilābham \\ yas te aśvasanir iti prāṇabhakṣaṃ bhakṣayitvottaravedau nivapanti //
meaning: उत्तरवेदौ वा निधाय विलाभम् \\ यस् ते अश्वसनिर् इति प्राणभक्षं भक्षयित्वोत्तरवेदौ निवपन्ति //
text_mt: Or having placed it on the high altar, distributing it; having consumed it by inhalation with: "You who bestow horses...", they scatter it on the high altar.
The placing of the splinters with the respective mantra: "Of the god-made [sin]..."

sanskrit_iast: apareṇa cātvālaṃ yathāsvaṃ camasān pūrṇapātrān avamṛśanti haritakuśān avadhāya saṃ varcasā \\ iti //
meaning: अपरेण चात्वालं यथास्वं चमसान् पूर्णपात्रान् अवमृशन्ति हरितकुशान् अवधाय सं वर्चसा \\ इति //
text_mt: West of the Cātvāla pit, having inserted fresh kuśa grass, they touch their respective full cups with: "Together with lustre..."
The consumption of curds in the Āgnīdhra shed is with: "Of Dadhikrāvan..."
The Patnīsaṃyājas are like those of the animal sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast: sam indra ṇas \\ iti nava samiṣṭayajūm̐ṣi juhoti pratimantram //
meaning: सम् इन्द्र णस् \\ इति नव समिष्टयजूम्̐षि जुहोति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: He offers the nine samiṣṭayajus oblations, each with its respective mantra, beginning with: "Together, O Indra, with us..."
They carry the seat, the Udumbara staff, and whatever is smeared with soma to the Cātvāla pit.

sanskrit_iast: kṛṣṇaviṣāṇāmekhale cātvāle prāsyati māhir bhūr iti //
meaning: कृष्णविषाणामेखले चात्वाले प्रास्यति माहिर् भूर् इति //
text_mt: He throws the black antelope horn and the girdle into the Cātvāla pit with: "Do not become a snake!"
And the Pratiprasthātṛ [throws] the peg and the yoke-halter silently.

sanskrit_iast: sāma preṣyati gāya \ brūhi \\ iti vā //
meaning: साम प्रेष्यति गाय \ ब्रूहि \\ इति वा //
text_mt: He commands the sāman: "Sing!" or "Chant!"
All join in the finale.
Taking what was brought, they go to the purifying bath, to standing bodies of flowing waters.

meaning: नमो वरुणाय \\ इति वाचयत्य् अपो ऽवक्रमयन् //
text_mt: Causing [the sacrificer] to step into the water, he makes him recite: "Homage to Varuṇa!"

sanskrit_iast: prāsya samidhaṃ caturgṛhītenābhijuhoti \\ agner anīkam iti //
meaning: प्रास्य समिधं चतुर्गृहीतेनाभिजुहोति \\ अग्नेर् अनीकम् इति //
text_mt: Having thrown in a kindling stick, he offers over it with four ladlings [of clarified butter], with: "The face of Agni..."
[The oblations are made] behind, [namely] the fore-offerings excluding the barhis.
He performs the cutting [of portions] with the single-potsherd [cake].
If he wishes, he may cut a portion of the dregs of soma.
To Agni and Varuṇa the rest is offered entirely.
And once of the dregs of soma, if [taken] in the former [offering].
There are the two ghee portions and two after-offerings excluding the barhis, as spoken by the sacrificer.
he floats the jar of soma dregs with: 'In the ocean your [heart...]…'
Releasing it, he attends [the waters] with: 'O divine waters…'
He immerses it with: 'O bath (avabhṛtha)…'

sanskrit_iast: kṛṣṇājināntaṃ ca mā maindryaṃ jyaiṣṭhyam̐ śraiṣṭhyaṃ vyauṣīr iti putrāyainat pradāya varuṇapraghāsavat snānaprabhṛy ā samidādhānāt //
meaning: कृष्णाजिनान्तं च मा मैन्द्र्यं ज्यैष्ठ्यम्̐ श्रैष्ठ्यं व्यौषीर् इति पुत्रायैनत् प्रदाय वरुणप्रघासवत् स्नानप्रभृय् आ समिदाधानात् //
text_mt: And handing over to his son the border of the black-antelope skin with: 'May you not take away my Indra-like power, seniority, and pre-eminence', [the procedure takes place] as in the Varuṇapraghāsa, from the bathing up to the placing of the kindling stick.

sanskrit_iast: ud vayam ity unnetronnītā āmahīyāṃ japanto gachanti \\ apāma somam amṛtā abhūma \\ aganma jyotir avidāma devān \ kiṃ nūnam asmān kṛṇavad arātiḥ \ kim u dhūrtir amṛta martyasya \\ iti //
meaning: उद् वयम् इत्य् उन्नेत्रोन्नीता आमहीयां जपन्तो गछन्ति \\ अपाम सोमम् अमृता अभूम \\ अगन्म ज्योतिर् अविदाम देवान् \ किं नूनम् अस्मान् कृणवद् अरातिः \ किम् उ धूर्तिर् अमृत मर्त्यस्य \\ इति //
text_mt: Brought forth by the Unnetṛ priest with: 'Upwards we [have risen]…', they proceed muttering the Āmahīyā [verse]: 'We have drunk the soma, we have become immortal; / we have reached the light, we have found the gods. / What can malice do to us now? / What can the deceit of a mortal do, O immortal?'
The sacrificer sits behind the Śālādvārya fire, placing the black-antelope skin on his lap.

sanskrit_iast: sruvāhutiṃ juhoti maindryaṃ jyaiṣṭhyam̐ śraiṣṭhyam agnir dadhātu svāhā \\ iti //
meaning: स्रुवाहुतिं जुहोति मैन्द्र्यं ज्यैष्ठ्यम्̐ श्रैष्ठ्यम् अग्निर् दधातु स्वाहा \\ इति //
text_mt: He offers a ladleful offering with: 'May Agni bestow Indra-like power, seniority, and pre-eminence upon me, svāhā.'
Having laid down the black-antelope skin, the Udayanīyā rite is [performed] like the Prāyaṇīyā.
Pathyā Svasti is the fourth [deity].

sanskrit_iast: pātraprokṣaṇādy ājyāsādanāt savanīyavat parivyayaṇādi maitrāvaruṇī vaśānūbandhyā //
meaning: पात्रप्रोक्षणाद्य् आज्यासादनात् सवनीयवत् परिव्ययणादि मैत्रावरुणी वशानूबन्ध्या //
text_mt: From the sprinkling of the vessels up to the placing of the clarified butter, it is like the Savanīyā [animal sacrifice]; beginning with the encircling, the Anūbandhyā is a sterile cow for Mitra and Varuṇa.
Or [it begins] with the hiding of the Svaru-chip, because [the preceding actions] have already been performed.
Some say: having placed it, [the rite proceeds] from the clarified butter portions up to the Iḍā.
The Udavasānīyā is [a cake] on five potsherds for Agni, [offered] on the fire churned out of the mounted [fires].
[It is] a subsidiary of the soma sacrifice, because of proximity and absence of conflict.
Or it is an obligatory [daily rite], because of the scriptural rule about the morning oblation;

meaning: अत्यग्निष्टोम उक्थ्यः षोडशी वाजपेयो ऽतिरात्रो ऽप्तोर्यामः //
text_mt: the Atyagniṣṭoma, Ukthya, Ṣoḍaśin, Vājapeya, Atirātra, and Aptoryāma.

sanskrit_iast: teṣām ukthyo 'chāvākam abhi saṃtiṣṭhate hotāram itare //
meaning: तेषाम् उक्थ्यो ऽछावाकम् अभि संतिष्ठते होतारम् इतरे //
text_mt: Of these, the Ukthya concludes after the Acchāvāka priest; the others, after the Hotṛ priest.

sanskrit_iast: vaiśyarājanyayoḥ some nyagrodhastibhīn upanahyechan bhakṣāya krayaṇaprabhṛty anusomam āvṛtā samānam āsādanaṃ prāg abhiṣavāt //
meaning: वैश्यराजन्ययोः सोमे न्यग्रोधस्तिभीन् उपनह्येछन् भक्षाय क्रयणप्रभृत्य् अनुसोमम् आवृता समानम् आसादनं प्राग् अभिषवात् //
text_mt: In the soma sacrifice of a Vaiśya or Rājanya, if he desires to tie up shoots of the Nyagrodha tree for consumption, [the procedure is] identical according to the soma ritual from the buying [of soma] onwards; their placing takes place before the pressing.
Or having brought [the shoots] at the time of drawing into the cups and crushing them with curd, he draws [it] into that cup following [the rest].

sanskrit_iast: hūyamāneṣu kuśataruṇena juhoti \\ ahaṃ tvad asmi \\ iti //
meaning: हूयमानेषु कुशतरुणेन जुहोति \\ अहं त्वद् अस्मि \\ इति //
text_mt: While [the oblations] are being offered, he offers with a fresh shoot of Kuśa grass: 'I am from you.'
He remains restrained in speech while the ritual action is taking place.

meaning: हिरण्यवत्याम्̐ हुतायां दक्षिणो ऽनुगछत्य् आ क्रयात् //
text_mt: When the [oblation] accompanied by gold has been offered, he follows along on the south side up to the purchase [of soma].

sanskrit_iast: krīte prāṅ atītya pūrveṇānaḥ parītyāpareṇa vā dakṣiṇo 'nugachaty ā nidhānāt //
meaning: क्रीते प्राङ् अतीत्य पूर्वेणानः परीत्यापरेण वा दक्षिणो ऽनुगछत्य् आ निधानात् //
text_mt: When [the soma] is purchased, having gone across to the east, having walked around the cart by the east or by the west, he follows along on the south side up to the deposit.
Or behind the Dakṣiṇāgni during the Gharma offering.
When [the Adhvaryu] is about to carry the Stambayajus, he sits to the south of the Āhavanīya place together with the vedi.
Thus everywhere prior to the bringing forward of Agni and Soma.
Or following each successive rite together [with it],

meaning: आहवनीये प्रणीयमाने ऽप्रतिरथस्य द्वादश ब्रुवन्न् अग्नौ //
text_mt: while the Āhavanīya fire is being led forward, he recites the twelve [verses] of the Apratiratha hymn over the fire.
When [the vedi] is strewn, he goes as required.
For the bringing forward of Agni and Soma, having gone north of the Dhiṣṇya hearths and east of the Śālādvārya fire, he sits on the south.
And when the oblation is offered, taking the soma, he follows the fire.
Or the sacrificer may carry the soma.
Having handed it to another, while it is not yet deposited, having gone as he came, he sits to the south.
And when the oblation is offered, taking the soma and going past the Āhavanīya fire,
in the latter part of the night, if he wishes, [he acts] as during the bringing forward of Agni and Soma.

sanskrit_iast: vipruṣām̐ homam̐ hutvā pratihartāram anvārabheta vādīkṣitaḥ //
meaning: विप्रुषाम्̐ होमम्̐ हुत्वा प्रतिहर्तारम् अन्वारभेत वादीक्षितः //
text_mt: Having offered the oblation of drops, the consecrated sacrificer may take hold of the Pratihartṛ priest from behind.

sanskrit_iast: prastotrāmantritas \\ etaṃ te deva savitaḥ \ stuta savituḥ prasave \\ ity uktvā prasauti //
meaning: प्रस्तोत्रामन्त्रितस् \\ एतं ते देव सवितः \ स्तुत सवितुः प्रसवे \\ इत्य् उक्त्वा प्रसौति //
text_mt: Invited by the Prastotṛ, having uttered, "This for you, god Savitṛ; chant at the instigation of Savitṛ," he gives permission.

sanskrit_iast: deva savitar etad bṛhaspate pra \\ iti vā //
meaning: देव सवितर् एतद् बृहस्पते प्र \\ इति वा //
text_mt: Or with: "God Savitṛ, this; Bṛhaspati, chant!"
Or with: "By the ray for truth," according to each mantra.
Gliding [takes place] by that [way] through which the entrance [was made].
If [he enters] after going around the sacrificial post by the east, [he glides] by the west.
He sits to the south of the Praśāstṛ.
The others [sit] to the west of the dhiṣṇya hearths.
During the pavamāna chant, the movement after completion [is] to the north of the Praśāstṛ's dhiṣṇya hearth.
The rules of the Jyotiṣṭoma [apply] to the one-day sacrifice and to the twelve-day sacrifice, because its qualities are seen [in them].
Because of the statement [that they apply] to the Vrātyastomas and Sādyaḥkras [derived] from the first [i.e., the one-day sacrifice].
The twelve-day sacrifice is [both] a sacrificial session and a multi-day sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast: āsata upayantīti sattraliṅgaṃ yajata ity ahīnasya //
meaning: आसत उपयन्तीति सत्त्रलिङ्गं यजत इत्य् अहीनस्य //
text_mt: "They sit," "they undertake" are the distinctive marks of a sacrificial session; "he sacrifices" [is the mark] of a multi-day sacrifice.
A sacrificial session has Atirātras at both ends; of a multi-day sacrifice, [the Atirātra is] at the end.
All are sacrificers in sacrificial sessions.
And [they are] without sacrificial gifts, because of the conjunction of the masters.
The householder performs the duties of the sacrificer, because of [the others] not being enjoined.
When it is impossible, there is touching of the householder.
In rites for the sake of another, one [acts], because it is already accomplished.

sanskrit_iast: agniṃ ceṣyamāṇāḥ samārohya gṛhapatir madhye manthaty ardhaśa itare dakṣiṇottarāḥ //
meaning: अग्निं चेष्यमाणाः समारोह्य गृहपतिर् मध्ये मन्थत्य् अर्धश इतरे दक्षिणोत्तराः //
text_mt: Intending to pile the fire, having mounted [the fires], the householder churns in the middle; the others [churn] divided into halves, south and north.
The throwing of embers [takes place] into the householder's Āhavanīya fire.
There [an animal victim] sacred to Prajāpati [is offered].
The Patnīsaṃyāja offerings are made with ghee, except for the householder's [wife].
In case of inability, the fixed rite [is performed] everywhere on the fires that are mounted and churned out.
At the time of consecration, churning [is performed] in the north-beamed hall as before.
The throwing [of embers takes place] into the Gārhapatya fire here.

sanskrit_iast: upavasathaprabhṛti prāg anīṣomapraṇayanād upaśamayya cinoty enāñ chālādvaryād dakṣiṇottarān dhiṣṇyavad vā śruteḥ //
meaning: उपवसथप्रभृति प्राग् अनीषोमप्रणयनाद् उपशमय्य चिनोत्य् एनाञ् छालाद्वर्याद् दक्षिणोत्तरान् धिष्ण्यवद् वा श्रुतेः //
text_mt: Beginning from the Upavasatha day, prior to the carrying forward of the Agnīṣoma, having extinguished them, he piles them south to north from the Śālādvārya fire, or like the dhiṣṇya hearths, because of scripture.
Or, as prescribed, for the householder.

sanskrit_iast: āgnīdhrīya udyate 'ṅgāram ekaikam̐ haranti praticiti śālādvāryāt //
meaning: आग्नीध्रीय उद्यते ऽङ्गारम् एकैकम्̐ हरन्ति प्रतिचिति शालाद्वार्यात् //
text_mt: When the Āgnīdhra fire is being raised, they take embers one by one from the Śālādvārya fire to each pile.

sanskrit_iast: pratyagni savanīyapuroḍāśā bhūyo haviruchiṣṭam asatsamāptyā iti śruteḥ //
meaning: प्रत्यग्नि सवनीयपुरोडाशा भूयो हविरुछिष्टम् असत्समाप्त्या इति श्रुतेः //
text_mt: The offering-cakes for the pressing are offered on each fire, because of scripture: "Let the sacrificial oblation not be in excess until completion."
And the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings [are performed] as before.
Or, sitting around the householder, they churn.
The householder is first and foremost in every case.
As each [fire] is born, they throw it into the householder's Gārhapatya fire in both cases.
Beginning from the Upavasatha day, [it is] identical for all.

sanskrit_iast: araṇyor vāhur gṛhapater ya ito 'gnir janiṣyate sa naḥ saha \ yad anena yajñena jeṣyāmo 'nena paśubandhena tan naḥ saha \ saha naḥ sādhukṛtyā \ nānā pāpakṛtyā \ ya eva pāpaṃ karavat tasyaiva tat \\ ity uktvā gṛhapatiḥ samārohayate svau prathamam //
meaning: अरण्योर् वाहुर् गृहपतेर् य इतो ऽग्निर् जनिष्यते स नः सह \ यद् अनेन यज्ञेन जेष्यामो ऽनेन पशुबन्धेन तन् नः सह \ सह नः साधुकृत्या \ नाना पापकृत्या \ य एव पापं करवत् तस्यैव तत् \\ इत्य् उक्त्वा गृहपतिः समारोहयते स्वौ प्रथमम् //
text_mt: Or into the two churning sticks; having said: "The fire of the householder which shall be born from here, that is shared by us; whatever we shall win through this sacrifice, through this animal sacrifice, that is shared by us; shared by us is good action, separate is evil action; whoever alone does evil, his alone is that," the householder mounts his own [two sticks] first.
At the time of consecration, beginning with the dialogue, in place of the animal sacrifice [they recite]: "Through the sacrificial session..."
Or as in a one-day sacrifice, on the final day, are the Śālāgārhapatya offering-cake and the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings.

sanskrit_iast: ekapuroḍāśeṣu vratyāsambhavād aindraṃ pañcaśarāvam odanaṃ nirvapet puroḍāśaṃ vā yady odanīyanti yady apūpīyantīti śruteḥ //
meaning: एकपुरोडाशेषु व्रत्यासम्भवाद् ऐन्द्रं पञ्चशरावम् ओदनं निर्वपेत् पुरोडाशं वा यद्य् ओदनीयन्ति यद्य् अपूपीयन्तीति श्रुतेः //
text_mt: Since fasting food is not possible in the case of one offering-cake, one should pour out five platters of cooked rice sacred to Indra, or an offering-cake, because of scripture: "If they desire cooked rice, or if they desire offering-cakes."
There are twelve consecrations and twelve Upasads.

sanskrit_iast: adhvaryur gṛhapatiṃ dīkṣayati brahmādīṃś cādhvaryvādīn pratiprasthātā pratiprasthātrādīn neṣṭā neṣṭrādīn unnetonnetāraṃ brahmacārī snātako 'nyo vā brāhmaṇo na pūtaḥ pāvayed iti śruteḥ //
meaning: अध्वर्युर् गृहपतिं दीक्षयति ब्रह्मादींश् चाध्वर्य्वादीन् प्रतिप्रस्थाता प्रतिप्रस्थात्रादीन् नेष्टा नेष्ट्रादीन् उन्नेतोन्नेतारं ब्रह्मचारी स्नातको ऽन्यो वा ब्राह्मणो न पूतः पावयेद् इति श्रुतेः //
text_mt: The Adhvaryu consecrates the householder and those beginning with the Brahman; the Pratiprasthātṛ [consecrates] those beginning with the Adhvaryu; the Neṣṭṛ [consecrates] those beginning with the Pratiprasthātṛ; the Unnetṛ [consecrates] those beginning with the Neṣṭṛ; a celibate student, a Snātaka, or another Brahmin [consecrates] the Unnetṛ, because of scripture: "One who is not purified may not purify."
Each subsequent one [consecrates] the wives according to each husband.

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇākāle kṛṣṇājināni dhūnvānā dakṣiṇāpathena japanto gachanti yan me 'gadāyuṣaḥ parāg ito 'gāt tāṃ te 'gada dakṣiṇāṃ nayāmi \\ iti \\ idam aham amum āmuṣyāyaṇam amuṣya putram amuṣyāḥ putraṃ kāmāya dakṣiṇāṃ nayāmi \\ iti //
meaning: दक्षिणाकाले कृष्णाजिनानि धून्वाना दक्षिणापथेन जपन्तो गछन्ति यन् मे ऽगदायुषः पराग् इतो ऽगात् तां ते ऽगद दक्षिणां नयामि \\ इति \\ इदम् अहम् अमुम् आमुष्यायणम् अमुष्य पुत्रम् अमुष्याः पुत्रं कामाय दक्षिणां नयामि \\ इति //
text_mt: At the time of sacrificial gifts, shaking black antelope skins, going along the southern path and muttering: "What has gone away from here of my unimpaired life, that sacrificial gift I lead to you, O healthy one; here do I lead this N.N., of such lineage, son of such a father, son of such a mother, as a sacrificial gift for desire."

sanskrit_iast: pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍahaḥ prathamo 'gniṣṭomaś caturthaḥ ṣoḍaśy ukthyā itare //
meaning: पृष्ठ्यः षडहः प्रथमो ऽग्निष्टोमश् चतुर्थः षोडश्य् उक्थ्या इतरे //
text_mt: The first Pṛṣṭhya six-day period has an Agniṣṭoma [first], a Ṣoḍaśin fourth, and the others are Ukthyas.

sanskrit_iast: tatrātigrāhyagrahaṇaṃ tryahe pūrve \\ agne pavasva \\ uttiṣṭhann \ adṛśram ity anvaham ekaikam //
meaning: तत्रातिग्राह्यग्रहणं त्र्यहे पूर्वे \\ अग्ने पवस्व \\ उत्तिष्ठन्न् \ अदृश्रम् इत्य् अन्वहम् एकैकम् //
text_mt: There, the drawing of the Atigrāhya cups [occurs] in the first three days, one on each day: "Agne pavasva", "Uttiṣṭhan", "Adṛśram".

sanskrit_iast: agne varcasvin \\ indraujiṣṭha \ sūrya bhrājiṣṭha \\ iti bhakṣaṇaṃ yajamānaiḥ //
meaning: अग्ने वर्चस्विन् \\ इन्द्रौजिष्ठ \ सूर्य भ्राजिष्ठ \\ इति भक्षणं यजमानैः //
text_mt: The consuming [is done] by the sacrificers with: "O Agni, full of splendour!", "O Indra, most mighty!", "O Sūrya, most brilliant!".
At the time of the Pṛṣṭha stotras, at the first [round], the running of the chariot is to the south of the vedi.
On the second [day], the introductory rite [of the stotra] is by means of the sound of a drum.

sanskrit_iast: caturthe 'raṇibhyāṃ manthanaṃ codgātur ūrau homaś ca //
meaning: चतुर्थे ऽरणिभ्यां मन्थनं चोद्गातुर् ऊरौ होमश् च //
text_mt: On the fourth, the churning [of fire] is with two kindling-sticks, and the oblation is on the thigh of the Udgātṛ priest.
On the fifth, with a water pot containing avakā plants.

sanskrit_iast: mātṛbhir vatsānt sam̐sṛjya sadaḥ pūrveṇa vyāvartayanti //
meaning: मातृभिर् वत्सान्त् सम्̐सृज्य सदः पूर्वेण व्यावर्तयन्ति //
text_mt: Having united the calves with their mothers, they lead them away past the east of the sadas.

sanskrit_iast: svayamṛtuyājejya \\ arvāñcam adya yayyaṃ nṛvāhaṇam \\ rathaṃ yuñjāthām iha vāṃ vimocanam \ pṛṅktam̐ havīm̐ṣi madhunā hi kaṃ gatam \ athā somaṃ pibataṃ vājinīvasū iti //
meaning: स्वयमृतुयाजेज्य \\ अर्वाञ्चम् अद्य यय्यं नृवाहणम् \\ रथं युञ्जाथाम् इह वां विमोचनम् \ पृङ्क्तम्̐ हवीम्̐षि मधुना हि कं गतम् \ अथा सोमं पिबतं वाजिनीवसू इति //
text_mt: The ritual sacrifice of the season-offerings [is performed] by [the sacrificer] himself with: "Hitherward today, traveling, carrying men / yoke the chariot; here is your unyoking; / mix the offerings with sweet drink, for you have gone [there]; / then drink the soma, O you who are rich in horses!"
The response belongs to the comprehension of the Hotṛ priest.
And [it is] the archetypal one, because the others have a different purpose.

sanskrit_iast: ṣaḍahānte na bahu vaden nānyaṃ pṛchen nānyasmai prabrūyāt //
meaning: षडहान्ते न बहु वदेन् नान्यं पृछेन् नान्यस्मै प्रब्रूयात् //
text_mt: At the end of the six-day period, he should not speak much, he should not ask another, nor should he tell another.
There is eating of honey or of clarified butter.
The next three Chandoma [days] are Ukthya [rites].
The tenth, the Avivākya, is an Atyagniṣṭoma.
The days end with the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings, except for the last [day].

sanskrit_iast: ekaiko vāgyataḥ somam̐ rakṣaty ā bodhanāt //
meaning: एकैको वाग्यतः सोमम्̐ रक्षत्य् आ बोधनात् //
text_mt: Keeping silence one by one, each guards the soma until waking.
Or [it is done] starting from the carrying around of the Vasatīvarī waters.
The others are dismissed for their Vedic recitation or for firewood.
At sunset, the placing of firewood takes place on all [the fires].
On the tenth [day], in the afternoon, having touched water, there is entering into the hall.

meaning: शालाद्वार्ये ऽन्वारब्धेषु \\ इह रतिर् इति जुहोति //
text_mt: While they remain in contact [with him], he offers into the Śālādvārya fire with: "Here is delight..."

sanskrit_iast: uttareṇa parikramyāpareṇa havirdhānaṃ praviśyottarasya havirdhānasyāparakūbarīm ālambhya sattrasyarddhi gāyanti sattrasya ṛddhir iti //
meaning: उत्तरेण परिक्रम्यापरेण हविर्धानं प्रविश्योत्तरस्य हविर्धानस्यापरकूबरीम् आलम्भ्य सत्त्रस्यर्द्धि गायन्ति सत्त्रस्य ऋद्धिर् इति //
text_mt: Having circumambulated by the north and entered behind the Havirdhāna cart, seizing the rear pole of the northern Havirdhāna cart, they sing the Sattrasyarddhi [sāman] with: "The prosperity of the sacrificial session..."
Or on the northern buttock of the Uttaravedi.

sanskrit_iast: yuvaṃ tam iti dakṣiṇasyādho 'kṣaṃ prāñco niṣkrāmanti //
meaning: युवं तम् इति दक्षिणस्याधो ऽक्षं प्राञ्चो निष्क्रामन्ति //
text_mt: With: "You two, him...", they step out towards the east beneath the axle of the southern [cart].
Having entered the sadas, they sit down on their own seats towards the east.

sanskrit_iast: grahaṃ gṛhṇāti prājāpatyaṃ vāyuṃ pṛthivyā pātreṇa //
meaning: ग्रहं गृह्णाति प्राजापत्यं वायुं पृथिव्या पात्रेण //
text_mt: He draws the soma cup belonging to Prajāpati [with]: "Vāyu with the earth as vessel..."
The drawing, setting down, introducing of the chant, offering, bringing of the portion, and consuming are done mentally.
The explanation of the Caturhotṛ [mantras] belongs to the Hotṛ priest.

sanskrit_iast: pratigṛṇāti \\ arātsur ime yajamānās \\< bhadram ebhyo yajamānebhyo 'bhūt >\\ iti //
meaning: प्रतिगृणाति \\ अरात्सुर् इमे यजमानास् \\< भद्रम् एभ्यो यजमानेभ्यो ऽभूत् >\\ इति //
text_mt: He responds: "These sacrificers have prospered; auspiciousness has arisen for these sacrificers!"
It is a narration of the lack of qualities of Prajāpati.
Or, in case of non-comprehension, that dialogue [takes place].
Or [it is] that which belongs to the Aśvamedha, because of the name.
Before sunset, holding the Audumbarī pillar, they restrain their speech.

sanskrit_iast: astamite niṣkramyāpareṇottaravedim āsate pratiprasthātā vasatīvarīḥ pariharati //
meaning: अस्तमिते निष्क्रम्यापरेणोत्तरवेदिम् आसते प्रतिप्रस्थाता वसतीवरीः परिहरति //
text_mt: At sunset, having gone out, they sit behind the Uttaravedi; the Pratiprasthātā priest carries around the Vasatīvarī waters.
The release of speech is by [the mantra] "With the desire for the sacrificial session".
If they have separate desires, [it is] with: "Bhūr, bhuvaḥ..."
The Subrahmaṇyā-call belongs to the householder, or to whomever he designates.

sanskrit_iast: subrahmaṇya upa mā hvayasva \\ ity uktvā samidādhānam //
meaning: सुब्रह्मण्य उप मा ह्वयस्व \\ इत्य् उक्त्वा समिदाधानम् //
text_mt: Having said, "O Subrahmaṇya, call upon me!", there is the placing of firewood.
This departure from the sacrificial session begins with the touching of water.
The place of additional soma cups is between the Āgrayaṇa and the Ukthya [cups].

sanskrit_iast: prātaḥsavane 'tigrāhyān gṛhītvā ṣoḍaśinaṃ khādireṇa catuḥsraktinā \\ ātiṣṭha \ yukṣvā hi \\ iti vā //
meaning: प्रातःसवने ऽतिग्राह्यान् गृहीत्वा षोडशिनं खादिरेण चतुःस्रक्तिना \\ आतिष्ठ \ युक्ष्वा हि \\ इति वा //
text_mt: Having drawn the Atigrāhya cups at the morning pressing, [he draws] the Ṣoḍaśin with a four-cornered [cup] of khadira wood, or with: "Stand upon..." and "Yoke indeed..."
Or at the midday [pressing], following the Āgrayaṇa cup.
Or he draws the Atigrāhya cups at the end of the continuous-stream cup.
Or [from] the Pūtabhṛt [vat], when about to begin the introductory rite of the pṛṣṭha stotra.
Having set down the waters, the drawing of the Am̐śu and Adābhya cups is done with a four-cornered [cup] of udumbara wood.
He performs taking up the pressing stone, throwing down the soma stalks, pouring on water, striking once, drawing, and offering; and he smells the gold.
The drawing is in a sacrificial session, a thousand-[cow sacrifice], a Sarvavedasa, a Vājapeya, a Rājasūya, a Viśvajit, and a Sarvapṛṣṭha, if there is room for it.
Twelve pregnant heifers are the sacrificial gift in a non-sattra.
For one who desires to become [prosperous], he draws the Adābhya cup.

sanskrit_iast: āsicya nigrābhyāḥ pātre tasmiṃs tūṣṇīṃ trīn am̐śūn avadhāya \\ agnaye tvā gāyatrachandasam iti pratimantram //
meaning: आसिच्य निग्राभ्याः पात्रे तस्मिंस् तूष्णीं त्रीन् अम्̐शून् अवधाय \\ अग्नये त्वा गायत्रछन्दसम् इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: Having poured [the water of] the Nigrābhyā into that vessel, having placed three soma stalks silently into it, [he draws it] reciting each mantra: "For Agni thee, whose metre is the Gāyatrī..."
The Upayāma formula [is used] everywhere without distinction.
And because there is a prohibition of the separate-drawing and the Āditya cup.

sanskrit_iast: anuṣṭup te \\ ity uktvādhūnoty am̐śubhir vreśīnāṃ tvā \\ iti gachann āhavanīyam \\ tasmai te \\ iti juhoti //
meaning: अनुष्टुप् ते \\ इत्य् उक्त्वाधूनोत्य् अम्̐शुभिर् व्रेशीनां त्वा \\ इति गछन्न् आहवनीयम् \\ तस्मै ते \\ इति जुहोति //
text_mt: Having said, "Thy Anuṣṭubh...", he shakes [it] with the soma stalks; saying, "Thee of the Vreśīs...", while walking toward the Āhavanīya fire, he offers with: "To that thee..."

sanskrit_iast: am̐śūnt some nidadhāti \\ uśik tvam iti pratimantram //
meaning: अम्̐शून्त् सोमे निदधाति \\ उशिक् त्वम् इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: He deposits the soma shoots into the soma, with the respective mantras beginning: "You are the desiring one..."

sanskrit_iast: ukthyānte ṣoḍaśicaraṇam upasthāyainam \\ yasmān na jātas \\ iti camasān unnīya //
meaning: उक्थ्यान्ते षोडशिचरणम् उपस्थायैनम् \\ यस्मान् न जातस् \\ इति चमसान् उन्नीय //
text_mt: At the end of the Ukthya, the performance of the Ṣoḍaśin [takes place]: having attended upon it with "From whom none was born...", having poured out the cups,

sanskrit_iast: tṛṇahiraṇyai stotropākaraṇam upāstam ayam̐ somo 'tyareci \\ upāvartadhvam iti kṛṣṇe 'śva upatiṣṭhati //
meaning: तृणहिरण्यै स्तोत्रोपाकरणम् उपास्तम् अयम्̐ सोमो ऽत्यरेचि \\ उपावर्तध्वम् इति कृष्णे ऽश्व उपतिष्ठति //
text_mt: the bringing near of the chant is done with blades of grass and pieces of gold; with "This soma has been left over; return!", he attends upon the black horse.
The consuming [is done] with "And Indra is sovereign..."

sanskrit_iast: ā pātraprakṣālanāt kṛtvātirātraś cet saumyena sahāśvino dvikapālaḥ sarvatra //
meaning: आ पात्रप्रक्षालनात् कृत्वातिरात्रश् चेत् सौम्येन सहाश्विनो द्विकपालः सर्वत्र //
text_mt: Having performed [the rites] up to the washing of the vessels, if it is an Atirātra, the two-kapāla cake for the Aśvins along with the Saumya [cake] is everywhere [offered].
There are three rounds with the cups, each round having four chants.
The first [chant and recitation of each round] belongs to the Hotṛ priest; for the others, it is as in the Ukthya.
At its conclusion, having poured out the cups, [takes place] the bringing near of the chant of the twilight [stotra].
At the end of the recitation, he proceeds with the Āśvina [graha], which is offered entirely.
The invitation and direction for the soma [offerings] kept overnight are [made] for the two Aśvins.
A savanīya [animal] dedicated to Indra and Agni [is offered] each day;

sanskrit_iast: ahīne vyūḍhachandasi daśarātrasya caturthanavamayor ahnor āgrayaṇagrahaṇaṃ prathamam //
meaning: अहीने व्यूढछन्दसि दशरात्रस्य चतुर्थनवमयोर् अह्नोर् आग्रयणग्रहणं प्रथमम् //
text_mt: In a multi-day sacrifice with transposed meters, on the fourth and ninth days of the ten-day period, the drawing of the Āgrayaṇa cup is first;
on the sixth and seventh, that of the Śukra cup.
The setting down [of the cup is omitted] until the drawing of the preceding [cups];
at the proper time, beginning with the wiping, the setting down [is done] after uttering 'hiṅ'.

sanskrit_iast: atipreṣite 'gnīd āha śvaḥsutyām indrāgnibhyāṃ prabravīmi viśvebhyo devebhyo brāhmaṇebhyaḥ somapebhyas \\ brahman vācaṃ yacha \\ iti //
meaning: अतिप्रेषिते ऽग्नीद् आह श्वःसुत्याम् इन्द्राग्निभ्यां प्रब्रवीमि विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यो ब्राह्मणेभ्यः सोमपेभ्यस् \\ ब्रह्मन् वाचं यछ \\ इति //
text_mt: When instructed [with the word 'atirātra'], the Agnīdh priest says: "I proclaim the pressing of tomorrow to Indra and Agni, to the All-gods, and to the soma-drinking Brahmins; Brahman priest, restrain your speech!"
On the introductory day, some [say] "the pressing of today", because its time has arrived;
and from the indicative mark: "Agni today..."
The day subsequent to the introductory day [is meant by] "tomorrow", because of the absence of time [for another interpretation];
The rules of the twelve-day sacrifice apply in sacrificial sessions, because its characteristics are seen there.
For the Gavāmayana, the consecration takes place on the Ekāṣṭakā;
or four days before the full moon;

sanskrit_iast: pavamāneṣūdgātāram anvārabheran \\ śyeno 'si gāyatrachandās \\ anu tvārabhe svasti mā sampāraya \ suparṇo 'si triṣṭupchandās \\ ṛbhur asi jagacchandās \\ itītarayoḥ savanayoḥ //
meaning: पवमानेषूद्गातारम् अन्वारभेरन् \\ श्येनो ऽसि गायत्रछन्दास् \\ अनु त्वारभे स्वस्ति मा सम्पारय \ सुपर्णो ऽसि त्रिष्टुप्छन्दास् \\ ऋभुर् असि जगच्छन्दास् \\ इतीतरयोः सवनयोः //
text_mt: During the Pavamāna chants, they should hold onto the Udgātṛ priest, [with]: "You are a falcon, having the gāyatrī meter; I take hold of you: carry me across safely!"; with "You are a fair-winged bird, having the triṣṭubh meter..." and "You are an Ṛbhu, having the jagatī meter..." at the other two soma pressings.

sanskrit_iast: savanānteṣu japanti mayi bhargas \\ mayi mahas \\ mayi yaśas \\ mayi sarvam iti //
meaning: सवनान्तेषु जपन्ति मयि भर्गस् \\ मयि महस् \\ मयि यशस् \\ मयि सर्वम् इति //
text_mt: At the ends of the soma pressings, they murmur: "In me be splendor; in me be greatness; in me be glory; in me be all!"

meaning: अभिप्लवः षडहो ऽग्निष्टोमौ प्रथमान्त्या उक्थ्या इतरे //
text_mt: The Abhiplava is a six-day rite: the first and last [days] are Agniṣṭomas, the others are Ukthyas.

sanskrit_iast: atirātrāc caturvim̐śam ahar agniṣṭoma ukthyo vā //
meaning: अतिरात्राच् चतुर्विम्̐शम् अहर् अग्निष्टोम उक्थ्यो वा //
text_mt: After the Atirātra, the twenty-fourth day is an Agniṣṭoma or an Ukthya.

sanskrit_iast: catvāro 'bhiplavāḥ pṛṣṭhyaś ca māsa evaṃ catvāra uttare //
meaning: चत्वारो ऽभिप्लवाः पृष्ठ्यश् च मास एवं चत्वार उत्तरे //
text_mt: Four Abhiplavas and one Pṛṣṭhya make a month; so also the four subsequent [months].
In the sixth [month], there are three Abhiplavas and one Pṛṣṭhya;
the three Svarasāman days are Agniṣṭomas or Ukthyas;
The morning recitation is at the time of twilight;

sanskrit_iast: ud u tyam iti grahagrahaṇam atigrāhyavad bhakṣavarjam //
meaning: उद् उ त्यम् इति ग्रहग्रहणम् अतिग्राह्यवद् भक्षवर्जम् //
text_mt: The drawing of the cup [is performed] with [the mantra]: 'Up that [all-seeing Surya]...' like the Atigrāhya cups, without the consumption.
The earlier half [is performed] in reverse order.
In place of the Abhijit [there is] the Viśvajit Agniṣṭoma.
If it is Sarvapṛṣṭha, all the Atigrāhyas [are drawn].

sanskrit_iast: ṣaṣṭhe māse trayo 'bhiplavā goāyuṣī daśarātro mahāvratam agniṣṭomaḥ //
meaning: षष्ठे मासे त्रयो ऽभिप्लवा गोआयुषी दशरात्रो महाव्रतम् अग्निष्टोमः //
text_mt: In the sixth month there are three Abhiplavas, the Go and Āyus days, the ten-day period, the Mahāvrata, and the Agniṣṭoma.
An animal sacred to Prajāpati is to be seized.

sanskrit_iast: grahaṃ gṛhṇāti vi na indra \ vācaspatim \\ viśvakarman \\ iti vātigrāhyavat //
meaning: ग्रहं गृह्णाति वि न इन्द्र \ वाचस्पतिम् \\ विश्वकर्मन् \\ इति वातिग्राह्यवत् //
text_mt: He draws the cup with: 'Distribute among us, O Indra...', 'The lord of speech...', or 'O Viśvakarman...', like the Atigrāhya cups.

sanskrit_iast: upa mā yantu majjayas sanīḍās \\ upa mā jakṣur upa mā manīṣā \ priyām ahaṃ tanvaṃ paśyamānas \\ mayi ramo devānāṃ tejase brahmavarcasāya \\ iti bhakṣaṇaṃ yajamānaiḥ //
meaning: उप मा यन्तु मज्जयस् सनीडास् \\ उप मा जक्षुर् उप मा मनीषा \ प्रियाम् अहं तन्वं पश्यमानस् \\ मयि रमो देवानां तेजसे ब्रह्मवर्चसाय \\ इति भक्षणं यजमानैः //
text_mt: The consumption by the sacrificers is done with: 'May the marrows, having a common nest, come to me; may the feastings come to me, may the insight come to me; beholding my dear body, may my delight be among the gods for fiery energy, for spiritual splendor.'
The prelude to the Pṛṣṭhastotra is performed with a harp of a hundred strings.
The strings are of muñja grass; the plectrum is of cane.

meaning: बृसीषूपविशन्ति प्रेङ्खे होता फलके ऽध्वर्युः प्रतिगृणाति //
text_mt: They sit on grass cushions; the Hotṛ priest [sits] on a swing; the Adhvaryu priest responds on a wooden board.
The Udgātṛ priest [sits] on a chair whose legs are a span high, like the soma chair.
One curses, the other praises.
A courtesan and a Brahmacārin revile each other.
A Śūdra and an Ārya pull back and forth against each other on a round hide.
To the south of the Mārjālīya [hearth], in an enclosed space, a copulation takes place.
He girds a Kṣatriya to the west of the southern hip of the altar.
With: '[I cover] your vital spots...', he hands him armor.

sanskrit_iast: triḥ samantaṃ pariyanti śālām apareṇottareṇa cātvālaṃ vaśācarma kaṭe viśākhyāṃ vāstīrṇam uchritaṃ vā vidhyanty aniṣpattram //
meaning: त्रिः समन्तं परियन्ति शालाम् अपरेणोत्तरेण चात्वालं वशाचर्म कटे विशाख्यां वास्तीर्णम् उछ्रितं वा विध्यन्त्य् अनिष्पत्त्रम् //
text_mt: They go around three times completely: to the west of the hall, north of the Cātvāla pit, they pierce the skin of a barren cow, spread or hung upon a mat or a branched post, without letting the arrows pass completely through.

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇena carma yanti trir viddhvā purastād vimocanam //
meaning: दक्षिणेन चर्म यन्ति त्रिर् विद्ध्वा पुरस्ताद् विमोचनम् //
text_mt: They go south of the hide; having pierced it three times, the releasing [of the bow] takes place in the east.
They beat drums at the corners of the Sadas.

sanskrit_iast: āgnīdhram apareṇa śvabhram̐ savāladhānena carmaṇāvanahya vāladhānenāhanti //
meaning: आग्नीध्रम् अपरेण श्वभ्रम्̐ सवालधानेन चर्मणावनह्य वालधानेनाहन्ति //
text_mt: Behind the Āgnīdhra [hearth], having tied a tail-bearing skin over a pit, he beats it with the tail.

sanskrit_iast: godhāvīṇākāḥ kāṇḍavīṇāś ca patnyo vādayanty upagāyanti //
meaning: गोधावीणाकाः काण्डवीणाश् च पत्न्यो वादयन्त्य् उपगायन्ति //
text_mt: The wives play godhā-lutes and reed-lutes, and sing along.
And they make other sounds.

sanskrit_iast: udakumbhāñ chiraḥsu kṛtvā mārjālīyaṃ dāsyaḥ pariyanti vācayaty enāḥ paryāyādiṣu //
meaning: उदकुम्भाञ् छिरःसु कृत्वा मार्जालीयं दास्यः परियन्ति वाचयत्य् एनाः पर्यायादिषु //
text_mt: Having placed water jars on their heads, female servants go around the Mārjālīya; he makes them recite at the beginnings of the rounds:

sanskrit_iast: gāvo hāre surabhayas \\ idaṃ madhu \ gāvo gulgulugandhayas \\ idaṃ madhu \ gāvo ghṛtasya mātaras \\ idaṃ madhu \ tā iha santu bhūyasīr \ idaṃ madhu \ takā vayaṃ plavāmahe \\ idaṃ madhu \ śamyāḥ prataratām iva \\ idaṃ madhu \ na vai gāvo mandīrasya \ gaṅgāyā udakaṃ papuḥ \ papuḥ sarasvatīṃ nadīm \\ tāḥ prācya ujjigāhīre \\ idaṃ madhu \ nigīrya sarvā ādhīr \ idaṃ madhu \ madhv ity ākarṣaiḥ kuśair yathā \\ idaṃ madhu \\ iti //
meaning: गावो हारे सुरभयस् \\ इदं मधु \ गावो गुल्गुलुगन्धयस् \\ इदं मधु \ गावो घृतस्य मातरस् \\ इदं मधु \ ता इह सन्तु भूयसीर् \ इदं मधु \ तका वयं प्लवामहे \\ इदं मधु \ शम्याः प्रतरताम् इव \\ इदं मधु \ न वै गावो मन्दीरस्य \ गङ्गाया उदकं पपुः \ पपुः सरस्वतीं नदीम् \\ ताः प्राच्य उज्जिगाहीरे \\ इदं मधु \ निगीर्य सर्वा आधीर् \ इदं मधु \ मध्व् इत्य् आकर्षैः कुशैर् यथा \\ इदं मधु \\ इति //
text_mt: 'The cows, O dear one, are fragrant: this is honey! The cows smell of bdellium: this is honey! The cows are mothers of ghee: this is honey! May they become more numerous here: this is honey! With these we cross over: this is honey! As if by means of a boat of pegs: this is honey! Indeed the cows did not drink the water of the Mandīra, the Ganges; they drank the Sarasvatī river; flowing eastward, they plunged into it: this is honey! Having swallowed down all distress: this is honey! As with blades of kuśa grass drawing honey: this is honey!'
Counter-clockwise and clockwise until the end of the chant.
Having poured [water] out at the Mārjālīya, they place [the jars] down full.
Everything, beginning with the praise and blame, is done while [the stotra] is being chanted.
There are three Anūbandhyā cows: sacred to Mitra-Varuṇa, to the Viśvedevas, and to Bṛhaspati.
In sattras lasting less than a year, in non-Sārasvata ones, and in those where the sacrificial gift is less than a thousand.
At the end of the omentum oblation of the Anūbandhyā cow, shaving of all hair, beard, and body hair takes place on the southern hip of the altar.
The Traidhātavī is the concluding offering everywhere.

sanskrit_iast: avabhṛthād udetya jyotiṣṭomo 'gniṣṭomaḥ pṛṣṭhaśamanīyaḥ sahasradakṣiṇo vā //
meaning: अवभृथाद् उदेत्य ज्योतिष्टोमो ऽग्निष्टोमः पृष्ठशमनीयः सहस्रदक्षिणो वा //
text_mt: Rising from the concluding bath, the Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma serves as the Pṛṣṭhaśamanīya day, or one with a sacrificial gift of a thousand.
It is an auxiliary of the sattra, on account of the context,

sanskrit_iast:
kālaprādhānyāc ca //
sahasradakṣiṇe trirātre prativibhajya nayan rohiṇīm upadhvastām apravītām atirecayati //
meaning:
कालप्राधान्याच् च //
सहस्रदक्षिणे त्रिरात्रे प्रतिविभज्य नयन् रोहिणीम् उपध्वस्ताम् अप्रवीताम् अतिरेचयति //
text_mt: and because time is primary. In a three-day rite with a thousand sacrificial gifts, distributing them day by day, as he leads them, he sets aside a reddish, speckled, unbred cow.

sanskrit_iast: ādye 'han prathamāṃ nayed antye vā paścāt //
meaning: आद्ये ऽहन् प्रथमां नयेद् अन्त्ये वा पश्चात् //
text_mt: He should lead it first on the first day, or at the end on the last day.

sanskrit_iast: havirdhānāgnīdhrāntare droṇakalaśam enām āghrāpayati \\ ājighra \\ iti //
meaning: हविर्धानाग्नीध्रान्तरे द्रोणकलशम् एनाम् आघ्रापयति \\ आजिघ्र \\ इति //
text_mt: Between the Havirdhāna and the Āgnīdhra, he makes her smell the Droṇakalaśa with: 'Sniff!'

sanskrit_iast: iḍe rante \\ iti dakṣiṇe 'syāḥ karṇe yajamāno japati //
meaning: इडे रन्ते \\ इति दक्षिणे ऽस्याः कर्णे यजमानो जपति //
text_mt: The sacrificer whispers in her right ear: 'O Iḍā, O Rantā...'

sanskrit_iast: sarvato navasu daśamīṃ kṛtvā hotre dadyāt //
meaning: सर्वतो नवसु दशमीं कृत्वा होत्रे दद्यात् //
text_mt: Making her the tenth among nine on every side, he should give her to the Hotṛ priest.
Or having made [the gift] without the two Unnetṛ priests, he issues the call.
He should give the sacrificial gifts in undivided units of ten.
He should give her at the end of the omentum oblation of the Anūbandhyā cow,
In a series of days, [the priests] step out day by day [from the Sadas], beginning with the first day.
And the drawing of the Vasatīvarī waters [takes place day by day].
Some [authorities hold that this is done] having poured [them] out at midday.
The Vājapeya [is performed] in autumn by a non-Vaiśya.
During two bright fortnights on either side, he sacrifices with the Bṛhaspatisava.
Before [the Vājapeya], on the odd days [there is] the Jyotiṣṭoma; on the others [the days of] the Pṛṣṭhya [ṣaḍaha].
Afterwards [the days of] the Pṛṣṭhya [ṣaḍaha are performed] in reverse order.
Or with all-Agniṣṭoma soma sacrifices of the Rājasūya.
The surrounding sacrifices have separate consecrations, because of the difference of time.
He offers with: "O divine Savitṛ…" at the rites beginning with the offering.
Once [only] at the beginning of the consecration, because of the oneness of the rite.

And at the buying [of Soma], the commencement of the altar, the setting aside of the Pravargya, the carrying forward of the fire, the Havirdhāna, the [animal sacrifice to] Agni-Soma, the settling of the Sadas and the Āgnīdhra mound, and the drawing and carrying round of the Vasatīvarī waters, [an oblation is made] because each is a distinct action prior to the pressing day.

sanskrit_iast: somāt krīyamāṇāt sahitaṃ dakṣiṇataḥ sīsena parisrutaḥ krayaṇaṃ keśavāt //
meaning: सोमात् क्रीयमाणात् सहितं दक्षिणतः सीसेन परिस्रुतः क्रयणं केशवात् //
text_mt: While Soma is being purchased, the purchase of the Parisrut liquor from a long-haired man with lead is made together [with it], to the south.
When [Soma] is being conveyed around, [the Parisrut] is carried along after it.

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇena praveśya dakṣiṇāgnau paktvāpare 'nte neṣṭā surāṃ karoti //
meaning: दक्षिणेन प्रवेश्य दक्षिणाग्नौ पक्त्वापरे ऽन्ते नेष्टा सुरां करोति //
text_mt: Having brought [the ingredients] in by the south, having cooked [them] on the Dakṣiṇāgni fire, the Neṣṭṛ priest makes the surā at the western end [of the hall].
Having prepared a mound, [he prepares] another [mound] in place of the Nārāśaṃsa [cups].
He makes a passage on the south side.

sanskrit_iast: yūpaveṣṭanam̐ saptadaśabhir vastrair vyudgranthanaṃ vā parivyayaṇakāle //
meaning: यूपवेष्टनम्̐ सप्तदशभिर् वस्त्रैर् व्युद्ग्रन्थनं वा परिव्ययणकाले //
text_mt: The wrapping of the sacrificial post with seventeen cloths or tying knots upwards takes place at the time of girding [it].
The top-ring is made of wheat, even-ended and hollowed out.

meaning: सुत्यादौ हिर्ण्यस्रजो ऽपिनह्यन्ते ऽधिकृता यजमानः पत्नी च //
text_mt: At the beginning of the pressing day, golden garlands are tied on by the qualified [priests], the sacrificer, and his wife.

sanskrit_iast: ekadhanapraveśanakāle surāṃ neṣṭāpareṇa praveśya khare karoti //
meaning: एकधनप्रवेशनकाले सुरां नेष्टापरेण प्रवेश्य खरे करोति //
text_mt: At the time of bringing in the Ekadhana waters, the Neṣṭṛ priest, having brought in the surā from the west, places it on the mound.

sanskrit_iast: saṃdhinā pātrāṇy āhṛtya pātre vālena punāti //
meaning: संधिना पात्राण्य् आहृत्य पात्रे वालेन पुनाति //
text_mt: Having brought the vessels through the passage, he strains [the surā] into a vessel with horsehair.

meaning: प्रातःसवने ऽतिग्राह्यान् गृहीत्वा षोडशिनं पञ्च चैन्द्रान् //
text_mt: At the morning pressing, having drawn the Atigrāhya cups, [he draws] the Ṣoḍaśin and five [cups] for Indra.
With: "Dwelling firmly…" for each respective mantra.
And the Neṣṭṛ priest [draws] as many cups of surā.
The cups do not pass beyond the axle [of the southern cart].

sanskrit_iast: uparyupary akṣam adhvaryur dhārayaty adho'dho neṣṭā sampṛcau \\ iti //
meaning: उपर्युपर्य् अक्षम् अध्वर्युर् धारयत्य् अधोऽधो नेष्टा सम्पृचौ \\ इति //
text_mt: The Adhvaryu holds [his cup] just above the axle, and the Neṣṭṛ priest holds [his] just below, with: "United…"
Having drawn the honey cup with a golden [vessel], he sets it down in the middle of the mound.

sanskrit_iast: atirārtapaśūn upākṛtya vaśāṃ pṛśniṃ marudbhya ujjeṣebhyaḥ //
meaning: अतिरार्तपशून् उपाकृत्य वशां पृश्निं मरुद्भ्य उज्जेषेभ्यः //
text_mt: Having brought near the animal victims of the Atirātra, [he brings near] a speckled barren cow for the victorious Maruts.
And seventeen dark-coloured, hornless he-goats sacred to Prajāpati.
In the absence of those qualities in all of them, [they may be present] in a part [of them].
At the conclusion of the Māhendra cup, the omentum of the barren cow is offered.
And [the offering of its limbs is performed] divided into two parts by the cooked portions.
He cuts portions from the former [parts] for the deities and the Sviṣṭakṛt.
At the conclusion of the Vāmadevya cup, [the offering] of the animals sacred to Prajāpati [takes place].
Before the moving aside of the ladles, [the offering is made] with the sacrificial substance.
Along with the midday offerings, there is a caru of wild rice sacred to Bṛhaspati, consisting of seventeen platters.
The number of handfuls ceases, because of the common nature [of the measurement].
He gives seventeen hundreds each of cattle, garments, goats, and sheep.
[He gives] seventeen female servants wearing golden necklaces;
[and seventeen each] of elephants, light carts, and wagons;
and of each kind, until completing a group of seventeen.

sanskrit_iast: dravyeṣu vā saptadaśatā saptadaśa saptadaśāni dadātīti śruteḥ //
meaning: द्रव्येषु वा सप्तदशता सप्तदश सप्तदशानि ददातीति श्रुतेः //
text_mt: Or the seventeenfold nature applies to the articles, because the scripture says: "He gives seventeen seventeenfold [gifts]."
At the end of the Marutvatīya [śastra], [the Adhvaryu performs] the bringing down of the chariot with: "Indra's thunderbolt..."

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇena cātvālam āvartayati vājasya \\ iti dhūrgṛhītam //
meaning: दक्षिणेन चात्वालम् आवर्तयति वाजस्य \\ इति धूर्गृहीतम् //
text_mt: Holding it by the pole, he turns it around to the south of the Cātvāla with: "Of speed..."

sanskrit_iast: aśvān prokṣaty apo 'vanīyamānānt snātān vāgatān apsv antar iti //
meaning: अश्वान् प्रोक्षत्य् अपो ऽवनीयमानान्त् स्नातान् वागतान् अप्स्व् अन्तर् इति //
text_mt: He sprinkles the horses with water that is poured out, or when they are bathed and arrived, with: "Within the waters..."
He yokes the right horse with: "Either the wind..."
The left one with: "Swift as wind..."
The right trace-horse with: "The speed which is yours..."
An unyoked fourth [horse], restraining all, follows behind.
He causes them to smell the caru for Bṛhaspati with: "O swift runners..."

sanskrit_iast: caturyujo yunakty aparāṃs tūṣṇīṃ bahirvedi ṣoḍaśa //
meaning: चतुर्युजो युनक्त्य् अपरांस् तूष्णीं बहिर्वेदि षोडश //
text_mt: He yokes sixteen other four-horse [chariots] silently outside the vedi.

sanskrit_iast: devasyāham iti brahmā rathacakram ārohaty utkare nābhimātre sthāṇau sthitam //
meaning: देवस्याहम् इति ब्रह्मा रथचक्रम् आरोहत्य् उत्करे नाभिमात्रे स्थाणौ स्थितम् //
text_mt: With: "By the impulse of the god...", the Brahman ascends a chariot wheel placed upon a post of navel height on the rubbish heap.
The wheel-drums of a kṣatriya [sacrificer] belong to Indra.

sanskrit_iast: saptadaśa dundubhīn āsajaty anuvedi paścād āgnīdhrāt //
meaning: सप्तदश दुन्दुभीन् आसजत्य् अनुवेदि पश्चाद् आग्नीध्रात् //
text_mt: He sets seventeen war-drums along the vedi, behind the Āgnīdhra [shed].

sanskrit_iast: bṛhaspate vājam ity ekaṃ dundubhim āhanti tūṣṇīm itarān //
meaning: बृहस्पते वाजम् इत्य् एकं दुन्दुभिम् आहन्ति तूष्णीम् इतरान् //
text_mt: He beats one drum with: "O Bṛhaspati, [win] the prize!", and the others silently.
A kṣatriya shoots seventeen arrow-ranges northwards from the tīrtha.
At the end [of the distance] he sets up an udumbara branch.
With: "By the impulse of the god...", the sacrificer mounts the [chariot] yoked with mantras.

sanskrit_iast: adhvaryoś ca tūṣṇīṃ brahmacāry antevāsī vā vācanāya //
meaning: अध्वर्योश् च तूष्णीं ब्रह्मचार्य् अन्तेवासी वा वाचनाय //
text_mt: And on the Adhvaryu's [chariot, mounts] silently a Vedic student or an apprentice, for the sake of prompting [the mantras];

sanskrit_iast: itareṣām ekasmin rājanyo vaiśyo vā saurapratigrahāya //
meaning: इतरेषाम् एकस्मिन् राजन्यो वैश्यो वा सौरप्रतिग्रहाय //
text_mt: on one of the other [chariots], a noble or a vaiśya, to receive the surā [cup].
The Brahman sings the sāman three times.
With: "This one here...", he offers oblation verse by verse;
Having turned clockwise around the branch, they return.
When they have returned, the Brahman descends with: "By the impulse of the god..."
With: "This is your...", [the Adhvaryu] takes down the [drum] struck with the mantra;

sanskrit_iast: avaruhya naivāram ālabhate tīrthe sthitam ā mā vājasya \\ iti //
meaning: अवरुह्य नैवारम् आलभते तीर्थे स्थितम् आ मा वाजस्य \\ इति //
text_mt: Having stepped down, [the sacrificer] touches the nivāra-grain [caru] standing at the tīrtha with: "May I attain the prize..."
He causes the horses yoked with mantras to smell it with: "O swift runners..."
Having yoked the fourth [horse], he gives [the chariot] to the Adhvaryu.

sanskrit_iast: adhvaryuyajamānau madhugraham̐ saurapratigrahāya prayachata uttarasyāṃ vediśroṇā upaviṣṭāya //
meaning: अध्वर्युयजमानौ मधुग्रहम्̐ सौरप्रतिग्रहाय प्रयछत उत्तरस्यां वेदिश्रोणा उपविष्टाय //
text_mt: The Adhvaryu and the sacrificer hand the honey-cup to the receiver of the surā [cup] seated on the northern buttock of the vedi;

sanskrit_iast: neṣṭā ca saurān paścimena nirhṛtya śālām apareṇa hṛtvaikaṃ prayachann āha \\ anena ta imaṃ niṣkrīṇāmi \\ iti //
meaning: नेष्टा च सौरान् पश्चिमेन निर्हृत्य शालाम् अपरेण हृत्वैकं प्रयछन्न् आह \\ अनेन त इमं निष्क्रीणामि \\ इति //
text_mt: and the Neṣṭṛ, having brought out the surā cups by the west, and having carried [them] behind the hall, giving one [to him], says: "With this I buy this [cup] back from you."
He gives the honey-cup along with its vessel to the Brahman.
The latter does with it as he pleases.

sanskrit_iast: dvādaśa sruvāhutīr juhoti \\ āpaye svāhā \\ iti pratimantraṃ vācayati vā //
meaning: द्वादश स्रुवाहुतीर् जुहोति \\ आपये स्वाहा \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रं वाचयति वा //
text_mt: He offers twelve spoon-oblations with: "To Āpi, svāhā!", etc., with each mantra, or causes [the sacrificer] to recite them;

sanskrit_iast: neṣṭā patnīm āneṣyan kauśaṃ vāsaḥ paridhāpayati caṇḍātakaṃ daharam vā //
meaning: नेष्टा पत्नीम् आनेष्यन् कौशं वासः परिधापयति चण्डातकं दहरम् वा //
text_mt: The Neṣṭṛ, intending to bring the wife [of the sacrificer], makes her put on a garment of kuśa grass, an inner petticoat, or a short skirt,
inside the consecration garment.

sanskrit_iast: niśrayaṇīṃ yūpa uchrayaty uttarāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ vā //
meaning: निश्रयणीं यूप उछ्रयत्य् उत्तरां दक्षिणां वा //
text_mt: He sets up a ladder against the sacrificial post, on the north or on the south.

sanskrit_iast: ārokṣyan jāyām āmantrayate jāya ehi \ svo rohāva \\ iti //
meaning: आरोक्ष्यन् जायाम् आमन्त्रयते जाय एहि \ स्वो रोहाव \\ इति //
text_mt: Intending to ascend, [the sacrificer] addresses his wife: "Wife, come, let us two ascend to heaven!"
With: "Of Prajāpati...", the two ascend.
With: "Heaven!", he touches the wheat [top-piece].
He rises above the sacrificial post with his head, with: "Immortal..."
With: "For us be your...", he looks at the quarters.
The commoners throw up to him seventeen bags of saline earth tied in aśvattha leaves.
With: "Homage to the Mother...", he looks down at the earth.
He steps down onto a goatskin containing a gold plate;

sanskrit_iast: uttaravedim apareṇaudumbarīm āsandīṃ bastacarmaṇāstṛṇāti \\ iyaṃ te \\ iti //
meaning: उत्तरवेदिम् अपरेणौदुम्बरीम् आसन्दीं बस्तचर्मणास्तृणाति \\ इयं ते \\ इति //
text_mt: West of the high altar, he spreads a goat skin over a stool made of udumbara wood with the mantra, "This is thine..."
He makes the presser sit down upon it with the mantra, "Thou art the restrainer..."

sanskrit_iast: prāk sviṣṭakṛta audumbare pātre 'pa āsicya payaś ca saptadaśānnāny āvapati //
meaning: प्राक् स्विष्टकृत औदुम्बरे पात्रे ऽप आसिच्य पयश् च सप्तदशान्नान्य् आवपति //
text_mt: Before the sviṣṭakṛt offering, having poured water and milk into an udumbara vessel, he casts in seventeen kinds of food.
Or as many as he can remember, omitting one.
He does not eat of it until his breath [has recovered].

sanskrit_iast: sruveṇa sambhṛtāj juhoti vājasyemam iti pratimantram //
meaning: स्रुवेण सम्भृताज् जुहोति वाजस्येमम् इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: With the dipping spoon, he offers from the collected mixture with the mantra, "This of the contest...", reciting a mantra for each [oblation].
With the remainder, he consecrates the sacrificer with the mantra, "Of the divine [Savitṛ]..."
In place of "Sarasvatī Vāc", [he uses] "All-Gods".

sanskrit_iast: samrāḍ ayam asau \\ ity āha nāmagrahaṃ trir uccaiḥ //
meaning: सम्राड् अयम् असौ \\ इत्य् आह नामग्रहं त्रिर् उच्चैः //
text_mt: He calls out thrice aloud by name, "This N.N. is universal ruler!"

sanskrit_iast: agnir ekākṣareṇa \\ ity anuvākaṃ dvādaśavat kṛtvā naivārasviṣṭakṛdiḍaṃ karoti //
meaning: अग्निर् एकाक्षरेण \\ इत्य् अनुवाकं द्वादशवत् कृत्वा नैवारस्विष्टकृदिडं करोति //
text_mt: Having treated the anuvāka beginning with "Agni by a single syllable..." as containing twelve [parts], he performs the sviṣṭakṛt and iḍā offerings of the wild-rice oblation.
Having stepped down, [the sacrificer] goes forward for the chant when directed.
Or the Māhendra cup comes after the victory formulas.
At the end of the Ṣoḍaśin, the chant [is sung] with the cups alone.
He pours out seventeen [portions] into the cups of the officiating priests, two by two,
At the end of the conclusion-rite, he gives the sacrificial-post wrappers to the Adhvaryu priest.
He gives the golden garlands according as they have been used.
The iṣṭi, soma, and animal sacrifices have distinct common procedures because of differences in time.
The consecration takes place on the day of sacrifice of the Māgha fortnight.
At its conclusion, if he wishes, a full-spoon oblation is offered in his house, with a boon as sacrificial gift.
Beginning tomorrow, five succeeding [offerings are performed] day after day.

sanskrit_iast: śamyāyāḥ paścād dhaviṣyaśannam̐ sruve kṛtvā dakṣiṇāgnyulmukam ādāya dakṣiṇā gatvā svayampradīrṇa iriṇe vāgnau juhoti \\ eṣa te nirṛte \\ iti //
meaning: शम्यायाः पश्चाद् धविष्यशन्नम्̐ स्रुवे कृत्वा दक्षिणाग्न्युल्मुकम् आदाय दक्षिणा गत्वा स्वयम्प्रदीर्ण इरिणे वाग्नौ जुहोति \\ एष ते निरृते \\ इति //
text_mt: Having placed behind the yoke-pin the sacrificial food that has dropped into the dipping spoon, having taken a firebrand from the Dakṣiṇa fire and gone to the south, he offers it on fire in a natural cleft or in a barren tract with the mantra, "This to thee, O Nirṛti..."
Having returned without looking back, he performs the putting together of the grains and the rest for the Anumati cake.
Gold is [the dakṣiṇā] for the oblation to Agni and Viṣṇu.
A cow set free again is [the dakṣiṇā] for the oblation to Agni and Soma.
An uncastrated draught-ox is [the dakṣiṇā] for the oblation to Indra and Agni.
The performance of the Four-Month sacrifices takes place on the full-moon day of Phālguna.
Covering the dark fortnights by the full-moon sacrifice and the bright fortnights by the new-moon sacrifice, [he proceeds] up to the Śunāsīrīya.
The Śunāsīrīya takes place in the position of the consecration of the Pavitra.

sanskrit_iast: pañcavātīyam āhavanīyaṃ pratidiśaṃ vyuhya madhye ca sruveṇāgniṣu juhoti \\ agninetrebhyas \\ iti pratimantram //
meaning: पञ्चवातीयम् आहवनीयं प्रतिदिशं व्युह्य मध्ये च स्रुवेणाग्निषु जुहोति \\ अग्निनेत्रेभ्यस् \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: At the Pañcavātīya, having pushed apart the Āhavanīya fire toward each direction and into the center, he makes offerings in the fires with the dipping spoon, reciting a mantra for each with the formula beginning, "To those whose eyes are fire..."

sanskrit_iast: uttarāḥ samasya ye devās \\ iti pratimantram //
meaning: उत्तराः समस्य ये देवास् \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: Bringing them together [in the middle], he makes the following offerings, reciting a mantra for each with the formula beginning, "Which gods..."
A horse chariot drawn by three [horses] is the sacrificial gift.
a barley pap for Varuṇa;
Having placed grains of apāmārga in a dipping spoon made of palāśa or of vikankata wood,
The taking of the firebrand is done with the mantra, "O Agni, overpower..."

sanskrit_iast: rakṣasāṃ tvā \\ iti sruvam asyati tāṃ diśaṃ yasyāṃ juhoti //
meaning: रक्षसां त्वा \\ इति स्रुवम् अस्यति तां दिशं यस्यां जुहोति //
text_mt: He throws the dipping spoon with the mantra, "To the demons thee...", in the direction in which he offers.
They return without looking back, reciting, "We have slain the demons..."
Also when one is being bewitched, having gone in that direction,
If [the sacrificer] is practicing malevolent sorcery, he should utter the name [of his enemy] during the oblation, the throwing of the dipping spoon, and the returning.
[An offering] to Agni and Viṣṇu, [one] to Indra and Viṣṇu, and [one] to Viṣṇu; a dwarf [bull] is the sacrificial gift.
Wherever no gender is specified, a bovine [is meant] everywhere.
[An offering] to Agni and Pūṣan, [one] to Indra and Pūṣan, and [one] to Pūṣan; a black [bovine] is the sacrificial gift.
[An offering] to Agni and Soma, [one] to Indra and Soma, and [one] to Soma; a brown [bovine] is the sacrificial gift.
Each first [cake] is on eleven potsherds; the others are pap offerings.
Or the [cake] to Viṣṇu is on three potsherds.
On the next day, [a cake] to Vaiśvānara on twelve potsherds and [one] to Varuṇa, within a single common procedure;

sanskrit_iast: ṛṣabhaḥ pūrvasya dakṣiṇā kṛṣṇaṃ vāsa uttarasyābhāve 'kṛṣṇam //
meaning: ऋषभः पूर्वस्य दक्षिणा कृष्णं वास उत्तरस्याभावे ऽकृष्णम् //
text_mt: A bull is the sacrificial gift for the first; a black garment for the second, [or] in its absence, a non-black [garment].
Next are the twelve jewel offerings.
One in each house on successive days.
On fire produced by churning from [the fires] taken up [into the churning sticks], [a cake] to Agni Anīkavat [is offered] at the house of the commander of the army.
A pap to Bṛhaspati at the house of the royal priest.
[A pap] of gavedhukā grass seeds to Rudra at the house of the sacrificer from [materials taken from] the houses of the dice-keeper and the hunter.

meaning: चतुर्गृहीतम् \\ जुषाणो ऽध्वाज्यस्य वेतु \\ इति दूतस्य //
text_mt: A fourfold-ladled [ghee portion is offered] at the house of the messenger with the mantra: 'Taking pleasure, may the pathway partake of the ghee.'

sanskrit_iast: nairṛtaḥ parivṛttyai kṛṣṇavrīhīṇāṃ nakhanirbhinnānāṃ darvihomas \\ eṣa te nirṛte \\ iti juhoti //
meaning: नैरृतः परिवृत्त्यै कृष्णव्रीहीणां नखनिर्भिन्नानां दर्विहोमस् \\ एष ते निरृते \\ इति जुहोति //
text_mt: A ladle-offering to Nirṛti [of pap] made of black rice pierced with fingernails [is offered] at the house of the discarded wife with the formula: 'This is yours, O Nirṛti,' he offers;
The sacrificial gifts are in corresponding order:
either one with white forelegs or one with a white tail;
For the next [offering to the messenger, the gift is] a bow bound with a horsehair string and wrapped in pyukṣṇa bark;
For the last [offering, the gift is] a black, decrepit, lame [cow].

sanskrit_iast: parivṛttīṃ cāha mā me 'dyeśāyāṃ vātsīt \\ iti //
meaning: परिवृत्तीं चाह मा मे ऽद्येशायां वात्सीत् \\ इति //
text_mt: And he says to the discarded wife: 'May she not dwell in my realm today.'
Then there is a pap to Soma and Rudra in the milk of a white cow having a white calf.
One who has studied the Veda but is without fame should also perform this sacrifice;
[Then follows] a pap to Mitra and Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit_iast: bārhaspatyam adhiśrityāśvatthī yā svayambhagnā prācy udīcī vā śākhā tatpātreṇāpidadhāti //
meaning: बार्हस्पत्यम् अधिश्रित्याश्वत्थी या स्वयम्भग्ना प्राच्य् उदीची वा शाखा तत्पात्रेणापिदधाति //
text_mt: Having placed the pap to Bṛhaspati on the fire, he covers it with a bowl made of an aśvattha branch that was naturally broken off and pointed towards the east or towards the north.

sanskrit_iast: vināṭād rathaparyūḍhān navanītam̐ svayaṃjātam ājyam āsicya pātre tasmint sthaviṣṭhāṃs taṇḍulān mitrāyāvapati //
meaning: विनाटाद् रथपर्यूढान् नवनीतम्̐ स्वयंजातम् आज्यम् आसिच्य पात्रे तस्मिन्त् स्थविष्ठांस् तण्डुलान् मित्रायावपति //
text_mt: Having poured into that bowl melted butter that was spontaneously produced as butter in a leather bag driven on a chariot, he pours the thickest rice grains into it for Mitra.
The sacrificial grounds for the Abhiṣecanīya and Daśapeya are the southern and the northern [respectively].
The southern is for the Abhiṣecanīya.
He undergoes consecration for the Abhiṣecanīya on the day of sacrifice of the Phālguna fortnight.

sanskrit_iast: somaṃ krītvā dvaidham upanahyaṃ paryuhyaikaṃ brahmāgāre nidadhāti //
meaning: सोमं क्रीत्वा द्वैधम् उपनह्यं पर्युह्यैकं ब्रह्मागारे निदधाति //
text_mt: Having purchased the soma, having tied it into two bundles and carried it around, he places one in the Brahman's hall.

sanskrit_iast: agnīṣomīyasya paśupuroḍāśam anu devasūhavīm̐ṣi nirvapati yajapraiṣāṇi //
meaning: अग्नीषोमीयस्य पशुपुरोडाशम् अनु देवसूहवीम्̐षि निर्वपति यजप्रैषाणि //
text_mt: After the animal cake for Agni-Soma, he pours out the oblations to the divine impeller deities (devasū-havis), which have yajapraiṣa calls.
[A cake] of quick-growing rice for Savitṛ of true impulse;
of fast-growing rice for Agni, lord of the house;
of wild millet (śyāmāka) for Soma, lord of the forest;
of wild rice (nīvāra) for Bṛhaspati, lord of speech;
of red rice (hāyana) for Indra the eldest;
[and another] for Varuṇa, lord of dharma.

sanskrit_iast: uttamena caritvā savitā tvā \\ ity āha yajamānabāhuṃ dakṣiṇaṃ gṛhītvā //
meaning: उत्तमेन चरित्वा सविता त्वा \\ इत्य् आह यजमानबाहुं दक्षिणं गृहीत्वा //
text_mt: Having performed the last [offering], having grasped the sacrificer's right arm, he says: 'May Savitṛ... [impel] thee'.
He utters his name in the mantra at the appropriate place,

sanskrit_iast: yasyāś ca jāte rājā bhavati deśasyānavasthitatvāt //
meaning: यस्याश् च जाते राजा भवति देशस्यानवस्थितत्वात् //
text_mt: and of the people over whom he becomes king, because the country is not fixed.
The common procedure (tantra) is that of the animal cake, because of its primary status;
or [it is that] of the other [oblations], because they are more numerous,
the incidental waters north of the sacrificial post, because [the others] are not available [there];
in separate vessels made of udumbara wood:

sanskrit_iast: avagāhyāvagāḍhāt paśoḥ puruṣād vā pūrvāparā ūrmī //
meaning: अवगाह्यावगाढात् पशोः पुरुषाद् वा पूर्वापरा ऊर्मी //
text_mt: having plunged into [a river], the fore and hind waves caused by a plunging animal or man;
still waters of flowing [rivers] in the sunshine;
waters from the sun's heat, having caught [them] from the sky;
He collects the Sarasvatī waters with: 'Divine waters...'

sanskrit_iast: juhoty uttarāsu caturgṛhītāni vṛṣṇaūrmyādibhiḥ svāhākārāntaiḥ pūrvaiḥpūrvaiḥ pratimantram uttarairuttarair gṛhṇāti //
meaning: जुहोत्य् उत्तरासु चतुर्गृहीतानि वृष्णऊर्म्यादिभिः स्वाहाकारान्तैः पूर्वैःपूर्वैः प्रतिमन्त्रम् उत्तरैरुत्तरैर् गृह्णाति //
text_mt: With regard to the subsequent [waters], he offers four ladlefuls [each] with the preceding [half-verses] beginning with 'Of the bull, wave...' ending in svāhā, and collects [the waters] with each of the following [half-verses], mantra by mantra.

sanskrit_iast: āpaḥ svarājas \\ iti marīcīr gṛhītvāgṛhītvāñjalinā sarvāsu sam̐sṛjati //
meaning: आपः स्वराजस् \\ इति मरीचीर् गृहीत्वागृहीत्वाञ्जलिना सर्वासु सम्̐सृजति //
text_mt: With: 'The waters are self-ruling...', having gathered rays of light in the hollow of his hands, he mixes [them] into all [the waters].

sanskrit_iast: audumbare pātre samāsiñcaty enās \\ madhumatīr iti //
meaning: औदुम्बरे पात्रे समासिञ्चत्य् एनास् \\ मधुमतीर् इति //
text_mt: He pours them together into an udumbara vessel with: 'Rich in honey...'

sanskrit_iast: maitrāvaruṇadhiṣṇyasya purastān nidadhāti \\ anādhṛṣṭāḥ sīdata \\ iti //
meaning: मैत्रावरुणधिष्ण्यस्य पुरस्तान् निदधाति \\ अनाधृष्टाः सीदत \\ इति //
text_mt: He sets it down in front of the Maitrāvaruṇa's mound with: 'Sit down, unassailable!'
And [he sets down] silently the vessels of palāśa, udumbara, nyagrodha, and aśvattha for the unction.
The curds-mixture (payasyā) for Mitra-Varuṇa is [offered] along with the midday [libations].
The sacrificial gifts are a hundred thousand [cows].

sanskrit_iast: marutvatīyānte pātrāṇi pūrveṇa vyāghracarmāstṛṇāti somasya tviṣir iti //
meaning: मरुत्वतीयान्ते पात्राणि पूर्वेण व्याघ्रचर्मास्तृणाति सोमस्य त्विषिर् इति //
text_mt: At the end of the Marutvatīya libation, to the east of the vessels, he spreads out a tiger skin with: 'Thou art the splendour of Soma...'
At its western edge, he places a piece of lead.

sanskrit_iast: pārthānām agnaye svāhā \\ iti ṣaḍ juhoti pratimantram //
meaning: पार्थानाम् अग्नये स्वाहा \\ इति षड् जुहोति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: He makes six oblations of the earth-mantras (pārtha) with: 'To Agni, svāhā...', mantra by mantra.
Having made two strainers, he weaves a piece of gold into them.

sanskrit_iast: tābhyām utpunāty apaḥ savitur vas \\ iti //
meaning: ताभ्याम् उत्पुनात्य् अपः सवितुर् वस् \\ इति //
text_mt: With them both, he purifies the waters with: 'Of Savitṛ you are...'
He pours them into the unction vessels with: 'Companions in revelry...'
He causes [the sacrificer] to put on a tārpya garment,
Putting on an upper garment [and] winding a turban, he wears it hanging down his neck.
Or he winds it around the region of the navel.
[He puts on] the tārpya garment and the others with the mantras beginning, "Of the realm…", respectively.

sanskrit_iast: dīkṣitavasananivṛttir virodhān māhendrādau vā punaḥparidhānaṃ nidhāyaitāni //
meaning: दीक्षितवसननिवृत्तिर् विरोधान् माहेन्द्रादौ वा पुनःपरिधानं निधायैतानि //
text_mt: There is cessation of wearing the garments of the consecrated, because of incompatibility; or having deposited them, he puts them on again at the beginning of the Māhendra [cup] or the like.
With "Indra's slayer of Vṛtra…", he strings the bow.

sanskrit_iast: mitrasya \ varuṇasya \\ ity asya bāhū vimārṣṭi //
meaning: मित्रस्य \ वरुणस्य \\ इत्य् अस्य बाहू विमार्ष्टि //
text_mt: With "Of Mitra…" [and] "…of Varuṇa…", he wipes his arms.
He hands over the bow with "By thee, this…".

sanskrit_iast: dṛbāsi \\ iti pratimantram ādāya tisraḥ iṣūḥ prayachati pātainam iti pratimantram //
meaning: दृबासि \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् आदाय तिस्रः इषूः प्रयछति पातैनम् इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: Taking three arrows, each with the mantra, "A piercer art thou…", he hands them over, each with the mantra, "Protect him…".
He causes [him] to recite, "Manifest, O mortals…".

sanskrit_iast: aveṣṭās \\ iti lohāyasam āvidhyati keśavāsye sado'nta upaviṣṭāya //
meaning: अवेष्टास् \\ इति लोहायसम् आविध्यति केशवास्ये सदोऽन्त उपविष्टाय //
text_mt: With "Thou art enveloped…", he shoots a copper piece at a long-haired man seated at the end of the Sadas.

sanskrit_iast: sunvantam ākramayan diśaḥ prācīm āroha \\ iti vācayati pratidiśaṃ yathāliṅgam //
meaning: सुन्वन्तम् आक्रमयन् दिशः प्राचीम् आरोह \\ इति वाचयति प्रतिदिशं यथालिङ्गम् //
text_mt: Making the soma-presser step across the quarters, he causes him to recite according to the characteristic mark for each quarter, "Ascend the east…".

sanskrit_iast: ākramya pādena sīsaṃ nirasyati pratyastam iti //
meaning: आक्रम्य पादेन सीसं निरस्यति प्रत्यस्तम् इति //
text_mt: Having stepped on a piece of lead with his foot, he kicks it away with "Cast off!".
He causes him to step onto a tiger-skin with "The splendour of Soma art thou…".
He places a gold plate under his feet with "From death…".

sanskrit_iast: śirasi ca navatardmam̐ śatatardmaṃ vā \\ ojo 'si \\ iti //
meaning: शिरसि च नवतर्द्मम्̐ शततर्द्मं वा \\ ओजो ऽसि \\ इति //
text_mt: And on his head [he places a gold plate] having nine perforations or a hundred perforations, with "Ojas art thou…".
He raises his arms with "Golden-formed…".

meaning: मित्रो ऽसि \ वरुणो ऽसि \\ इति वा //
text_mt: Or with "Thou art Mitra…", "Thou art Varuṇa…".

sanskrit_iast: sthitaṃ prāñcam abhiṣiñcati purohito 'dhvaryur vā purastāt pālāśena prathamam paścād itare dvitīyena svastṛtīyena mitryo rājanyo vaiśyaś caturthena somasya tvā dyumnena \\ iti pratimantram //
meaning: स्थितं प्राञ्चम् अभिषिञ्चति पुरोहितो ऽध्वर्युर् वा पुरस्तात् पालाशेन प्रथमम् पश्चाद् इतरे द्वितीयेन स्वस्तृतीयेन मित्र्यो राजन्यो वैश्यश् चतुर्थेन सोमस्य त्वा द्युम्नेन \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: While he stands facing east, the royal chaplain or the Adhvaryu consecrates [him] from the east first with the palāśa vessel; the others from the west with the second; a relative with the third; an allied nobleman or a Vaiśya with the fourth, each with the mantra, "With the glory of Soma, thee…".
[He supplies] "I consecrate" everywhere, because [the mantra] requires it.
And [he recites], "Become the lord of realms among realms…".

sanskrit_iast: imam amuṣya \\ iti ca prathamo devasūvat //
meaning: इमम् अमुष्य \\ इति च प्रथमो देवसूवत् //
text_mt: And the first [officiant recites], "This [man], of such-and-such…", as in the Devasū oblations.

sanskrit_iast: pārthānām indrāya svāhā \\ iti ṣaḍ juhoti pratimantram //
meaning: पार्थानाम् इन्द्राय स्वाहा \\ इति षड् जुहोति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: He makes six offerings to Indra of the Pārthas, each with the mantra, "To Indra, hail!".
And he orders the Śunaḥśepa [story to be recited].

sanskrit_iast: o3m ity ṛcāṃ pratigaras tathā \\ iti gāthānām //
meaning: ओ3म् इत्य् ऋचां प्रतिगरस् तथा \\ इति गाथानाम् //
text_mt: "Om" is the response to the verses; "Thus" [is the response] to the gāthās.
The Hotṛ and the Adhvaryu are seated on two golden cushions.
At the conclusion of the Śunaḥśepa [recitation], he gives a hundred [cows] each.
With the scratching-stick, he smears himself with the unction with "Forth from the mountain…".

sanskrit_iast: carmaṇi trir vikramayati viṣṇor iti pratimantram //
meaning: चर्मणि त्रिर् विक्रमयति विष्णोर् इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: He makes him take three steps on the skin, each with the mantra, "Of Viṣṇu…".

sanskrit_iast: pālāśe śeṣān āsicya putrāya prayachati priyatamāya \\ idaṃ me karmedaṃ vīryaṃ putro 'nusaṃtanotu \\ iti //
meaning: पालाशे शेषान् आसिच्य पुत्राय प्रयछति प्रियतमाय \\ इदं मे कर्मेदं वीर्यं पुत्रो ऽनुसंतनोतु \\ इति //
text_mt: Pouring the remainder into the palāśa vessel, he hands it to his dearest son with "May my son continue this action of mine, this virility of mine!".

sanskrit_iast: śālādvārye juhoti putre 'nvārabdhe prajāpate \\ iti putrayajamānayor nāma gṛhṇāti pitṛśabdaṃ putre kṛtvā yathāyathaṃ paścāt //
meaning: शालाद्वार्ये जुहोति पुत्रे ऽन्वारब्धे प्रजापते \\ इति पुत्रयजमानयोर् नाम गृह्णाति पितृशब्दं पुत्रे कृत्वा यथायथं पश्चात् //
text_mt: While the son holds on [to him], he offers in the Śālādvārya fire with "O Prajāpati…"; he utters the names of the son and the sacrificer, applying the word "father" to the son, appropriately thereafter.

sanskrit_iast: āgnīdhrīye pālāśena śeṣān juhoti rudra yat te \\ ity uttarārdhe //
meaning: आग्नीध्रीये पालाशेन शेषान् जुहोति रुद्र यत् ते \\ इत्य् उत्तरार्धे //
text_mt: With the palāśa vessel, he offers the remains in the northern half of the Āgnīdhra fire with "O Rudra, that which is thine…".

sanskrit_iast: gavām̐ śatam adhikaṃ vā svasyāhavanīyasyottarata sthāpayati //
meaning: गवाम्̐ शतम् अधिकं वा स्वस्याहवनीयस्योत्तरत स्थापयति //
text_mt: He places a hundred cows or more to the north of his own Āhavanīya fire.
And the vehicle for the former fire, along with the fire.

sanskrit_iast: vājapeyavad ratham avahṛtya dakṣiṇasyāṃ vediśroṇau yunakti pūrvavat \\ mitrāvaruṇayor iti caturbhiḥ //
meaning: वाजपेयवद् रथम् अवहृत्य दक्षिणस्यां वेदिश्रोणौ युनक्ति पूर्ववत् \\ मित्रावरुणयोर् इति चतुर्भिः //
text_mt: Bringing down the chariot as in the Vājapeya sacrifice, he yokes it at the southern hip of the altar as before, with the four mantras beginning with "Of Mitra and Varuṇa…".
Going by the southern path, he stops it west of the Cātvāla pit.
With "For unsteadiness thee!", the soma-presser mounts [the chariot].
With "Of the Maruts…", he drives the right yoked horse.
He stops in the midst of the cows with "We have reached…".

sanskrit_iast: dhanurārtnyopaspṛśati gāṃ yajamānaḥ sam indriyeṇa \\ iti //
meaning: धनुरार्त्न्योपस्पृशति गां यजमानः सम् इन्द्रियेण \\ इति //
text_mt: With the end of the bow, the sacrificer touches a cow with "Together with virility…".
And he says, "These I conquer, these I make [mine].".

sanskrit_iast: tāvadbhūyo vā gosvāmine datvā pūrveṇa yūpaṃ parītyāntaḥpātyadeśe sthāpayati mā te \\ iti //
meaning: तावद्भूयो वा गोस्वामिने दत्वा पूर्वेण यूपं परीत्यान्तःपात्यदेशे स्थापयति मा ते \\ इति //
text_mt: Having given as many [cows] or more to the owner of the cows, he goes around to the east of the sacrificial post and stops in the Antaḥpātya space with "Let not thy…".

sanskrit_iast: agnaye gṛhapataye \\ iti catvāri rathavimocanīyāni juhoti pratimantram //
meaning: अग्नये गृहपतये \\ इति चत्वारि रथविमोचनीयानि जुहोति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: He offers the four chariot-unyoking oblations with "To Agni, lord of the house…", each with its mantra.

meaning: पशूनाम्̐ रसो ऽसि \\ इति वराहोपनहा उपमुञ्चते //
text_mt: With "The essence of beasts art thou…", he puts on boar-skin sandals.
He looks at the earth with "O mother Earth…".
He descends with "The goose seated in the clear…".
Having unyoked [the chariot], he places it along with the driver onto the chariot-stand.
The driver steps down to the south of the hall.

meaning: रथवाहणस्य दक्षिणे ऽन्ते शतमानाव् आसजति वृत्तौ //
text_mt: At the southern end of the chariot-stand, he attaches two round gold pieces of one hundred mānas.
Along the track, he conceals an audumbarī branch.
He touches the two hundred-māna pieces with "So much art thou…".

sanskrit_iast: tau brahmaṇe datvā \\ ūrg asi \\ iti śākhām upaspṛśati //
meaning: तौ ब्रह्मणे दत्वा \\ ऊर्ग् असि \\ इति शाखाम् उपस्पृशति //
text_mt: Having given those two to the Brahman priest, he touches the branch with "Vigour art thou…".

sanskrit_iast: indrasya vām ity avaharate bāhū payasyāyāṃ vyāghracarmadeśe sthitāyām //
meaning: इन्द्रस्य वाम् इत्य् अवहरते बाहू पयस्यायां व्याघ्रचर्मदेशे स्थितायाम् //
text_mt: With "Of Indra are ye two…", he lowers his arms, while the curd-mixture is placed on the site of the tiger-skin.
He hands over the bow together with the arrows.

sanskrit_iast: uttaravedim̐ hṛtvā pasyayā pracarati prāk sviṣṭakṛtaḥ //
meaning: उत्तरवेदिम्̐ हृत्वा पस्यया प्रचरति प्राक् स्विष्टकृतः //
text_mt: having carried away the high altar, he proceeds with the pasyā offering before the sviṣṭakṛt.

sanskrit_iast: khādirīm āsandīm̐ rajjūtāṃ vyāghracarmadeśe nidadhāti syonāsi \\ iti //
meaning: खादिरीम् आसन्दीम्̐ रज्जूतां व्याघ्रचर्मदेशे निदधाति स्योनासि \\ इति //
text_mt: He places a stool of khadira wood, woven with cords, on the place of the tiger skin with [the mantra]: "You are pleasant..."

sanskrit_iast: adhīvāsam asyām āstṛṇāti kṣatrasya yonir iti //
meaning: अधीवासम् अस्याम् आस्तृणाति क्षत्रस्य योनिर् इति //
text_mt: He spreads an upper garment upon it with [the mantra]: "The womb of royal power..."

sanskrit_iast: sunvantam asyām upaveśayati syonām āsīda \\ iti //
meaning: सुन्वन्तम् अस्याम् उपवेशयति स्योनाम् आसीद \\ इति //
text_mt: He makes the soma-presser sit down upon it with [the mantra]: "Sit upon the pleasant [stool]..."
With [the mantra]: "He has sat down...", he touches his chest.

sanskrit_iast: abhibhūr ity asmai pañcākṣān pāṇāv ādhāya paścād enaṃ yajñiyavṛkṣadaṇḍaiḥ śanais tūṣṇīṃ ghnanti //
meaning: अभिभूर् इत्य् अस्मै पञ्चाक्षान् पाणाव् आधाय पश्चाद् एनं यज्ञियवृक्षदण्डैः शनैस् तूष्णीं घ्नन्ति //
text_mt: With [the mantra]: "Victorious...", having placed five dice in his hand, they strike him quietly from behind with sticks of sacrificial trees, silently.

sanskrit_iast: pāpmānaṃ te 'pahanmas \\ ati tvā badhaṃ nayāmi \\ iti vā //
meaning: पाप्मानं ते ऽपहन्मस् \\ अति त्वा बधं नयामि \\ इति वा //
text_mt: Or with: "We smite away your evil!" [or] "I lead you beyond slaughter."

sanskrit_iast: varaṃ vṛtvā brahman \\ ity āmantrayate pañcakṛtvaḥ //
meaning: वरं वृत्वा ब्रह्मन् \\ इत्य् आमन्त्रयते पञ्चकृत्वः //
text_mt: Having chosen a boon, he addresses: "O Brahman!" five times.

sanskrit_iast: pratyāha vyatyāsam \\ savitā \ varuṇas \\ indras \\ rudras \\ iti tvaṃ brahmāsi \\ ityādibhiḥ //
meaning: प्रत्याह व्यत्यासम् \\ सविता \ वरुणस् \\ इन्द्रस् \\ रुद्रस् \\ इति त्वं ब्रह्मासि \\ इत्यादिभिः //
text_mt: He answers alternately with: "Savitṛ...", "Varuṇa...", "Indra...", "Rudra...", beginning with "You are the Brahman priest..."
And he calls out: "O Bahukāra!" to one of that name.

sanskrit_iast: sphyam asmai prayachati purohito 'dhvaryur vā \\ indrasya vajras \\ iti //
meaning: स्फ्यम् अस्मै प्रयछति पुरोहितो ऽध्वर्युर् वा \\ इन्द्रस्य वज्रस् \\ इति //
text_mt: The chaplain or the Adhvaryu priest hands him a wooden sword with [the mantra]: "The thunderbolt of Indra..."

sanskrit_iast: rājā rājabhrātā sūtasthapatyor anyataro grāmaṇīḥ sajātaś caivaṃ pūrvaḥpūrva uttarasmai //
meaning: राजा राजभ्राता सूतस्थपत्योर् अन्यतरो ग्रामणीः सजातश् चैवं पूर्वःपूर्व उत्तरस्मै //
text_mt: The king [hands it] to the king's brother, [he] to either the charioteer or the governor, [he] to the village headman, and [he] to a kinsman—in this way each preceding one to the succeeding one.

sanskrit_iast: prattena sajātaḥ pratiprasthātā ca pūrvāgnisahitām̐ śukrapurorucā dyūtabhūmiṃ kurutaḥ //
meaning: प्रत्तेन सजातः प्रतिप्रस्थाता च पूर्वाग्निसहिताम्̐ शुक्रपुरोरुचा द्यूतभूमिं कुरुतः //
text_mt: With that which has been handed over, the kinsman and the Pratiprasthātṛ prepare the gambling ground together with the eastern fire with the Śukra puroruc-verse.

sanskrit_iast: dyūtabhūmau hiraṇyaṃ nidhāyābhijuhoti caturgṛhītena \\ agniḥ pṛthur iti //
meaning: द्यूतभूमौ हिरण्यं निधायाभिजुहोति चतुर्गृहीतेन \\ अग्निः पृथुर् इति //
text_mt: Having placed gold on the gambling ground, he offers upon it with four ladlings [of clarified butter] with [the mantra]: "Agni is wide..."
He casts the dice with: "Consecrated with svāhā..."
Or he should assign the Kṛta and other [dice-throws] to the king and the others.
He performs the Sviṣṭakṛt and the Iḍā rites of the curd mixture (payasyā).
Having stepped down, [the sacrificer] goes [to the sadas] when summoned for the chant.

sanskrit_iast: avabhṛtham ekena tārpyādīni cet udaity ekena //
meaning: अवभृथम् एकेन तार्प्यादीनि चेत् उदैत्य् एकेन //
text_mt: If [he wears] the tarpya cloth and other garments, [he goes] into the final bath wearing one, and comes out wearing one.
And he casts away the garment of the consecrated.
He should give these [garments] at the end of the omentum oblation of the anūbandhyā cow.
The Udavasānīyā is the Traidhātavī rite.
[It consists of] a cake on twelve potsherds for Indra-and-Viṣṇu, made of rice and barley.
A third part of barley is in the middle.

sanskrit_iast: tisrastisro dakṣiṇā dadāti śatamānāni brahmaṇe dhenūr hotre vāsām̐sy adhvaryave gām agnīdhe //
meaning: तिस्रस्तिस्रो दक्षिणा ददाति शतमानानि ब्रह्मणे धेनूर् होत्रे वासाम्̐स्य् अध्वर्यवे गाम् अग्नीधे //
text_mt: He gives three sacrificial gifts each: three śatamānas of gold to the Brahman priest, three milch cows to the Hotṛ priest, three garments to the Adhvaryu priest, [and] a cow to the Agnīdh priest.
This [rite] is also for healing and for sorcery.
He offers the ten subsequent Saṃsṛp oblations.
With each one, he moves forward to another sacrificial ground.
[The offerings are] dedicated to Savitṛ, Sarasvatī, Tvaṣṭṛ, Pūṣan, Indra, Bṛhaspati, Varuṇa, Agni, Soma, and Viṣṇu, as prescribed.
At each offering (iṣṭi), he presents lotuses.
He fastens a garland made of them upon himself.
The two rites share a single common procedure, because the soma purchase is one.
Or they are separate, because of the scriptural mention of the final bath and consecration [for both].
However, it is a single rite, because of the adherence to continuous succession.
The repetition of the final bath and consecration is on account of explicit injunction.
On the seventh day, having fetched the soma from the Brahman priest's dwelling, he performs the touching of the stool and the other [rites].
Wishing to end with the Upasad rite, he offers the oblations to the Upasad deities as prescribed.
