text_mt: The placing of fuel sticks: śamī, kārṣmarya, vikaṅkata, and udumbara sticks, with each verse of: "That of Savitṛ…"; the last one has ear-like sprouts.
In the absence of ear-like sprouts, they are smeared with curd drops.

sanskrit_iast: sruvāhutī juhoti \\ agne tam adya \\ iti ca pratyṛcam //
meaning: स्रुवाहुती जुहोति \\ अग्ने तम् अद्य \\ इति च प्रत्यृचम् //
text_mt: He offers dipping-spoon oblations with each verse of: "O Agni, him today…",
and the full-spoon oblation (pūrṇāhuti) with: "Seven are thy…"
Standing, [he places] the fuel sticks everywhere in the middle;
having sat down, [he offers] the oblations at the ends.
Here [takes place] the attendance upon the fifth [layer] with seven verses, because of the laying down of everything;
or after having piled the dhiṣṇya hearths, because of connection with the highest.
If he wishes, he may touch it with: "The year art thou…"
He apportions the offerings to Vaiśvānara and the Maruts as prescribed.
Having set the Vaiśvānara [cake] on the fire, [he sets] the two Māruta [cakes] to the south and north,
and to the west, closer together;

sanskrit_iast: puchād aparān kuśān āstīryāhavanīyasahitān vā tatrāsādanam //
meaning: पुछाद् अपरान् कुशान् आस्तीर्याहवनीयसहितान् वा तत्रासादनम् //
text_mt: Having spread kuśa grass to the west of the tail, or together with the Āhavanīya fire, the setting down takes place there.

sanskrit_iast: vaiśvānareṇa pracarya sarvahutena hastena mārutān juhoty upaviśya vaiśvānare vā vaiśvānaraṃ pṛthuṃ kṛtvā śukrajyotir iti pratimantram //
meaning: वैश्वानरेण प्रचर्य सर्वहुतेन हस्तेन मारुतान् जुहोत्य् उपविश्य वैश्वानरे वा वैश्वानरं पृथुं कृत्वा शुक्रज्योतिर् इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: Having performed the rite with the Vaiśvānara [cake] as entirely offered, having sat down, he offers the Māruta [cakes] with his hand into the Vaiśvānara [fire], or having made the Vaiśvānara [fire] wide, with each mantra: "Of bright light…"
The Āraṇyānūcya [rite] [takes place] without the vimukha mantra.
He mutters: "Indra, the divine…"
Or he makes [the sacrificer] recite: "This breast…"

sanskrit_iast: vasordhārāṃ juhoty audumbaryā pañcagṛhītam̐ saṃtataṃ yajamāno 'raṇye 'nūcye 'gniprāpte vājaś ca me \\ ity aṣṭānuvākena //
meaning: वसोर्धारां जुहोत्य् औदुम्बर्या पञ्चगृहीतम्̐ संततं यजमानो ऽरण्ये ऽनूच्ये ऽग्निप्राप्ते वाजश् च मे \\ इत्य् अष्टानुवाकेन //
text_mt: The sacrificer offers the continuous shower of wealth (vasordhārā) with the udumbara ladle, consisting of five ladlings, when the Āraṇyānūcya has reached the fire, with the eight anuvākas: "And strength for me…"

sanskrit_iast: agnaye svāhā \\ iti ṣaṭ pārthāni juhoti //
meaning: अग्नये स्वाहा \\ इति षट् पार्थानि जुहोति //
text_mt: He offers the six Pārtha offerings with: "To Agni, svāhā…"

sanskrit_iast: vājaprasavīyāni vaprāvat sambhṛtya camasavat sruveṇa vājapeyikāni vājasyemam iti //
meaning: वाजप्रसवीयानि वप्रावत् सम्भृत्य चमसवत् स्रुवेण वाजपेयिकानि वाजस्येमम् इति //
text_mt: Having gathered the Vājaprasavīya oblations as at the mound, [and offered them] with the dipping spoon like the cups, the Vājapeya oblations [are offered] with: "This of vigour…",
and the offerings pertaining to Agni with: "Now of vigour…"

sanskrit_iast: sruvaṃ prāsya pariśritspṛkkṛṣṇājinam āstīrya puchād uttaram̐ śeṣe 'paḥ kṛtvā //
meaning: स्रुवं प्रास्य परिश्रित्स्पृक्कृष्णाजिनम् आस्तीर्य पुछाद् उत्तरम्̐ शेषे ऽपः कृत्वा //
text_mt: Throwing down the dipping spoon, spreading a black antelope skin touching the enclosing stones to the north of the tail [of the altar], and putting water into the residue;
Or milk and water, according to the Vedic text: "They belong to the Vājapeya";

sanskrit_iast: tatrābhiṣicyate brahmavarcasakāmaś cityanvārabdhas \\ devasya tvā \\ iti //
meaning: तत्राभिषिच्यते ब्रह्मवर्चसकामश् चित्यन्वारब्धस् \\ देवस्य त्वा \\ इति //
text_mt: There one desiring spiritual lustre is sprinkled, touching the altar, with [the mantra]: "At the impulse of the divine [Savitṛ]...";
On a he-goat skin, if he desires nourishment;
Some [say it takes place] to the south of the altar, or on it;

sanskrit_iast: prāsya camasam indrāya svāhā \\ iti ṣaḍ juhoti pratimantram //
meaning: प्रास्य चमसम् इन्द्राय स्वाहा \\ इति षड् जुहोति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: Having thrown down the cup, he offers six [oblations] with: "To Indra svāhā!", per mantra;

sanskrit_iast: dvādaśagṛhītaṃ vigrāhaṃ juhoti \\ ṛtāṣāḍ iti pratisvāhākāram̐ rāṣṭrabhṛto vāṭkārāntaḥ pūrvaḥpūrvo mantraḥ //
meaning: द्वादशगृहीतं विग्राहं जुहोति \\ ऋताषाड् इति प्रतिस्वाहाकारम्̐ राष्ट्रभृतो वाट्कारान्तः पूर्वःपूर्वो मन्त्रः //
text_mt: He makes a twelve-fold drawing and offers [it] with each svāhā-call [in]: "Ṛtāṣāḍ..."; or the realm-sustaining [oblations]—each preceding mantra ends with a vāṭ-call;

sanskrit_iast: pañcagṛhītaṃ ca rathaśirasy adhyadhy āhavanīyaṃ dhriyamāṇe pañcakṛtvaḥ sa no bhuvanasya \\ iti //
meaning: पञ्चगृहीतं च रथशिरस्य् अध्यध्य् आहवनीयं ध्रियमाणे पञ्चकृत्वः स नो भुवनस्य \\ इति //
text_mt: And five-times-drawn [clarified butter], while the chariot-head is held right over the Āhavanīya fire, five times with: "May he of the world...";
The carrying around the chariot seat is sunwise;
The Adhvaryu priest faces the chariot-head;

sanskrit_iast: vātahomān juhoty añjalināhṛtya purastād bahirveder adho dakṣiṇasyāṃ dhury uttarata uttarasyāṃ dakṣiṇato dakṣiṇāpraṣṭeḥ samudro 'si \\ iti pratimantram //
meaning: वातहोमान् जुहोत्य् अञ्जलिनाहृत्य पुरस्ताद् बहिर्वेदेर् अधो दक्षिणस्यां धुर्य् उत्तरत उत्तरस्यां दक्षिणतो दक्षिणाप्रष्टेः समुद्रो ऽसि \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: Having taken [water] in the hollow of his hands, he offers the wind-oblations in front, outside the sacrificial altar, below the southern yoke, to the north on the northern [yoke], to the south of the right-hand outrigger horse, per mantra with: "You are the ocean...";
And the leading around of the yoke-halter [takes place] everywhere;
Having taken [the chariot], it is carried to the Adhvaryu's dwelling;
At the time of the sacrificial gifts, he gives [it] to the Adhvaryu priest;

sanskrit_iast: nava juhoti yās te \\ iti pratimantram //
meaning: नव जुहोति यास् ते \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: He offers nine [oblations] with: "Those which are yours...", per mantra;
Knowing [them], he may alternatively offer those stated in the Brāhmaṇa;

sanskrit_iast: havirdhānaprakṣālanādy āgnīdhrālambhanāt kṛtvā dhiṣṇyāṃś cinoty aṣṭeṣṭakāṃ lokampṛṇābhiś catuḥsraktīṃs tiraśco nyupyanyupya //
meaning: हविर्धानप्रक्षालनाद्य् आग्नीध्रालम्भनात् कृत्वा धिष्ण्यांश् चिनोत्य् अष्टेष्टकां लोकम्पृणाभिश् चतुःस्रक्तींस् तिरश्चो न्युप्यन्युप्य //
text_mt: Having performed [the rites] from the washing of the havirdhāna carts up to the touching of the Āgnīdhra hearth, he piles the dhiṣṇya hearths with eight bricks [each], four-cornered, scattering [earth] crosswise repeatedly with the lokampṛṇā bricks;
And a speckled stone on the Āgnīdhra hearth;
On the Hotṛ's hearth, three times with twenty-one [bricks];
On the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin's hearth, twice with eleven; six on the Mārjālīya hearth;
Having placed the enclosing stones around according to the number of bricks;
[The rites] from the assignments up to the cake-sviṣṭakṛt are like those of the consecration ceremony;

sanskrit_iast: agniyojanaṃ prātaranuvākam upākariṣyan paridhīn ālambhya yathāpūrvam agniṃ yunajmi \\ iti pratyṛcam //
meaning: अग्नियोजनं प्रातरनुवाकम् उपाकरिष्यन् परिधीन् आलम्भ्य यथापूर्वम् अग्निं युनज्मि \\ इति प्रत्यृचम् //
text_mt: The yoking of the fire: when about to inaugurate the morning recitation, touching the enclosing sticks in regular sequence, [he yokes it] with: "I yoke Agni...", per verse;

sanskrit_iast: āgnimārutastotrapurastād vimocanaṃ paridhiṣaṃdhyor \\ divo mūrdhā \\ iti pratyṛcam //
meaning: आग्निमारुतस्तोत्रपुरस्ताद् विमोचनं परिधिषंध्योर् \\ दिवो मूर्धा \\ इति प्रत्यृचम् //
text_mt: The unyoking is before the Āgnimāruta chant, at the junctions of the enclosing sticks, with: "Head of heaven...", per verse;
Some say: having yoked [it] at the introductory Atirātra, the unyoking [takes place] at the concluding one;

sanskrit_iast: adhvarasamiṣṭayajurante \\ iṣṭo yajñas \\ iti pratyṛcam apare //
meaning: अध्वरसमिष्टयजुरन्ते \\ इष्टो यज्ञस् \\ इति प्रत्यृचम् अपरे //
text_mt: Others say: at the end of the Samiṣṭayajus offerings of the Soma sacrifice, with: "Offered is the sacrifice...", per verse;

sanskrit_iast: paśupuroḍāśam anv anūbandhyasya devikāhavīm̐ṣi nirvapati yajñapraiṣāṇi //
meaning: पशुपुरोडाशम् अन्व् अनूबन्ध्यस्य देविकाहवीम्̐षि निर्वपति यज्ञप्रैषाणि //
text_mt: Following the animal cake of the anūbandhyā cow, he measures out the oblations to the Devikās, which have sacrificial calls of the primary sacrifice;
Boiled rice dishes for Anumati, Rākā, Sinīvālī, and Kuhū; a cake on twelve potsherds for Dhātṛ, offered entirely;

sanskrit_iast: hṛdayaśūlānte sruvāhutīr juhoti yad ākūtāt \\ iti pratyṛcam aṣṭau //
meaning: हृदयशूलान्ते स्रुवाहुतीर् जुहोति यद् आकूतात् \\ इति प्रत्यृचम् अष्टौ //
text_mt: At the end of the heart-spit [rite], he offers eight dipping-spoon oblations with: "From what intention...", per verse;

sanskrit_iast: citro 'si \\ iti cityanāma kṛtvopatiṣṭhate ye agnayas \\ iti //
meaning: चित्रो ऽसि \\ इति चित्यनाम कृत्वोपतिष्ठते ये अग्नयस् \\ इति //
text_mt: Naming the altar: "You are the bright one...", he reveres it with: "Which fires...";
At the end of the concluding Udavasānīyā rite, there is a curd offering to Mitra and Varuṇa, with a pair of hornless [goats] as the sacrificial gift;
The observances last for life, due to the lack of specification;
Or for a year, because of the indefiniteness of time;
If one is unable to pile the altar at a subsequent soma sacrifice, [he sets down] any one among the naturally perforated, Viśvajyotis, and seasonal bricks;
Because the altar has already attained the status of the Āhavanīya fire;
The Sautrāmaṇī is a Brāhmaṇa sacrifice for one desiring prosperity;
For one who has piled the fire altar, one who has performed a soma sacrifice, one over-purged by soma, and one who has vomited soma;

sanskrit_iast: abhyādadhāmi \\ iti pratyṛcam āhavanīye tisraḥ samidho 'bhyādadhāti //
meaning: अभ्यादधामि \\ इति प्रत्यृचम् आहवनीये तिस्रः समिधो ऽभ्यादधाति //
text_mt: With the verse beginning 'I place upon,' verse by verse, he places three kindling sticks upon the Āhavanīya fire.
Some [authorities hold] the reverse order for the pap (caru) and the animal [sacrifice].

sanskrit_iast: antaḥpātyasthāne carmaṇi surāsomavikrayiṇaḥ sīsena śaṣpakrayas tokmānām ūrṇābhir lājānām̐ sūtraiḥ surāsomavikrayin krayyās te surāsomā ity āmantrya sarveṣu //
meaning: अन्तःपात्यस्थाने चर्मणि सुरासोमविक्रयिणः सीसेन शष्पक्रयस् तोक्मानाम् ऊर्णाभिर् लाजानाम्̐ सूत्रैः सुरासोमविक्रयिन् क्रय्यास् ते सुरासोमा इत्य् आमन्त्र्य सर्वेषु //
text_mt: On a hide at the place of the antaḥpātya-peg, he buys young sprouting grass with lead, malted grain with wool, and parched grain with threads from a seller of surā and soma, addressing [him] in all [cases] with: 'O seller of surā and soma, is your surā and soma for sale?'

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇena hṛtvā nagnahucūrṇāni kṛtvā tāṃś ca vrīhiśyāmākaudanayoḥ pṛthag ācāmau niṣicya cūrṇaiḥ sam̐sṛjya nidadhāti tan māsaram //
meaning: दक्षिणेन हृत्वा नग्नहुचूर्णानि कृत्वा तांश् च व्रीहिश्यामाकौदनयोः पृथग् आचामौ निषिच्य चूर्णैः सम्̐सृज्य निदधाति तन् मासरम् //
text_mt: Having carried [them] to the south, he powders the yeast; having poured out separately the gruels of rice and śyāmāka grain porridge and mixed [them] with the powders, he deposits [the mixture]: that is māsara.

sanskrit_iast: odanau cūrṇamāsaraiḥ sam̐sṛjya svādvīṃ tvā \\ am̐śunā te \\ iti trirātraṃ nidadhāti //
meaning: ओदनौ चूर्णमासरैः सम्̐सृज्य स्वाद्वीं त्वा \\ अम्̐शुना ते \\ इति त्रिरात्रं निदधाति //
text_mt: Having mixed the two porridges with the powders and the māsara, he deposits [them] for three nights with: 'Thee, sweet...' and 'Through thy shoot...'

sanskrit_iast: ekasyāḥ payasāpākṛtenāśvinena pariṣiñcati parīto ṣiñcatā \\ iti //
meaning: एकस्याः पयसापाकृतेनाश्विनेन परिषिञ्चति परीतो षिञ्चता \\ इति //
text_mt: He sprinkles [the mixture] with the milk of one [cow], which was taken aside, dedicated to the Aśvins, with: 'Sprinkle around from here...'
And he scatters powders of young sprouting grass.
In the morning, [he sprinkles] with [the milk] of two [cows], dedicated to Sarasvatī.
On the last [morning, he sprinkles] with [the milk] of three [cows], dedicated to Indra.
He measures out the two altars as in the Varuṇapraghāsa rites.
The northern [altar is laid out] like that of the soma [sacrifice], with one-third of a prakrama turned back.
West of the two, he makes two mounds.
Tomorrow he performs [the rites] beginning with the placing of the praṇayanīya fire up to the placing of the ghee.
On the southern [altar], he performs [the rites] beginning with the wooden sword as in the Varuṇapraghāsa rites.

sanskrit_iast: śvabhraṃ khātvā kharam apareṇa carmāvadhāya parisrutam āsicya kārotaram avadadhāti kārotarād vā carmaṇi mantraliṅgāt pūtām ādātte siñcanti pariṣiñcanti \\ iti //
meaning: श्वभ्रं खात्वा खरम् अपरेण चर्मावधाय परिस्रुतम् आसिच्य कारोतरम् अवदधाति कारोतराद् वा चर्मणि मन्त्रलिङ्गात् पूताम् आदात्ते सिञ्चन्ति परिषिञ्चन्ति \\ इति //
text_mt: Having dug a pit west of the mound, placed a hide [in it], and poured the liquor (parisrut), he inserts a filter-vessel; or, from the filter-vessel into the hide, according to the indication of the mantra, he takes the purified [liquor] with: 'They pour, they sprinkle around...'

sanskrit_iast: sate punāti go'śvavālavālena punāti te parisrutam iti //
meaning: सते पुनाति गोऽश्ववालवालेन पुनाति ते परिस्रुतम् इति //
text_mt: In a vessel, he strains [it] through a strainer of cow's hair and horse's hair, with: 'He purifies thy parisrut...'
[He uses the mantra] 'Purified by Vāyu...' in the case of one through whom soma has passed out [undigested].

sanskrit_iast: uttarasyāṃ payo vaitase 'jāvilomapavitreṇa brahma kṣatram iti //
meaning: उत्तरस्यां पयो वैतसे ऽजाविलोमपवित्रेण ब्रह्म क्षत्रम् इति //
text_mt: On the northern [altar], [he strains] milk into a cane vessel with a strainer of goat's and sheep's wool, with: 'The spiritual power and the royal power...'
The Brahman's following mantra is: 'O Adhvaryu, with the stones...'
He draws the cups of milk with: 'Surely indeed...'
And he scatters powders of wheat and kuvala jujube, with: 'Thou art splendor...'

sanskrit_iast: sārasvatam audumbareṇopavākabadaracūrṇāni ca vīryam asi \\ iti //
meaning: सारस्वतम् औदुम्बरेणोपवाकबदरचूर्णानि च वीर्यम् असि \\ इति //
text_mt: [He draws] the cup for Sarasvatī with [a cup] of udumbara wood, and [scatters powders] of upavāka and badara jujube, with: 'Thou art virility...'
[He draws] the cup for Indra with [a cup] of nyagrodha wood.
And [he scatters] powders of barley and karkandhu jujube, with: 'Thou art strength...'

sanskrit_iast: sthālībhiḥ saurān nānā hi vām iti vyatyāsam //
meaning: स्थालीभिः सौरान् नाना हि वाम् इति व्यत्यासम् //
text_mt: With the earthen pots, [he draws] the cups of surā alternately, with: 'Distinctly indeed for you both...'

sanskrit_iast: surāgrahāñ chrīṇāti \\ ojo 'si \\ iti vṛkavyāghrasim̐halomabhiḥ pratimantraṃ miśraiḥ //
meaning: सुराग्रहाञ् छ्रीणाति \\ ओजो ऽसि \\ इति वृकव्याघ्रसिम्̐हलोमभिः प्रतिमन्त्रं मिश्रैः //
text_mt: He blends the cups of surā, with: 'Thou art vigor...', with the hairs of a wolf, a tiger, and a lion mixed, mantra by mantra.

sanskrit_iast: somo rājā \\ ity anuvākena grahānupatiṣṭhate yugapat //
meaning: सोमो राजा \\ इत्य् अनुवाकेन ग्रहानुपतिष्ठते युगपत् //
text_mt: He attends upon the cups simultaneously with the section beginning 'King Soma...'
Or [he attends upon] the cups of milk with four [verses] and the cups of surā with the remainder.

sanskrit_iast: dīkṣāvat pāvayato 'ntaḥpātye śyenapattrābhyām \\ yā yvāghram iti //
meaning: दीक्षावत् पावयतो ऽन्तःपात्ये श्येनपत्त्राभ्याम् \\ या य्वाघ्रम् इति //
text_mt: Like the consecration, they purify [the sacrificer] at the antaḥpātya-peg with two falcon feathers, with: 'Which tiger...'
He makes [the sacrificer] look at the fire with: 'What he ground...'
The touching of the milk cups is with: 'You are united...'
[The touching] of the surā cups is with: 'You are separated...'

sanskrit_iast: sārasvato meṣa aindra ṛṣabho madhye yūpo dakṣiṇottarāv aindravāyodhasayoḥ //
meaning: सारस्वतो मेष ऐन्द्र ऋषभो मध्ये यूपो दक्षिणोत्तराव् ऐन्द्रवायोधसयोः //
text_mt: The ram for Sarasvatī, the bull for Indra; the sacrificial post is in the middle; the south and north [animals] are for Indra and the Aśvins [respectively].

sanskrit_iast: vapāmārjanānte grahān ādāya pūrvavad anuvācanam \\ surāsomebhyo 'nubrūhi \\ iti //
meaning: वपामार्जनान्ते ग्रहान् आदाय पूर्ववद् अनुवाचनम् \\ सुरासोमेभ्यो ऽनुब्रूहि \\ इति //
text_mt: At the end of wiping the omentum, having taken the cups, the recitation is summoned as before, with: 'Recite for the surā-somas.'

sanskrit_iast: pālāśaiḥ saurān na mṛnmayam āhutim ānaśa iti śruter yas te \\ iti //
meaning: पालाशैः सौरान् न मृन्मयम् आहुतिम् आनश इति श्रुतेर् यस् ते \\ इति //
text_mt: [He offers] the surā cups using palāśa cups, because of the Vedic text 'an earthen vessel does not reach the oblation', with: 'That which to thee...'

sanskrit_iast: adhvaryuḥ pratiprasthātāgnīd yam aśvinā \\ ity āśvinaṃ bhakṣayanti dvirdvir āvartam //
meaning: अध्वर्युः प्रतिप्रस्थाताग्नीद् यम् अश्विना \\ इत्य् आश्विनं भक्षयन्ति द्विर्द्विर् आवर्तम् //
text_mt: The Adhvaryu, the Pratiprasthātṛ, and the Agnīdh consume the cup for the Aśvins, repeating [the consumption] twice each, with: 'Which, O Aśvins...'
The Hotṛ, the Brahman, and the Maitrāvaruṇa consume the cup for Sarasvatī in the same manner as the Aśvins' [cup].
He pours whatever remnant there is of the earlier into the later [cup].

sanskrit_iast: yad atra \\ iti saurān bhakṣayanti yathābhakṣitaṃ prācīnāvītino dakṣiṇataḥ //
meaning: यद् अत्र \\ इति सौरान् भक्षयन्ति यथाभक्षितं प्राचीनावीतिनो दक्षिणतः //
text_mt: With [the mantra] "What here...", wearing their sacred thread over the right shoulder, to the south, they consume the liquor cups according to how they were consumed.
Or a hired man, one of a Vaiśya or a Rājanya [consumes it].

sanskrit_iast: aṅgāreṣu vā bahiṣparidhi dakṣiṇato juhoty āśvinam uttare madhyame sārasvatam aindraṃ dakṣiṇe pitṛbhyas \\ iti pratimantram //
meaning: अङ्गारेषु वा बहिष्परिधि दक्षिणतो जुहोत्य् आश्विनम् उत्तरे मध्यमे सारस्वतम् ऐन्द्रं दक्षिणे पितृभ्यस् \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: Or on the burning coals outside the enclosing sticks, to the south, he offers: the cup for the Aśvins on the northern [coal], the cup for Sarasvatī on the middle [one], the cup for Indra on the southern [one], each with its respective mantra ending with "to the fathers".
With "The fathers have eaten...", he pours around [the coals] with the washing-water.
He mutters, "Fathers, be purified!"

sanskrit_iast: kumbhīm āsajya kumbhavachatavitṛṇṇāṃ vālapavitrahiraṇyāny antardhāya navarcaṃ vācayati punantu mā \\ iti //
meaning: कुम्भीम् आसज्य कुम्भवछतवितृण्णां वालपवित्रहिरण्यान्य् अन्तर्धाय नवर्चं वाचयति पुनन्तु मा \\ इति //
text_mt: Having hung up a jar perforated with a hundred holes like a pitcher, and having placed between [them] a hair filter and gold [pieces], he makes [him] recite the nine verses beginning "May they purify me..."
[The oblations] belong to the fathers accompanied by Soma, sitting on the sacrificial grass, and consumed by Agni.
If he is one through whom Soma has over-flowed, [the procedure is] as before.
With "Those who are equal...", the sacrificer offers.
And on the northern [fire], wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder, with the next [verse].

sanskrit_iast: anvārabdheṣu payo juhoti dve sṛtī iti //
meaning: अन्वारब्धेषु पयो जुहोति द्वे सृती इति //
text_mt: While [the priests] touch him from behind, he offers milk with "Two paths..."

sanskrit_iast: śeṣaṃ yajamāno bhakṣayati \\ idam̐ havir iti //
meaning: शेषं यजमानो भक्षयति \\ इदम्̐ हविर् इति //
text_mt: The sacrificer consumes the remainder with "This offering..."
Together with his wife, having placed gold between, they purify themselves at the Cātvāla pit.

sanskrit_iast: paśupuroḍāśān nirvapaty aindram̐ sāvitraṃ vāruṇaṃ daśakapālam //
meaning: पशुपुरोडाशान् निर्वपत्य् ऐन्द्रम्̐ सावित्रं वारुणं दशकपालम् //
text_mt: He parcels out the animal cake offerings: one for Indra, one for Savitṛ, and one on ten potsherds for Varuṇa.
And an offering on one potsherd for the concluding bath.

sanskrit_iast: āsādyainān ājyabhāgau yajaty atra sviṣṭakṛdvanaspatyoḥ praiṣadarśanāt //
meaning: आसाद्यैनान् आज्यभागौ यजत्य् अत्र स्विष्टकृद्वनस्पत्योः प्रैषदर्शनात् //
text_mt: Having set these down, he offers the two butter portions here, because the call for the Sviṣṭakṛt and the Vanaspati is seen [here].
Or as previously stated, because the mantras are not prescribed.

sanskrit_iast: trayastrim̐śataṃ dakṣiṇā dadāty anuśiśuṃ ca vaḍabadhenum //
meaning: त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शतं दक्षिणा ददात्य् अनुशिशुं च वडबधेनुम् //
text_mt: He gives thirty-three [cows] as sacrificial gifts, and a mare with a foal.
The rules of the set of eleven victims apply to the groups of victims.

sanskrit_iast: śamitranuśāsanaprabhṛti vanaspatyantaṃ kṛtvā somāsandīvad āsandīṃ jānumātrapādīṃ vedyor nidadhāti kṣatrasya yonir iti //
meaning: शमित्रनुशासनप्रभृति वनस्पत्यन्तं कृत्वा सोमासन्दीवद् आसन्दीं जानुमात्रपादीं वेद्योर् निदधाति क्षत्रस्य योनिर् इति //
text_mt: Having performed [the rites] from the instruction to the slaughterer up to the Vanaspati offering, he places a chair with legs knee-high, like the Soma chair, between the two altars, with "The womb of the nobility..."

sanskrit_iast: kṛṣṇājinam asyām āstṛṇāti mā tvā \\ iti //
meaning: कृष्णाजिनम् अस्याम् आस्तृणाति मा त्वा \\ इति //
text_mt: On this he spreads a black antelope skin with "May not thee..."
On it the sacrificer sits down with "He has sat down..."

sanskrit_iast: pādayo rukmā upāsyati rājatam̐ savye mṛtyor iti //
meaning: पादयो रुक्मा उपास्यति राजतम्̐ सव्ये मृत्योर् इति //
text_mt: He throws down ornaments at [his] feet: a silver one at the left, with "From death..."
Some [say] a gold one on the head, with "Shine..."

sanskrit_iast: khurair vasāgrahān dvātrim̐śataṃ juhoti sīsena \\ iti pratyṛcam //
meaning: खुरैर् वसाग्रहान् द्वात्रिम्̐शतं जुहोति सीसेन \\ इति प्रत्यृचम् //
text_mt: With the hooves he offers thirty-two fat portions with "With lead...", verse by verse.
Having offered [them] two by two, he places the remainders in a shallow dish.

sanskrit_iast: sarvasurabhyunmṛditam̐ śeṣair abhiṣiñcaty ā mukhād avasrāvayan pratidiśam̐ sarvatra sāvitram aśvinoḥ \ sarasvatyai \\ indrasya \\ iti pratimantram //
meaning: सर्वसुरभ्युन्मृदितम्̐ शेषैर् अभिषिञ्चत्य् आ मुखाद् अवस्रावयन् प्रतिदिशम्̐ सर्वत्र सावित्रम् अश्विनोः \ सरस्वत्यै \\ इन्द्रस्य \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: He anoints [him], rubbed with all kinds of fragrant substances, with the remainders, making [them] flow down to his face, in each direction, [using] the verse to Savitṛ everywhere, each with its respective mantra: "Of the Aśvins...", "To Sarasvatī...", "Of Indra..."
Some [say], having poured the unguent into the consecration water.
He touches the sacrificer with "Who art thou?"
Being touched, he calls out with "O Suśloka..."

sanskrit_iast: aṅgāni cālabhate yathāliṅgam \\ śiro me \\ iti pratimantram //
meaning: अङ्गानि चालभते यथालिङ्गम् \\ शिरो मे \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: And he touches the limbs according to their characteristics, each with its respective mantra, beginning "My head..."
They lift him up according to the measures, as in the Śatarudriya rite.
He steps down onto the black antelope skin with "In nobility..."

sanskrit_iast: trayastrim̐śaṃ vasāgrahaṃ gṛhṇāti yo bhūtānām iti //
meaning: त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शं वसाग्रहं गृह्णाति यो भूतानाम् इति //
text_mt: He takes the thirty-third fat portion with "He who of beings..."
Some [say] a butter portion with [a cup of] Aśvattha wood.
He sings on the Bṛhatī verse addressed to Indra.

sanskrit_iast: sam̐śravase viśravase satyaśravase śravase \\ iti sarve nidhanamupayanti //
meaning: सम्̐श्रवसे विश्रवसे सत्यश्रवसे श्रवसे \\ इति सर्वे निधनमुपयन्ति //
text_mt: All join in the finale with "For renown, for wide renown, for true renown, for renown!"

sanskrit_iast: saṃjityai vijityai satyajityai jityai \\ iti kṣatriyasya //
meaning: संजित्यै विजित्यै सत्यजित्यै जित्यै \\ इति क्षत्रियस्य //
text_mt: [The finale] for a Kṣatriya is: "For conquest, for complete conquest, for true conquest, for conquest!"

sanskrit_iast: sampuṣṭyai vipuṣṭyai satyapuṣṭyai puṣṭyai \\ iti vaiśyasya //
meaning: सम्पुष्ट्यै विपुष्ट्यै सत्यपुष्ट्यै पुष्ट्यै \\ इति वैश्यस्य //
text_mt: [The finale] for a Vaiśya is: "For prosperity, for abundant prosperity, for true prosperity, for prosperity!"
Or as traditionally handed down for all.
With "Three gods...", he offers at the end of the recitation.

sanskrit_iast: śeṣam ṛtvijaḥ prāṇabhakṣaṃ bhakṣayanti prāṇapā me \\ iti //
meaning: शेषम् ऋत्विजः प्राणभक्षं भक्षयन्ति प्राणपा मे \\ इति //
text_mt: The officiating priests consume the remainder by inhaling, with "Protector of breath..."
The sacrificer consumes it directly with "The hairs are the effort..."

sanskrit_iast: sviṣṭakṛtprabhṛty ā barhirhomāt kṛtvā parisrutkṣīraliptāny ādāyāvabhṛthavad gamanam //
meaning: स्विष्टकृत्प्रभृत्य् आ बर्हिर्होमात् कृत्वा परिस्रुत्क्षीरलिप्तान्य् आदायावभृथवद् गमनम् //
text_mt: Having performed [the rites] from the Sviṣṭakṛt oblation up to the offering of sacrificial grass, taking the [vessels] smeared with liquor and milk, the departure [takes place] as in the concluding bath.
Having performed up to the addressing of the spit, [the procedure is that] of the concluding bath rite, beginning with standing in the water.
He sets the jar of māsara floating with "What the gods..."

sanskrit_iast: sumitriyā nas \\ ity apo 'ñjalinādāya durmitriyās \\ iti dveṣyaṃ pariṣiñcati dvau vikramā udaṅ gatvā //
meaning: सुमित्रिया नस् \\ इत्य् अपो ऽञ्जलिनादाय दुर्मित्रियास् \\ इति द्वेष्यं परिषिञ्चति द्वौ विक्रमा उदङ् गत्वा //
text_mt: Taking water in his cupped hands with "Friendly to us...", having walked two steps northward, he pours it around the hated enemy with "Unfriendly..."

sanskrit_iast: avabhṛthavat snātvā vāso 'pāsanam \\ drupadād iva \\ iti //
meaning: अवभृथवत् स्नात्वा वासो ऽपासनम् \\ द्रुपदाद् इव \\ इति //
text_mt: Having bathed as in the concluding bath, the casting off of the garment is done with "As if from a wooden post..."
The stepping out and the return are as in the soma [sacrifice].
He attends upon the Āhavanīya fire with "The waters today..."

sanskrit_iast: edho 'si \\ iti samidham ādāyāhavanīye 'bhyādadhāti samid asi \\ iti //
meaning: एधो ऽसि \\ इति समिधम् आदायाहवनीये ऽभ्यादधाति समिद् असि \\ इति //
text_mt: Taking a kindling stick with "Thou art kindling...", he places it on the Āhavanīya fire with "Thou art a kindling stick..."
And he offers with "He turns together..."
Having broken up the camp, there is a curd offering to Mitra and Varuṇa.
At its conclusion, there is an animal sacrifice to Indra Vayodhas.
In the Sautrāmaṇī, the iṣṭis and animal sacrifices have distinct common procedures because of the difference of time.
There are seventeen kindling verses.
The two portions of clarified butter are the Vṛtra-slaying [verses].
Or they contain the word vṛdhant in the animal sacrifices, because they are modifications of the sāṃnāyya.
The two accompanying offerings are Virāj verses, because there is no specific instruction.
For Vasiṣṭhas and Śunakas, the Āprī hymn has Nārāśaṃsa.
The summonses for fore-offerings and after-offerings for the first and last [animal sacrifices] are those of the archetype rite.
Some say they are dedicated to Indra for the first, and dedicated to Vayodhas for the last.
‘Kindled is Indra...’ are the Āprī verses of the first.

sanskrit_iast: yājyānuvākyāś ca vapāpuroḍāśapaśūnām āyātv indras \\ iti //
meaning: याज्यानुवाक्याश् च वपापुरोडाशपशूनाम् आयात्व् इन्द्रस् \\ इति //
text_mt: And the offering and introductory verses for the omenta, cake-offerings, and animals begin with: ‘May Indra come...’

sanskrit_iast: hotā yakṣat samidhāgnim iti prayājapraiṣās tripaśoḥ //
meaning: होता यक्षत् समिधाग्निम् इति प्रयाजप्रैषास् त्रिपशोः //
text_mt: ‘May the Hotṛ sacrifice to Agni with fuel...’ are the summonses for the fore-offerings of the three-animal sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast: āpriyaś ca samiddho agnir aśvinā \\ iti //
meaning: आप्रियश् च समिद्धो अग्निर् अश्विना \\ इति //
text_mt: And the Āprī verses begin with: ‘Agni, being kindled, [the two Aśvins]...’

sanskrit_iast: aśvinā havir iti tisro vapānāṃ yājyānuvākyāḥ //
meaning: अश्विना हविर् इति तिस्रो वपानां याज्यानुवाक्याः //
text_mt: ‘O Aśvins, the offering...’ are the three offering and introductory verses for the omenta.

sanskrit_iast: prathamām anūcya dvitīyā yājyā dvitīyām anūcya tṛtīyā yājyā tṛtīyām anūcya prathamā yājyā //
meaning: प्रथमाम् अनूच्य द्वितीया याज्या द्वितीयाम् अनूच्य तृतीया याज्या तृतीयाम् अनूच्य प्रथमा याज्या //
text_mt: Having recited the first as introductory, the second is the offering verse; having recited the second as introductory, the third is the offering verse; having recited the third as introductory, the first is the offering verse.
‘He who to Indra...’ [are the verses] for the cakes, as before.
And ‘O Aśvins, with cows...’ [are the verses] for the sacrificial portions.

sanskrit_iast: grahāṇām \\ yuvam̐ surāmam \\ putram iva \\ iti //
meaning: ग्रहाणाम् \\ युवम्̐ सुरामम् \\ पुत्रम् इव \\ इति //
text_mt: For the cups, ‘You two [the liquor]...’ and ‘Like a son...’ [are the verses].

sanskrit_iast: paśusviṣṭakṛtas \\ yasminn aśvāsas \\ ahāvy agne \\ iti //
meaning: पशुस्विष्टकृतस् \\ यस्मिन्न् अश्वासस् \\ अहाव्य् अग्ने \\ इति //
text_mt: For the animal Sviṣṭakṛt, ‘In whom horses...’ and ‘It has been offered, O Agni...’ [are the verses].

sanskrit_iast: hotā yakṣad aśvinau \\ iti trayo vapānāṃ praiṣā yathāliṅgam //
meaning: होता यक्षद् अश्विनौ \\ इति त्रयो वपानां प्रैषा यथालिङ्गम् //
text_mt: ‘May the Hotṛ sacrifice to the two Aśvins...’ are the three summonses for the omenta, according to their characteristic marks.
The subsequent ones are for the sacrificial portions, according to their characteristic marks.
The last two are for Vanaspati and Sviṣṭakṛt.

sanskrit_iast: pratigariṣyaty upaviṣṭe \\ adhvaryo śom̐sāva \\ ity āhūya //
meaning: प्रतिगरिष्यत्य् उपविष्टे \\ अध्वर्यो शोम्̐साव \\ इत्य् आहूय //
text_mt: When [the priest] who is to respond has sat down, having addressed him with: ‘O Adhvaryu, let us two recite!’;
he recites the section: ‘O Aśvins, with brilliance...’

sanskrit_iast: uttamām̐ śiṣṭvā prāṅ navamyā daśamyā vā trayā devās \\ iti //
meaning: उत्तमाम्̐ शिष्ट्वा प्राङ् नवम्या दशम्या वा त्रया देवास् \\ इति //
text_mt: leaving the last verse, before the ninth or tenth [verse he recites]: ‘Three gods...’
In the final syllable, there is elision from the vowel onward during the Praṇava.
Some say it ends with the Praṇava on that [syllable].

sanskrit_iast: aśvinā tejasā \\ aśvinā pibatām iti yājyānuvākye saśastrasya //
meaning: अश्विना तेजसा \\ अश्विना पिबताम् इति याज्यानुवाक्ये सशस्त्रस्य //
text_mt: ‘O Aśvins, with brilliance...’ and ‘O Aśvins, drink...’ are the offering and introductory verses for the [offering] accompanied by a recitation.
Having combined the summons for the introductory recitation [and the offering summons], the summonses for the after-offerings are: ‘The divine sacrificial grass...’
‘Agni today...’ is the summons for the Sūktavāka.
From the Sūktavāka onward, before the Avabhṛtha offering, it follows the archetype rite.

sanskrit_iast: imaṃ me \ tat tvā \\ ity ekakapālasya //
meaning: इमं मे \ तत् त्वा \\ इत्य् एककपालस्य //
text_mt: ‘This my [call]...’ and ‘That of you...’ are for the single-potsherd cake.

sanskrit_iast: agnīvaruṇayos tvaṃ naḥ \ sa tvam iti //
meaning: अग्नीवरुणयोस् त्वं नः \ स त्वम् इति //
text_mt: For Agni and Varuṇa, ‘You to us...’ and ‘He, you...’ [are the verses].

sanskrit_iast: ādityasya sutrāmāṇam \\ mahīm ū ṣu mātaram iti //
meaning: आदित्यस्य सुत्रामाणम् \\ महीम् ऊ षु मातरम् इति //
text_mt: For Āditya, ‘The good protector...’ and ‘The great mother indeed...’ [are the verses].

sanskrit_iast: ā naḥ \ pra bāhavā \\ iti payasyāyāḥ //
meaning: आ नः \ प्र बाहवा \\ इति पयस्यायाः //
text_mt: ‘To us...’ and ‘Forth arms...’ are for the curdled milk.
For the Vājina offering, ‘May it be well for us...’ and ‘In every battle...’ [are the verses].
The Āprī verses for Vayodhas are: ‘Agni, being kindled, with fuel...’

sanskrit_iast: yājyānuvākyāś ca vapāpuroḍāśapaśūnām \\ vasantena ṛtunā \\ iti //
meaning: याज्यानुवाक्याश् च वपापुरोडाशपशूनाम् \\ वसन्तेन ऋतुना \\ इति //
text_mt: And the offering and introductory verses for the omenta, cake-offerings, and animals are: ‘With the spring season...’
The Aśvamedha is a royal sacrifice for one who desires all.
On the eighth or ninth [lunar day] of the bright half of Phālguna [it begins].

sanskrit_iast: brahmaudanaṃ pacati caturṇāṃ pātrāṇām añjaliprasṛtānāṃ ca //
meaning: ब्रह्मौदनं पचति चतुर्णां पात्राणाम् अञ्जलिप्रसृतानां च //
text_mt: He cooks the Brahmā-rice of four vessels, and scooped with cupped hands.
Having anointed it, he presents it to the four principal officiating priests.

sanskrit_iast: tebhyaś catvāri sahasrāṇi dadāti śatamānāṃś ca tāvataḥ //
meaning: तेभ्यश् चत्वारि सहस्राणि ददाति शतमानांश् च तावतः //
text_mt: To them he gives four thousand [cows] and as many gold pieces.

sanskrit_iast: aktvājyaśeṣeṇa raśanāṃ dvādaśāratniṃ trayodaśāratniṃ vā nidadhāti //
meaning: अक्त्वाज्यशेषेण रशनां द्वादशारत्निं त्रयोदशारत्निं वा निदधाति //
text_mt: Having anointed the halter of twelve cubits or thirteen cubits with the remainder of clarified butter, he deposits it.

meaning: निष्कं प्रतिमुञ्चन् वाचयति तेजो ऽसि \\ इति //
text_mt: Fastening a gold ornament [upon the sacrificer], he causes him to recite: ‘You are brilliance...’
The restraint of speech lasts until the granting of boons.

sanskrit_iast: patnyaś cāyanty alaṅkṛtā niṣkiṇyo mahiṣī vāvātā parivṛktā pālāgalī sānucaryaḥ śatenásatena //
meaning: पत्न्यश् चायन्त्य् अलङ्कृता निष्किण्यो महिषी वावाता परिवृक्ता पालागली सानुचर्यः शतेन्áसतेन //
text_mt: And the wives arrive, adorned and wearing golden ornaments: the chief queen (mahiṣī), the favorite wife (vāvātā), the discarded wife (parivṛktā), and the lowly wife (pālāgalī), accompanied by female attendants, a hundred for each.
Daughters of kings [are the attendants] of the first.
[Daughters] of nobles [are the attendants] of the second.
[Daughters] of charioteers and village headmen [are the attendants] of the third.
[Daughters] of chamberlains and charioteers [are the attendants] of the fourth.

sanskrit_iast: agnyādheyavat praviśya hute 'gnihotre 'pareṇa gārhapatyam udakśirāḥ saṃviśati //
meaning: अग्न्याधेयवत् प्रविश्य हुते ऽग्निहोत्रे ऽपरेण गार्हपत्यम् उदक्शिराः संविशति //
text_mt: Having entered as at the establishment of the sacred fires, after the agnihotra has been offered, he lies down to the west of the Gārhapatya fire with his head to the north.
A student of sacred lore (brahmacārin) [lies down] between the thighs of the favorite wife.
When the morning oblation has been offered, at the end of the full-spoon oblation, the granting of a boon [is given] to the Brahman priest.
And to the Adhvaryu priest, the golden ornament fastened [around his neck].
A sacrificial cake is [offered] to Agni Pathikṛt.
The sacrificial gift is a piece of gold weighing one hundred mānas.
Elsewhere too, when gold is measured [it is of this weight].
He dispenses a mess of cooked grain for Pūṣan.

sanskrit_iast: devasya tvā \\ iti raśanām ādāya brahmann aśvaṃ bhantsyāmi \\ ity āha //
meaning: देवस्य त्वा \\ इति रशनाम् आदाय ब्रह्मन्न् अश्वं भन्त्स्यामि \\ इत्य् आह //
text_mt: Taking the halter with 'At the instigation of the divine Savitṛ...', he says: 'O Brahman priest, I shall bind the horse.'

sanskrit_iast: taṃ badhāna \\ iti brahmānujñātas \\ abhidhā asi \\ iti badhnāty aśvam //
meaning: तं बधान \\ इति ब्रह्मानुज्ञातस् \\ अभिधा असि \\ इति बध्नात्य् अश्वम् //
text_mt: Authorized by the Brahman priest with 'Bind it', he binds the horse with 'Thou art the halter...'
[The horse should be] of three colors, or of all colors.
Black on the fore-body and white on the hind-body.

sanskrit_iast: sthāvarā apo gatvā prajāpataye tvā \\ iti prokṣaty aśvaṃ pratimantram //
meaning: स्थावरा अपो गत्वा प्रजापतये त्वा \\ इति प्रोक्षत्य् अश्वं प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: Having gone to standing waters, he sprinkles the horse with each mantra: 'Thee for Prajāpati...'

sanskrit_iast: āyogavam āha śvānaṃ caturakṣam abhimanyasva \\ iti //
meaning: आयोगवम् आह श्वानं चतुरक्षम् अभिमन्यस्व \\ इति //
text_mt: He says to an Āyogava: 'Curse the four-eyed dog!'
He kills it with a pestle of sidhraka wood.
He makes [him] recite: 'He who against the steed...'

meaning: वेतसकटेनाधो ऽश्वं प्लावयति परो मर्तस् \\ इति //
text_mt: He makes [the dog] float under the horse on a mat of reeds, with: 'Away is the mortal...'

sanskrit_iast: agnisamīpam ānīya \\ agnaye svāhā \\ iti juhoty anuvākena pratimantram //
meaning: अग्निसमीपम् आनीय \\ अग्नये स्वाहा \\ इति जुहोत्य् अनुवाकेन प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: Having brought [the horse] near the fire, he offers [oblations] with the section 'To Agni svāhā...', mantra by mantra.
Or until the horse's neighing ceases.

sanskrit_iast: dvādaśakapālān nirvapati bhinnatantrāñ chatamānadakṣiṇān madhyamasya rājataḥ savitre prasavitre savitra āsavitre savitre satyaprasavāya \\ iti //
meaning: द्वादशकपालान् निर्वपति भिन्नतन्त्राञ् छतमानदक्षिणान् मध्यमस्य राजतः सवित्रे प्रसवित्रे सवित्र आसवित्रे सवित्रे सत्यप्रसवाय \\ इति //
text_mt: He dispenses [offerings of cakes] on twelve potsherds, having distinct common procedures, with a hundred mānas [of gold] as sacrificial gift, [and] for the middle one silver, to Savitṛ the stimulator, to Savitṛ the impeller, to Savitṛ of true instigation.

sanskrit_iast: prayājeṣu dakṣiṇato brāhmaṇo yajamānasya yajñadānayuktāḥ svayaṃkrtās tisro gāthā gāyaty uttaramandrāyām //
meaning: प्रयाजेषु दक्षिणतो ब्राह्मणो यजमानस्य यज्ञदानयुक्ताः स्वयंक्र्तास् तिस्रो गाथा गायत्य् उत्तरमन्द्रायाम् //
text_mt: During the preliminary offerings (prayājas), to the south, a Brāhmaṇa sings in the uttaramandrā note three self-composed verses connected with the sacrificer's sacrifices and gifts.
A noble [sings verses] connected with battles and victories during the dhṛti oblations.

sanskrit_iast: adhvaryuyajamānau dakṣiṇe 'śvakarṇe japatas \\ vibhūr mātrā \\ iti //
meaning: अध्वर्युयजमानौ दक्षिणे ऽश्वकर्णे जपतस् \\ विभूर् मात्रा \\ इति //
text_mt: The Adhvaryu priest and the sacrificer whisper into the right ear of the horse: 'Thou art a broad ruler by thy measure...'
The releasing is performed as in an animal sacrifice, amidst a hundred gelded horses.

sanskrit_iast: devā āśāpālās \\ iti rakṣiṇo 'syādiśatyanucarījñātīyāṃs tāvatastāvataḥ kavaciniṣaṅgikalāpidaṇḍino yathāsaṃkhyam //
meaning: देवा आशापालास् \\ इति रक्षिणो ऽस्यादिशत्यनुचरीज्ञातीयांस् तावतस्तावतः कवचिनिषङ्गिकलापिदण्डिनो यथासंख्यम् //
text_mt: With 'Ye gods who guard the regions...', he assigns its guards, the kinsmen of the female attendants, in equal numbers: wearing armor, bearing quivers, bearing bows, and holding staves, respectively.

meaning: ब्राह्मणो ऽश्वमेधे ऽविद्वान् वृत्तिः स वः //
text_mt: 'A Brāhmaṇa ignorant of the horse-sacrifice is your livelihood.'
And dwelling in the houses of chariot-makers.

sanskrit_iast: abhiṣekyā bhaviṣyata samāpnuvantas \\ ity āha rājaputrān //
meaning: अभिषेक्या भविष्यत समाप्नुवन्तस् \\ इत्य् आह राजपुत्रान् //
text_mt: 'May you who are to be consecrated attain [kingship]!' he says to the royal princes.
To the south of the altar, they sit upon golden seats.
The Adhvaryu priest and the sacrificer [sit] on two bunches of grass.
The Hotṛ priest, the Brahman priest, and the Udgātṛ priest [sit] on cushions.

sanskrit_iast: hotar bhūtāny ācakṣva \ bhūteṣv imaṃ yajamānam adhyūha \\ iti //
meaning: होतर् भूतान्य् आचक्ष्व \ भूतेष्व् इमं यजमानम् अध्यूह \\ इति //
text_mt: 'O Hotṛ priest, narrate the beings; place this sacrificer among the beings!'

sanskrit_iast: havai hotar iti pratigṛṇāti tadante preṣyati vīṇāgaṇagino rājarṣibhir yajamānam̐ saṃgāyata \\ iti //
meaning: हवै होतर् इति प्रतिगृणाति तदन्ते प्रेष्यति वीणागणगिनो राजर्षिभिर् यजमानम्̐ संगायत \\ इति //
text_mt: With 'Yes, O Hotṛ', he responds; at the end of that, he orders the lute-players: 'Sing together of the sacrificer along with the royal sages!'

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇāgnau juhoti hiṅkārāya svāhā \\ iti prakramān //
meaning: दक्षिणाग्नौ जुहोति हिङ्काराय स्वाहा \\ इति प्रक्रमान् //
text_mt: In the Dakṣiṇāgni fire, he offers the steps with 'To the sound hiṅ, svāhā!'

sanskrit_iast: āhavanīye 'stamite catasro dhṛtīr iha rantir iti //
meaning: आहवनीये ऽस्तमिते चतस्रो धृतीर् इह रन्तिर् इति //
text_mt: In the Āhavanīya fire at sunset, [he offers] the four dhṛti oblations with 'Here is delight...'
The lying down with the favorite wife, the offerings to Savitṛ, the singing in the uttaramandrā note, the revolving cycle of tales, and the dhṛti oblations [continue] for a year.
And some [say they last] half a month, a month, three months, or six months.
He gives a hundred [cows] each to the two lute-singers.
The singing together [of the sacrificer] with the royal sages continues up to the preparatory rite (dīkṣaṇīyā).
From the end of the consecration up to the day of preparation (aupavasathya), [the singing is] together with the gods.
At the beginning of [the offering of] the animal [victims], [he sings] with Prajāpati during the soma pressings.
The sacrifice for the horse’s misfortunes consists of pots of boiled rice (caru) at the conclusion of the Sāvitra [oblations].
If it has an incurable or violent disease, [a cake] baked on potsherds of earth dedicated to Agni Vaiśvānara.
Jātūkarṇya says: on potsherds made of clay clods, because of the breakage.

sanskrit_iast: nāśe tantreṇa dyāvāpṛthivyaḥ payo vāyavyam̐ sauryaḥ //
meaning: नाशे तन्त्रेण द्यावापृथिव्यः पयो वायव्यम्̐ सौर्यः //
text_mt: If it disappears, [there are offered] combined into a single procedure: milk dedicated to Dyāvāpṛthivī, [milk] dedicated to Vāyu, and [a caru] dedicated to Sūrya.
he performs taking the halter and the other [rites] connected with the horse for another [horse].

sanskrit_iast: paścālambhanādy ādhvaradīkṣāṇīyāyāḥ kṛtvā catvāry audgrabhaṇāni juhoty ādhvarikāṇi //
meaning: पश्चालम्भनाद्य् आध्वरदीक्षाणीयायाः कृत्वा चत्वार्य् औद्ग्रभणानि जुहोत्य् आध्वरिकाणि //
text_mt: Having performed [the rites] from the post-touching onward belonging to the dīkṣaṇīyā of the soma sacrifice, he offers the four audgrabhaṇa oblations of the soma sacrifice,
and three belonging to the horse sacrifice with [the mantra]: 'To Ka svāhā!'

sanskrit_iast: adhvaradīkṣaṇīyāyāś catvāri trīṇi trīṇi cāśvam adhikāni kṛṣṇājināntam anvaham //
meaning: अध्वरदीक्षणीयायाश् चत्वारि त्रीणि त्रीणि चाश्वम् अधिकानि कृष्णाजिनान्तम् अन्वहम् //
text_mt: he offers day after day up to the black antelope skin [rite] the four [audgrabhaṇa oblations] of the soma sacrifice’s dīkṣaṇīyā and the three additional ones of the horse sacrifice.
He observes the standard observance, because it has not [yet] been observed.
And on the seventh day he distributes [the oblations] belonging to the Fire-altar building.
He performs [the rites] beginning with anointing.
There are six [oblations] belonging to the Fire-altar in place of the four.
The tenth is with [the verse]: 'Of the divine Savitṛ, every...'

sanskrit_iast: kṛṣṇājinādy ā samidādhānāt kṛtvā \\ ā brahman \\ iti japati //
meaning: कृष्णाजिनाद्य् आ समिदाधानात् कृत्वा \\ आ ब्रह्मन् \\ इति जपति //
text_mt: Having performed [the rites] beginning with the black antelope skin up to the placing of fuel sticks, he mutters: 'May there be born in the Brahman...'
There are twelve consecration days and [twelve] Upasad days.
The sacrificial ground should have constant water to the east.

meaning: आद्यो ऽग्निर् द्विगुणस् त्रिगुण एकविम्̐शतिविधो वा //
text_mt: The first Fire-altar is double [the size], threefold, or twenty-one-fold.
There are twenty-one sacrificial posts, like the group of eleven.
There are six each of Bilva, Khadira, and Palāśa.
At each sacrificial post there is an animal victim dedicated to Agni-Soma.
The animal victims of the pressing day form two groups of eleven.

sanskrit_iast: vijayamadhyād dhotuḥ prācī dig dakṣiṇā brahmaṇo 'dhvaryoḥ pratīcy udgātur udīcī //
meaning: विजयमध्याद् धोतुः प्राची दिग् दक्षिणा ब्रह्मणो ऽध्वर्योः प्रतीच्य् उद्गातुर् उदीची //
text_mt: From the center of conquest, the eastern direction [of the realm] belongs to the Hotṛ, the southern to the Brahman, the western to the Adhvaryu, and the northern to the Udgātṛ.
He gives a third each day, excluding the land, the men, and the property of Brāhmaṇas.
At the third pressing, having drawn the Ukthya cup, at the time of the Āgnimāruta śastra he divides it threefold.
Corresponding to those cups are the offering and the consumption.
Having repeatedly drawn the Vasatīvarī waters, having poured them together in each direction, he carries them around.

sanskrit_iast: ājyasaktudhānālājānām ekaikaṃ juhoti prāṇāya svāhā \\ iti pratimantram̐ sarvarātram āvartam //
meaning: आज्यसक्तुधानालाजानाम् एकैकं जुहोति प्राणाय स्वाहा \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम्̐ सर्वरात्रम् आवर्तम् //
text_mt: Throughout the whole night, in rotation, he offers one [portion] each of ghee, parched grain meal, roasted grains, and fried grains with each mantra: 'To Prāṇa svāhā!'
With 'To the dawn [svāhā]' when it dawns.

sanskrit_iast: mahimānau gṛhṇāti sauvarṇena pūrvam \\ hiraṇyagarbhas \\ iti dvitīyam̐ rājatena yaḥ prāṇatas \\ iti //
meaning: महिमानौ गृह्णाति सौवर्णेन पूर्वम् \\ हिरण्यगर्भस् \\ इति द्वितीयम्̐ राजतेन यः प्राणतस् \\ इति //
text_mt: He draws the two Mahimān cups: the first with a golden [vessel] using 'The Golden Embryo...', the second with a silver [vessel] using 'He who is the giver of breath...'
The creeping toward the Bahiṣpavamāna chant takes place while holding on to the horse.
He shows it a mare; it neighs, [and] that is its chant.
With the horse they cause [the ground] of the Āstāva to be stepped upon.
Having dedicated the animals of the set of eleven and the horse and others,
he summons: 'Hotṛ, praise the horse!'
He yokes it with: 'They yoke the tawny [steed]...'
And the other [horses] with: 'They yoke his...'
The horses have golden ornaments.

sanskrit_iast: apo yātvāvagāḍheṣu vācayati yad vātas \\ iti //
meaning: अपो यात्वावगाढेषु वाचयति यद् वातस् \\ इति //
text_mt: Having driven to the water, when they have stepped into it, he makes [the sacrificer] recite: 'What the wind...'

sanskrit_iast: āyāya vimuktam aśvaṃ mahiṣī vāvātā parivṛktājyenābhyañjanti pūrvakāyamadhyāparakāyān yathādeśam \\ vasavas tvā \\ iti pratimantram //
meaning: आयाय विमुक्तम् अश्वं महिषी वावाता परिवृक्ताज्येनाभ्यञ्जन्ति पूर्वकायमध्यापरकायान् यथादेशम् \\ वसवस् त्वा \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: When [the horse] has returned and been unharnessed, the chief queen, the favourite wife, and the discarded wife anoint the horse with ghee—the fore-body, the middle, and the hindquarters respectively according to their places—with the mantras beginning 'May the Vasus [anoint] you', one mantra for each.

sanskrit_iast: abhram̐śyamānān maṇīnt sauvarṇān ekaśatamekaśataṃ kesarāpucheṣv āvayanti bhūr bhuvaḥ svar iti pratimahāvyāhṛti //
meaning: अभ्रम्̐श्यमानान् मणीन्त् सौवर्णान् एकशतमेकशतं केसरापुछेष्व् आवयन्ति भूर् भुवः स्वर् इति प्रतिमहाव्याहृति //
text_mt: They weave one hundred and one gold beads that do not fall off into its mane and tail, with the Great Utterances 'bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ', one for each.
According to some, the female attendants also [weave beads] silently.

sanskrit_iast: aśvāya rātrihutaśeṣaṃ prayachati lājī3ñ chācī3n iti //
meaning: अश्वाय रात्रिहुतशेषं प्रयछति लाजी3ञ् छाची3न् इति //
text_mt: He offers the remnant of the night offering to the horse, with: 'Lājī3n śācī3n...'.
If it does not eat, [there is] casting it into the waters.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmā pṛchati hotāraṃ yūpam abhitaḥ kaḥ svid ekākī \\ iti //
sūryas \\ ity ācaṣṭe //
meaning:
ब्रह्मा पृछति होतारं यूपम् अभितः कः स्विद् एकाकी \\ इति //
सूर्यस् \\ इत्य् आचष्टे //
text_mt: Near the sacrificial post, the Brahman priest asks the Hotṛ priest: 'Who indeed wanders alone?'; he answers: 'The sun'.

sanskrit_iast: hotā brahmāṇam \\ kā svid āsīt \\ iti //
meaning: होता ब्रह्माणम् \\ का स्विद् आसीत् \\ इति //
text_mt: The Hotṛ priest [asks] the Brahman priest: 'What indeed was [the first conception]?'
He performs the churning of fire and the subsequent rites.
To the central post facing the fire he binds the horse, the hornless he-goat, and the wild ox.
The deities of the horse and the others are as prescribed.
[He binds] fifteen [tame animals] each, beginning with the red deer and ending with those sacred to Sūrya, to the other [posts].
[He binds] thirteen [wild animals] each, beginning with the francolin partridges and ending with the spotted ones, between the sacrificial posts.

sanskrit_iast: aśvaprokṣaṇam adbhyas tvā \ vāyuṣ ṭvā \\ iti //
meaning: अश्वप्रोक्षणम् अद्भ्यस् त्वा \ वायुष् ट्वा \\ इति //
text_mt: The sprinkling of the horse is with: 'To the waters, you...', 'May Vāyu [protect] you...'.

sanskrit_iast: upagṛhṇāti \\ apāṃ perur \ agniḥ paśur iti //
meaning: उपगृह्णाति \\ अपां पेरुर् \ अग्निः पशुर् इति //
text_mt: He takes hold [of it] with: 'The drinker of the waters...', 'Agni is the animal...'
They release the francolin partridges and the others after carrying fire around them.
The suffocation of the horse takes place upon a gold cloth and upper garments.

sanskrit_iast: paripaśavye hutvā prāṇāya svāhā \\ iti tisro 'parāḥ //
meaning: परिपशव्ये हुत्वा प्राणाय स्वाहा \\ इति तिस्रो ऽपराः //
text_mt: Having offered the oblations regarding the animals, he offers three subsequent oblations with: 'To the out-breath, svāhā...'

sanskrit_iast: vācayati patnīr nayan namas te \\ ambe \\ iti //
meaning: वाचयति पत्नीर् नयन् नमस् ते \\ अम्बे \\ इति //
text_mt: Leading the wives, he makes them recite: 'Homage to you...', 'O mother...'

sanskrit_iast: aśvaṃ tristriḥ pariyanti pitṛvan madhye gaṇānām \\ priyāṇām \\ nidhīnām iti //
meaning: अश्वं त्रिस्त्रिः परियन्ति पितृवन् मध्ये गणानाम् \\ प्रियाणाम् \\ निधीनाम् इति //
text_mt: They walk around the horse three times each, like the rite for the Fathers, reciting in the middle: 'Of the troops...', 'Of the dear ones...', 'Of the treasures...'

sanskrit_iast: prakṣāliteṣu mahiṣyaśvam upasṃviśati \\ āham ajāni \\ iti //
meaning: प्रक्षालितेषु महिष्यश्वम् उपस्ंविशति \\ आहम् अजानि \\ इति //
text_mt: When they have washed [the horse], the chief queen lies down beside the horse, reciting: 'I will urge...'
He covers [them] with an upper garment, reciting: 'In the heavenly world...'

sanskrit_iast: aśvaśiśnam upasthe kurute vṛṣā vājī \\ iti //
meaning: अश्वशिश्नम् उपस्थे कुरुते वृषा वाजी \\ इति //
text_mt: She places the horse's penis upon her lap, reciting: 'The vigorous seed-pourer...'

meaning: उत् सक्थ्यास् \\ इत्य् अश्वं यजमानो ऽभिमन्त्रयते //
text_mt: With 'Raise the thighs...', the sacrificer addresses the horse.

sanskrit_iast: adhvaryubrahmodgātṛhotṛkṣattāraḥ kumārīpatnībhiḥ saṃvadante yakāsakau \\ iti daśarcasya dvābhyāṃdvābhyām \\ hayehaye 'sau \\ ity āmantryāmantrya //
meaning: अध्वर्युब्रह्मोद्गातृहोतृक्षत्तारः कुमारीपत्नीभिः संवदन्ते यकासकौ \\ इति दशर्चस्य द्वाभ्यांद्वाभ्याम् \\ हयेहये ऽसौ \\ इत्य् आमन्त्र्यामन्त्र्य //
text_mt: The Adhvaryu priest, the Brahman priest, the Udgātṛ priest, the Hotṛ priest, and the carver engage in abusive dialogue with the maiden and the wives with two verses each of the ten-verse hymn, having repeatedly hailed them with: 'Hey, hey, such a one!'

sanskrit_iast: mahiṣīm utthāpya puruṣās \\ dadhikrāvṇas \\ ity āhuḥ //
meaning: महिषीम् उत्थाप्य पुरुषास् \\ दधिक्राव्णस् \\ इत्य् आहुः //
text_mt: Having made the chief queen rise, the men recite: 'Of Dadhikrāvan...'

sanskrit_iast: tisraḥ patnyo 'sipathān kalpayanty aśvasya sūcībhir lauharājatasauvarṇībhir maṇisaṃkhyābhir gāyatrī triṣṭub iti dvābhyāṃdvābhyām //
meaning: तिस्रः पत्न्यो ऽसिपथान् कल्पयन्त्य् अश्वस्य सूचीभिर् लौहराजतसौवर्णीभिर् मणिसंख्याभिर् गायत्री त्रिष्टुब् इति द्वाभ्यांद्वाभ्याम् //
text_mt: The three wives mark the paths for the knife on the horse with copper, silver, and gold needles corresponding in number to the beads, with two verses each: 'The Gāyatrī...', 'The Triṣṭubh...'
Or with silver, gold, and lead [needles], because of the mention in the mantras.

sanskrit_iast: aśvaṃ viśāsty anuvākena kas tvā chyati \\ iti //
meaning: अश्वं विशास्त्य् अनुवाकेन कस् त्वा छ्यति \\ इति //
text_mt: He carves the horse with the section: 'Who cuts you?...'
They take out its fat for the purpose of the omentum.
And they cook its blood.

sanskrit_iast: prājāpatyavapānām uttarataḥ śrapaṇam̐ homo haviṣaś ca //
meaning: प्राजापत्यवपानाम् उत्तरतः श्रपणम्̐ होमो हविषश् च //
text_mt: The cooking and the offering of the omenta and the sacrificial substance for Prajāpati take place on the north.

sanskrit_iast: prāg vapāhomād dhotādhvaryū ca sadasi saṃvadete catasṛbhiḥ kaḥ svid ekākī \\ iti pūrvavat //
meaning: प्राग् वपाहोमाद् धोताध्वर्यू च सदसि संवदेते चतसृभिः कः स्विद् एकाकी \\ इति पूर्ववत् //
text_mt: Before the offering of the omentum, the Hotṛ priest and the Adhvaryu priest engage in dialogue in the Sadas with four verses: 'Who indeed wanders alone?...', as before.
And the Brahman priest and the Udgātṛ priest [converse], with: 'I ask you...'

sanskrit_iast: punaḥ pūrvāv apareṇottaravedim \\ kā svid āsīt \\ iti //
meaning: पुनः पूर्वाव् अपरेणोत्तरवेदिम् \\ का स्विद् आसीत् \\ इति //
text_mt: Again, the former two [converse] west of the high altar, with: 'What indeed was [the first conception]?...'
And the latter two [converse], with: 'How many [parts] of this?...'
The sacrificer [asks] the Adhvaryu priest: 'I ask you...'
The Adhvaryu priest [replies]: 'This altar...'

sanskrit_iast: sarvahutena mahimnā carati yas te 'han \\ iti juhoti //
meaning: सर्वहुतेन महिम्ना चरति यस् ते ऽहन् \\ इति जुहोति //
text_mt: He proceeds with the Mahiman cup offered entirely; he offers it with: 'That which by day...'
[The animals are] a goat, an ox, and a ram, in accordance with the characteristic marks of the names of the animals.
Because the prescriptive word expresses a quality.
According to some, immediately following are twenty-one offerings to the deities of the Four-Month sacrifices, excluding those to the Fathers, the Tryambaka rites, and the repetitions.
According to some, [they are dedicated] to Indrāgnī, the Viśvedevas, and Ka.

sanskrit_iast: vapānte dvitīyena pūrvavat \\ yas te rātrau \\ iti juhoti //
meaning: वपान्ते द्वितीयेन पूर्ववत् \\ यस् ते रात्रौ \\ इति जुहोति //
text_mt: At the end of the omentum [offering], he offers with the second [Mahiman cup] as before, with: 'That which by night...'
Having performed [the rites] from the gliding forth up to the setting down of the animal;
he portions out the blood in the windpipe of the wild ox and the hoof of the horse into an iron pot.
[The portions] of the animals for Prajāpati [are placed] on reed branches.

sanskrit_iast: sviṣṭakṛdvanaspatyantare śūlyam̐ hutvā devatāśvāṅgebhyo juhoti \\ amuṣmai svāhā \\ iti pratidevatam̐ śādaprabhṛtitvagantebhyaḥ //
meaning: स्विष्टकृद्वनस्पत्यन्तरे शूल्यम्̐ हुत्वा देवताश्वाङ्गेभ्यो जुहोति \\ अमुष्मै स्वाहा \\ इति प्रतिदेवतम्̐ शादप्रभृतित्वगन्तेभ्यः //
text_mt: Between the Sviṣṭakṛt and the Vanaspati offerings, having offered the roasted flesh on a spit, he makes oblations to the deities of the horse's limbs with, "To so-and-so, svāhā," for each deity, beginning with the grass and ending with the skin.

sanskrit_iast: mā no mitras \\ iti ca pratyṛcam anuvākābhyām //
meaning: मा नो मित्रस् \\ इति च प्रत्यृचम् अनुवाकाभ्याम् //
text_mt: And verse by verse with the two anuvākas: "Let not Mitra..."
[He offers] the last [verse], addressed to Dyāvāpṛthivī.

sanskrit_iast: sviṣṭakṛdante \\ agnibhyaḥ sviṣṭakṛdbhyaḥ svāhā \\ iti lohitaṃ juhoti yathāvattam //
meaning: स्विष्टकृदन्ते \\ अग्निभ्यः स्विष्टकृद्भ्यः स्वाहा \\ इति लोहितं जुहोति यथावत्तम् //
text_mt: At the conclusion of the Sviṣṭakṛt offering, he offers the blood as apportioned, with: "To the Sviṣṭakṛt Agnis, svāhā."
Or [he offers it] with a horse's hoof at the conclusion of the after-offerings.
With an iron vessel at the conclusion of the Patnīsaṃyājas.

sanskrit_iast: imā nu kam iti ca dvipadāḥ //
meaning: इमा नु कम् इति च द्विपदाः //
text_mt: And the two-verse lines: "Now indeed..."

sanskrit_iast: sarvastomo jyotir gaur āyur abhijid viśvajin mahāvratam aptoryāmo vā //
meaning: सर्वस्तोमो ज्योतिर् गौर् आयुर् अभिजिद् विश्वजिन् महाव्रतम् अप्तोर्यामो वा //
text_mt: Or [it is] a Sarvastoma, a Jyotis, a Gauḥ, an Āyus, an Abhijit, a Viśvajit, a Mahāvrata, or an Aptoryāma.
In the Aptoryāma, the night round is subsequent to the Tiro'hnya cups.
And the two Prājāpatya [victims are bound] to the Agniṣṭha post.

sanskrit_iast: avabhṛtheṣṭyante 'psu magnasya piṅgalakhalativiklidhaśuklasya mūrdhani juhoti jumbakāya svāhā \\ iti //
meaning: अवभृथेष्ट्यन्ते ऽप्सु मग्नस्य पिङ्गलखलतिविक्लिधशुक्लस्य मूर्धनि जुहोति जुम्बकाय स्वाहा \\ इति //
text_mt: At the end of the purificatory bath offering, he offers upon the head of a brown-eyed, bald, white-spotted man immersed in water, with: "To Jumbaka, svāhā."

meaning: उत्क्रान्ते यजमाने पापकृतो ऽभ्यवयन्त्य् अचरित्वा व्रतानि //
text_mt: When the sacrificer has stepped out, evil-doers descend [into the water] without having observed the observances.
They are called purified by the Aśvamedha.
[The procedure] of the first two ends with the striking together of the water jars.
Because in the remaining rites there is an absence of consecration observances.
There are twenty-one Anūbandhyā cows.
At the end of the Udavasānīyā offering, he gives the wives together with their female attendants, according to the agreement.
And the maiden and the Pālāgalī to the Adhvaryu.
Or only the female attendants, because the others have eligibility for the result [of the rite].
For twelve days there is a sacrificial cake for Agni.

sanskrit_iast: pratyṛtu paśūn ālabhate ṣaṭṣaḍ vasantādy āgneyān aindrān pārjanyān mārutān vā maitrāvaruṇān aindravaiṣṇavān aindrābārhaspatyān //
meaning: प्रत्यृतु पशून् आलभते षट्षड् वसन्ताद्य् आग्नेयान् ऐन्द्रान् पार्जन्यान् मारुतान् वा मैत्रावरुणान् ऐन्द्रवैष्णवान् ऐन्द्राबार्हस्पत्यान् //
text_mt: Season by season he immolates victims, six each, beginning in spring: [six] for Agni, [six] for Indra, [six] for Parjanya, or [six] for the Maruts, [six] for Mitrā-Varuṇā, [six] for Indrā-Viṣṇū, and [six] for Indrā-Bṛhaspatī.
The Puruṣamedha has twenty-three consecration days, for one who desires pre-eminence.
Between two Agniṣṭomas there is an Atirātra flanked by Ukthyas.
There is a set of eleven sacrificial posts.

sanskrit_iast: paśūn upākariṣyann atirātre deva savitar iti pratyṛcaṃ tisro juhoti //
meaning: पशून् उपाकरिष्यन्न् अतिरात्रे देव सवितर् इति प्रत्यृचं तिस्रो जुहोति //
text_mt: When about to bring up the victims on the Atirātra day, he offers three oblations verse by verse with: "God Savitṛ..."
Having brought up the eleven victims and the Brāhmaṇa and other human victims,
at the time of tying them, [he ties] the first forty-eight to the Agniṣṭha post;
eleven to each of the others;

sanskrit_iast: niyuktān brahmābhiṣṭauti hotṛvad anuvākena sahasraśīrṣā \\ iti //
meaning: नियुक्तान् ब्रह्माभिष्टौति होतृवद् अनुवाकेन सहस्रशीर्षा \\ इति //
text_mt: The Brahman priest praises the tied victims like the Hotṛ, with the anuvāka: "The thousand-headed..."
They release the Brāhmaṇa and other human victims like the Kapiñjala and other wild creatures.
Between the Sviṣṭakṛt and the Vanaspati offerings, he offers to the deities of the human victims.
The sacrificial gift is as in the Aśvamedha, along with the human victims.
All possessions [are given] by a Brāhmaṇa.
There are three Anūbandhyā cows for each deity, and five for the last.

sanskrit_iast: traidhātavyante samārohyātmann agnī sūryam upasthāya \\ adbhyaḥ sambhṛtaḥ ity anuvākenānapekṣamāṇo 'raṇyaṃ gatvā na pratyeyāt //
meaning: त्रैधातव्यन्ते समारोह्यात्मन्न् अग्नी सूर्यम् उपस्थाय \\ अद्भ्यः सम्भृतः इत्य् अनुवाकेनानपेक्षमाणो ऽरण्यं गत्वा न प्रत्येयात् //
text_mt: At the conclusion of the Traidhātavīyā offering, having mounted the fires into himself, having paid reverence to the sun with the anuvāka, "Brought together from the waters...," he should go to the forest without looking back and not return.
Or, if he intends to dwell in the village, [he mounts them] into the two churning sticks.
The Sarvamedha is for one who desires everything.

sanskrit_iast: agniṣṭut traya ukthyā indrastut sūryastud vaiśvadevastut vājapeyo 'ptoryāmaḥ sarvam asminn ālabhate //
meaning: अग्निष्टुत् त्रय उक्थ्या इन्द्रस्तुत् सूर्यस्तुद् वैश्वदेवस्तुत् वाजपेयो ऽप्तोर्यामः सर्वम् अस्मिन्न् आलभते //
text_mt: An Agniṣṭut, three Ukthyas, an Indrastut, a Sūryastut, a Vaiśvadevastut, a Vājapeya, and an Aptoryāma; in this he immolates everything.
He offers the skins of baked foods.
The cuttings of herbs and trees.
He offers every kind of food at the end of the omentum oblation;
and at the third soma pressing when the oblations have been offered.
The middle day of the Aśvamedha takes the place of the Vrata day.
That of the Puruṣamedha takes the place of the Vājapeya.
The two Ukthyas are a Triṇava and a Trayastriṃśa.
The sacrificial gift is as in the Puruṣamedha, including the land.
The Pitṛmedha is performed when the year is forgotten;

sanskrit_iast: yāvanto dhuviṣyantaḥ syus tāvataḥ kumbhān ādāya chattrāṇi cāparimitāni //
meaning: यावन्तो धुविष्यन्तः स्युस् तावतः कुम्भान् आदाय छत्त्राणि चापरिमितानि //
text_mt: Having taken as many jars as there will be persons shaking [the winnowing fans], and an unlimited number of umbrellas,

sanskrit_iast: śarīrāṇi grāmasamīpam āhṛtya kumbhena talpe kṛtvāhatapakṣeṇa paritatyāyaseṣu vādyamāneṣu vīṇāyāṃ coddhatāyām amātyās tristriḥ parikrāmanty uttarīyair upavājanair vopavājayantaḥ //
meaning: शरीराणि ग्रामसमीपम् आहृत्य कुम्भेन तल्पे कृत्वाहतपक्षेण परितत्यायसेषु वाद्यमानेषु वीणायां चोद्धतायाम् अमात्यास् त्रिस्त्रिः परिक्रामन्त्य् उत्तरीयैर् उपवाजनैर् वोपवाजयन्तः //
text_mt: having brought the bones near the village, placed them in a jar on a couch, surrounded [them] with unwashed cloth, while iron [instruments] are being beaten and a lute is loudly played, the relatives walk around three times each, fanning [them] with upper garments or fans;
And [they do so] in the early night, midnight, and the latter part of the night.
On this day, the food is devoid of solid grain;
and it is accompanied by dance, song, and musical instruments.
Some bring food near for him.
At dawn, taking the bones, they go toward the south,
so that as one performs [the rite], the sun rises;
on saline soil, sloping towards the north, or level;
and far from Nyagrodha, Aśvattha, Tilvaka, Haridru, Sphūrjaka, Bibhīdaka, and trees of inauspicious names;

sanskrit_iast: grāmatas tejanīm uchritya na nyasyed gṛheṣūchrayet //
meaning: ग्रामतस् तेजनीम् उछ्रित्य न न्यस्येद् गृहेषूछ्रयेत् //
text_mt: Having raised a reed shaft towards the village, he should not set it down; he should raise it in the houses.
He measures out a man's length with corners facing the cardinal directions;
broader to the north and to the west.
Having measured it out, he drives pegs into the corners:
a Palāśa peg in the east; Śamī, Vāraṇa, and wooden pegs in the others.

sanskrit_iast: apasalavisṛṣṭayā rajjvā paritatya \\ apeto yantu \\ iti palāśaśākhayā vyudūhati //
meaning: अपसलविसृष्टया रज्ज्वा परितत्य \\ अपेतो यन्तु \\ इति पलाशशाखया व्युदूहति //
text_mt: Having enclosed it with a cord spun counter-clockwise, he sweeps it out with a Palāśa branch with: 'Let them go away.'

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇā śākhāṃ nirasya pariśridbhiḥ pariśrayati pūrvavad aparimitābhiḥ //
meaning: दक्षिणा शाखां निरस्य परिश्रिद्भिः परिश्रयति पूर्ववद् अपरिमिताभिः //
text_mt: Having discarded the branch to the south, he encloses [it] with an unlimited number of enclosing stones, as before.

sanskrit_iast: audumbarasīra uttarato vā ṣaḍgave yujyamāne yuṅkta \\ iti sampreṣya savitā te \\ iti japati //
meaning: औदुम्बरसीर उत्तरतो वा षड्गवे युज्यमाने युङ्क्त \\ इति सम्प्रेष्य सविता ते \\ इति जपति //
text_mt: A plow of Udumbara wood, or to the north; while a team of six oxen is being yoked, having given the call: 'Yoke!', he mutters: 'May Savitṛ for you.'

sanskrit_iast: anurajju catasraḥ sītāḥ kṛṣati vāyuḥ punātu \\ iti pratimantram //
meaning: अनुरज्जु चतस्रः सीताः कृषति वायुः पुनातु \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् //
text_mt: Along the cord, he plows four furrows, with a mantra for each: 'May Vāyu purify.'
The first [furrow] is to the north, running west;
an unlimited number in the middle, silently.

sanskrit_iast: anaḍuho vimucya vimucyantām iti dakṣiṇā sīra nirasya \\ aśvatthe vas \\ iti sarvauṣadhaṃ vapati //
meaning: अनडुहो विमुच्य विमुच्यन्ताम् इति दक्षिणा सीर निरस्य \\ अश्वत्थे वस् \\ इति सर्वौषधं वपति //
text_mt: Having unyoked the oxen with: 'Let them be unyoked,' and cast the plow to the south, he sows all herbs with: 'In the Aśvattha, your [dwelling].'

sanskrit_iast: savitā te \\ iti śarīrāṇi nivapati madhye //
meaning: सविता ते \\ इति शरीराणि निवपति मध्ये //
text_mt: With: 'May Savitṛ for you,' he pours out the bones in the middle.

sanskrit_iast: tūṣṇīm anyaḥ kumbham ākṣṇauti dakṣiṇānavānant sṛtvā //
meaning: तूष्णीम् अन्यः कुम्भम् आक्ष्णौति दक्षिणानवानन्त् सृत्वा //
text_mt: Another person silently breaks the jar, having run towards the south without breathing out.
When he has returned, [the Adhvaryu] mutters: 'Far away, O Death.'

sanskrit_iast: śaṃ vātas \\ iti yathāṅgaṃ kalpayitveṣṭakāṃ nidadhāti madhye tūṣṇīm //
meaning: शं वातस् \\ इति यथाङ्गं कल्पयित्वेष्टकां निदधाति मध्ये तूष्णीम् //
text_mt: Having arranged [the bones] limb by limb with: 'May the wind be auspicious,' he places a brick in the middle silently;

meaning: प्रतिदिशम् अन्तेषु पराचीस् तिस्रस्तिस्रो ऽलक्षणाः पादमात्रीः //
text_mt: in each direction at the borders, three each facing away, without marks, measuring a foot.

sanskrit_iast: pradarāt purīṣam āhṛtya parikṛṣya vā sarvato 'purastāt //
meaning: प्रदरात् पुरीषम् आहृत्य परिकृष्य वा सर्वतो ऽपुरस्तात् //
text_mt: Having brought earth from a cleft, or having dug around on all sides except the east;
The height is up to the mouth for a Brāhmaṇa;

sanskrit_iast: avakābhiḥ kuśaiś ca prachādya parikṛṣṭaṃ ced yavān vapet //
meaning: अवकाभिः कुशैश् च प्रछाद्य परिकृष्टं चेद् यवान् वपेत् //
text_mt: Having covered [it] with Avakā plants and Kuśa grass, if it was dug around, he should sow barley.

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇataḥ kuṭile karṣū khātvā kṣīrodakābhyāṃ pūrayanti saptottarataḥ prācīr udakasya //
meaning: दक्षिणतः कुटिले कर्षू खात्वा क्षीरोदकाभ्यां पूरयन्ति सप्तोत्तरतः प्राचीर् उदकस्य //
text_mt: To the south having dug curved furrows, they fill [them] with milk and water, and to the north seven [furrows] running east [with] water.
They throw in three stones each.
They cross over [them] with: 'Possessing stones.'
With: 'Wiping away evil,' they wipe themselves with Apāmārga plants.

sanskrit_iast: sumitrayā nas \\ iti snātvāhatavāsaso 'naḍutpucham anvārabhya \\ anaḍvāham iti \\ ud vayam ity āgachanti //
meaning: सुमित्रया नस् \\ इति स्नात्वाहतवाससो ऽनडुत्पुछम् अन्वारभ्य \\ अनड्वाहम् इति \\ उद् वयम् इत्य् आगछन्ति //
text_mt: Having bathed with: 'With a friendly [eye] may [the waters gaze upon] us,' dressed in unwashed garments, holding on to the tail of an ox with: 'The ox,' they return with: 'Upwards we [behold the light].'

sanskrit_iast: grāmaśmaśānāntare maryādāloṣṭaṃ nidadhāti \\ imaṃ jīvebhyas \\ iti //
meaning: ग्रामश्मशानान्तरे मर्यादालोष्टं निदधाति \\ इमं जीवेभ्यस् \\ इति //
text_mt: Between the village and the cremation ground, he places a boundary clod with: 'This [barrier] for the living.'

sanskrit_iast: āñjanābhyañjane kṛtvaupāsanaṃ paristīrya vāraṇān paridhīn paridhāya vāraṇena sruveṇaikām āhutiṃ juhoti \\ agna āyūm̐ṣi \\ āyuṣmān agne \\ iti //
meaning: आञ्जनाभ्यञ्जने कृत्वौपासनं परिस्तीर्य वारणान् परिधीन् परिधाय वारणेन स्रुवेणैकाम् आहुतिं जुहोति \\ अग्न आयूम्̐षि \\ आयुष्मान् अग्ने \\ इति //
text_mt: Having applied salve and ointment, having strewn around the domestic fire, and having set around enclosing sticks of Vāraṇa wood, he offers one oblation with a Vāraṇa dipping spoon with: 'O Agni, life-spans,' [and] 'Possessing long life, O Agni.'

sanskrit_iast: athaiṣāṃ paridāṃ vadati parīme gām aneṣata \\ iti //
meaning: अथैषां परिदां वदति परीमे गाम् अनेषत \\ इति //
text_mt: Then he recites their entrustment: 'Around these they have led the cow.'
By a non-door he removes the domestic fire with: 'The flesh-eater.'

sanskrit_iast: āsandī sopadhānā dakṣiṇānaḍvān yavāś ca sarvaṃ purāṇam //
meaning: आसन्दी सोपधाना दक्षिणानड्वान् यवाश् च सर्वं पुराणम् //
text_mt: A stool with a cushion, an ox, and barley constitute the sacrificial gift—all of it old.
A thousand [cows are] the sacrificial gift for the Abhijit;
For the Viśvajit, [it is] a thousand [cows] or all of one's possessions (sarvavedasa).

sanskrit_iast: jyeṣṭhaṃ putram apabhajya bhūmiśūdravarjaṃ yogāviśeṣāt sarveṣām //
meaning: ज्येष्ठं पुत्रम् अपभज्य भूमिशूद्रवर्जं योगाविशेषात् सर्वेषाम् //
text_mt: Having portioned out the eldest son, excluding land and Śūdras, because there is no distinction regarding the ownership of all.
Or the giving of a Śūdra is [permitted], because of textual mention and lack of contradiction.
Due to the absence of sacrificial substance, it ends there;
or [there is] completion [of the sacrifice], because the purifying bath (avabhṛtha) is enjoined by sacred text,
In the case of a fixed quantity, all [is given], because there is no specification.
Or [only] the excess [is given], in conformity with the archetype rite;

sanskrit_iast: avabhṛthād udetya rohiṇyau vatsachavyau sakarṇapuchāvachāte paridadhāte //
meaning: अवभृथाद् उदेत्य रोहिण्यौ वत्सछव्यौ सकर्णपुछावछाते परिदधाते //
text_mt: Having stepped out from the purifying bath, they put on two red skins of calves, with ears and tails attached, which have been unstitched.
He resides outside for twelve nights, carrying a spade just as [the sacrificer carrying] the fire-pan (ukhā),
at the Udumbara tree, he feeds on roots and fruits;
"Ordinary people" means a Vaiśya; "people of one's own standing" means a Rājanya, according to sacred text.
Among the Niṣādas, [he observes] abstention from cultivated food, and drinking from earthenware vessels.
he should not refuse what is given.
Or he may sacrifice with the twin [rites, the Abhijit and Viśvajit], the preceding and following [successively],
The two sacrificial grounds (devayajanas) are to the south and north.
The rites outside the altar (vedi) are common;
If there is a conflict of actions, the Abhijit takes precedence each time.
The sacrificial gift is a separate thousand [cows for each].

sanskrit_iast: sarvajit samahāvrataḥ saṃvatsaradīkṣaḥ saptāhābhiṣavas tisra upasadaḥ ṣaḍ vā //
meaning: सर्वजित् समहाव्रतः संवत्सरदीक्षः सप्ताहाभिषवस् तिस्र उपसदः षड् वा //
text_mt: The Sarvajit has the Mahāvrata, a year-long consecration, seven days of soma-pressing, and three or six Upasad days.
He gives a chariot drawn by one hundred horses to the Adhvaryu while the fire-altar is being piled;
At the time of the sacrificial gifts, [he gives] a thousand to all [the priests together].
There are four Sāhasra sacrifices, having a thousand [cows] as their sacrificial gift.
The Jyotis and the Viśvajyotis are equal to a three-day rite (trirātra).
The first is for those who desire heaven, those who desire cattle, or those who have rivals.
The sacrificial gift is a white horse with a gold ornament on its forehead;
There is no cessation of the archetypal [gift], because of its connection with the Udgātṛ priest.
The second [rite is performed] for those who have a chronic disease, who desire firm standing, or who desire food.
The sacrificial gift is twenty-one [cows] with a horse, or a horse.
The sacrificial gift is a hundred [cows] with a horse, or a horse.

sanskrit_iast: yathādravye janapade yajeta teṣāṃ yathotsāhaṃ dadyāt //
meaning: यथाद्रव्ये जनपदे यजेत तेषां यथोत्साहं दद्यात् //
text_mt: Whatever substances are in the country in which he sacrifices, he should give those according to his capacity.
Mule-chariots among the northern peoples.
Or [he gives] substitutes for all his possessions:
A milk-cow, an ox, a plough, grain, a storage jar, a pair of male and female slaves, a kitchen, a vehicle, a tent, and beds.
Where plants do not grow, that is the sacrificial ground.
The two pressing-boards are the naves of a hearse.
The animal offering during the soma pressing is red, for Agni accompanied by Rudra.
The officiating priests officiate wearing red garments and red turbans.

sanskrit_iast: kāṇakhorakūṭabaṇḍā hrutamiśrā navanava dakṣiṇā dadāti liṅgānām //
meaning: काणखोरकूटबण्डा ह्रुतमिश्रा नवनव दक्षिणा ददाति लिङ्गानाम् //
text_mt: He gives as sacrificial gift one-eyed, lame, hornless, tailless, and defective animals, nine of each, for each characteristic.
Or [nine] per person, because of the eligibility for giving.
Or bringing forward the archetypal [cows] in division.
At the time of the sacrificial gift, they should pierce them with thorns.
While they are distressed, [they take] the clarified butter of those that are not distressed.
The rules of the Sādhyaḥkras [apply], like that having a golden garland.
In the Ekatrika, the sacrificial gift is one hundred and sixty-six [cows].
Everything beginning with the consecration is performed on the same day.
Or a sacrificial cake is [offered] in place of the animal victim for Agni-Soma.
The Subrahmaṇyā chant ceases at the end of the omentum [offering].
The officiating priests dwell in each [cardinal] direction.
The others at distances decreased by one krośa each.
They convey them in four horse-chariots with leather bags of milk.
The [animal] for buying the soma is a three-year-old [bull] with testicles intact.
He occupies [a field of] ripe rice or barley.
It is a grain threshing-floor, according to common understanding.

sanskrit_iast: ye vedim abhitas tān uttaravedideśe mṛdhnanti //
meaning: ये वेदिम् अभितस् तान् उत्तरवेदिदेशे मृध्नन्ति //
text_mt: Those [sheaves] that are around the altar they thresh in the place of the high altar.
Or [it is] a heap of dust, because of the lack of distinction in understanding.
The threshing post is the sacrificial post, [or] the pole of a plough.
Because of the mention of ready-made [items], there is cessation of the archetypal [procedures].
Or arable land and the like [are the sacrificial gifts] of the second, because of proximity.
The Vrātyastomas are four.

sanskrit_iast: vrātyagaṇasya ye sampādayeyus te prathamena yajeran //
meaning: व्रात्यगणस्य ये सम्पादयेयुस् ते प्रथमेन यजेरन् //
text_mt: Those of a Vrātya group who can afford it should sacrifice with the first.
Censured and cruel [persons should sacrifice] with the second.

sanskrit_iast: apetaprajananā sthavirās tadākhyās teṣāṃ yo nṛśam̐satamaḥ syād dravyavattamo vānūcānatamo vā tasya gārhapate dīkṣeran //
meaning: अपेतप्रजनना स्थविरास् तदाख्यास् तेषां यो नृशम्̐सतमः स्याद् द्रव्यवत्तमो वानूचानतमो वा तस्य गार्हपते दीक्षेरन् //
text_mt: Those past procreative age, the elders, are designated by that name; among them, he who is the most cruel, or the wealthiest, or the most learned, at his Gārhapatya fire they should undergo consecration.
They should sit consuming [portions of soma] after his consumption.
There are Vrātya possessions.
A turban tied across, [and] a goad.
A jyāhroḍa—a bow unfit [for battle] is so designated.
Not black, or with black borders, is so designated.
A rough cart covered with planks.

sanskrit_iast: aśvāśvatarābhyāṃ kamprābhyāṃ yuktaḥ syād ity eke //
meaning: अश्वाश्वतराभ्यां कम्प्राभ्यां युक्तः स्याद् इत्य् एके //
text_mt: It should be yoked with a horse and a mule that are skittish, say some.
Two sheepskins with flanks attached, black and white.
In the same manner the skins belong to the others.

sanskrit_iast: dāmatūṣāṇi balūkāntāni dvicūḍānyāvikāni vāsām̐si lohitāntāni kṛṣṇāntāni vā tadākhyāni //
meaning: दामतूषाणि बलूकान्तानि द्विचूडान्याविकानि वासाम्̐सि लोहितान्तानि कृष्णान्तानि वा तदाख्यानि //
text_mt: Woollen garments with fringed cords, ending in tassels, with two crests, red-bordered or black-bordered, are so designated.

sanskrit_iast: dāmanī dvedve upānahau ca karṇinyau kṛṣṇe syātām ity eke //
meaning: दामनी द्वेद्वे उपानहौ च कर्णिन्यौ कृष्णे स्याताम् इत्य् एके //
text_mt: Two ropes each, and two shoes with ears, black, should be [theirs], say some.
At the time of the sacrificial gift, they should give the Vrātya possessions to a degraded Brahmin of the Māgadha region.
Or to those who have not ceased from Vrātya conduct.
Because of the Vedic text: "Wiping off [guilt] upon them indeed, they go forth."
They should each give thirty-three [cows as] sacrificial gifts.
The householder [gives] double, say some.
Having sacrificed with a Vrātyastoma, they should cease from Vrātya-hood.
The Agniṣṭut is for those desiring spiritual lustre, valour, food, [or] firm standing, and for one who considers himself as if unpurified.
Or [for one desiring that priests] should not fall away from him.
The particular [chant variations are] in the Chāndogya [tradition], according to desire.
He should give according to capacity among things sacred to Agni: an ox, gold, a horse, [or] goats.
The first has an unexpressed morning pressing.
The sacrificial gift is a horse-drawn chariot yoked with four, one of them dark brown.
The Bṛhaspatisava is for one desiring fiery energy, spiritual lustre, [or] priesthood.
He pours out the Devasū oblations.

sanskrit_iast: atigrāhyavad grahaṃ gṛhṇāti bṛhaspate ati yad aryas \\ iti //
meaning: अतिग्राह्यवद् ग्रहं गृह्णाति बृहस्पते अति यद् अर्यस् \\ इति //
text_mt: He draws a soma cup like an Atigrāhya cup with: "O Bṛhaspati, that which [exceeds] the rival..."
The animal to be seized belongs to Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit_iast: nihiteṣu nārāśam̐seṣu prātaḥsavane 'napākurvann ekādaśa dakṣiṇā vyādiśati //
meaning: निहितेषु नाराशम्̐सेषु प्रातःसवने ऽनपाकुर्वन्न् एकादश दक्षिणा व्यादिशति //
text_mt: When the Nārāśaṃsa cups have been deposited at the morning pressing, without leading [them] away, he assigns eleven sacrificial gifts.
At the midday [pressing], twelve, with a horse [as the twelfth].
The leading away takes place at the end of the omentum oblation of the Anūbandhyā cow.
And the crossing over of all [the cows].
Or there should be eleven hundred each.
A horse, however, is additional at the midday [soma pressing].
He is consecrated with clarified butter on a black antelope skin in the manner of the Vājapeya.
Or with the residue of the Śukra and Manthin cups.
They should address him: 'O Sthapati!'

sanskrit_iast: sarājāno brāhmaṇā yaṃ puraskurvīrant sa etena yajeta //
meaning: सराजानो ब्राह्मणा यं पुरस्कुर्वीरन्त् स एतेन यजेत //
text_mt: He whom the Brāhmaṇas, together with kings, place at their head, should sacrifice with this [rite].
The Sarvasvāra has cooked food for sacrificial gifts.
Beginning from the consecration, he only smells the portions to be consumed.
The disposal into water is for the non-soma portions.

sanskrit_iast: ārbhave stūyamāne dakṣiṇenaudumbarīṃ kṛṣṇājine saṃviśati dakṣiṇāśirāḥ //
meaning: आर्भवे स्तूयमाने दक्षिणेनौदुम्बरीं कृष्णाजिने संविशति दक्षिणाशिराः //
text_mt: While the Ārbhava [stotra] is being chanted, he lies down south of the audumbarī post on a black antelope skin with his head toward the south.

sanskrit_iast: tad eva mriyate jīvec ced dairghaśravasam̐ svāsu yajñāyajñiyasthāne kuryuḥ //
meaning: तद् एव म्रियते जीवेच् चेद् दैर्घश्रवसम्̐ स्वासु यज्ञायज्ञियस्थाने कुर्युः //
text_mt: He dies right then; if he should live, they should perform the Dairghaśravasa [sāman] on its own verses in place of the Yajñāyajñīya.
When he is dead, it ends right there, because of the absence of need.
