Having thrown the sacrificer’s utensils, soma residue, and oblations into the Āhavanīya fire, they may go according to their purpose.
Or there is completion [of the sacrifice], because both are enjoined.

sanskrit_iast: samiṣṭayajurante saṃ tvā hinvanti \\ iti dārvāharaṇam //
meaning: समिष्टयजुरन्ते सं त्वा हिन्वन्ति \\ इति दार्वाहरणम् //
text_mt: At the conclusion of the samiṣṭayajus offerings, bringing of the wood takes place with: 'They speed thee…'
The fashioning [of the litter takes place] with: 'They have fashioned thee…'
The washing [takes place] with: 'They cleanse thee…'
The weaving of the chair-litter [takes place] with: 'They sharpen thee…'

sanskrit_iast: āsandyainam avabhṛtham̐ hṛtvābhyukṣya somopanahanena prachādyānūbandhyavapāhomānte dakṣiṇasyāṃ vediśroṇau sarvakeśaśmaśrulomavapanam //
meaning: आसन्द्यैनम् अवभृथम्̐ हृत्वाभ्युक्ष्य सोमोपनहनेन प्रछाद्यानूबन्ध्यवपाहोमान्ते दक्षिणस्यां वेदिश्रोणौ सर्वकेशश्मश्रुलोमवपनम् //
text_mt: Having carried him on the chair-litter to the final bath, sprinkled [him] with water, covered [him] with the soma-cloth, and concluded the offering of the omentum of the anūbandhyā cow, the shaving of all hair of the head, beard, and body [takes place] on the southern buttock of the vedi.

sanskrit_iast: anūbandhyānte 'gnīn āhṛtya vedimadhyam āgnīdhrād dakṣiṇaṃ dakṣiṇāśirasaṃ citāv āhitam udgātā trir yāmena parigāyan nāke suparṇam ity etasyām //
meaning: अनूबन्ध्यान्ते ऽग्नीन् आहृत्य वेदिमध्यम् आग्नीध्राद् दक्षिणं दक्षिणाशिरसं चिताव् आहितम् उद्गाता त्रिर् यामेन परिगायन् नाके सुपर्णम् इत्य् एतस्याम् //
text_mt: At the conclusion of the anūbandhyā, having brought the fires to the middle of the vedi, to the south of the Āgnīdhra [hearth], when he has been placed on the pyre with his head to the south, the Udgātṛ chants thrice around [him] with the Yāma [sāman] on this [verse]: 'The fair-winged bird on the firmament…'

sanskrit_iast: dhūmaprāptam \\ tveṣas te dhūma ṛṇvati \\ iti //
meaning: धूमप्राप्तम् \\ त्वेषस् ते धूम ऋण्वति \\ इति //
text_mt: When the smoke reaches him, with: 'Fierce does thy smoke rise…'

sanskrit_iast: agniprāptam agne mṛḍa mahā3ṃ asi \\ ity anyatareṇa //
meaning: अग्निप्राप्तम् अग्ने मृड महा3ं असि \\ इत्य् अन्यतरेण //
text_mt: When the fire reaches him, with either: 'O Agni, be gracious; thou art great3…'
Or [the funeral rites take place] at the end of the concluding bath (udavasanīyā), because of the completion of everything.
If he should live, he should seek to die by this very undertaking.
The Ṛtvigapohanīya rites are three.
And the two final days of the Chandoma [period] having been separated.
The Pṛṣṭhyastomas are: Trivṛt, Pañcadaśa, Saptadaśa, Ekaviṃśa, Triṇava, and Trayastriṃśa.

sanskrit_iast: cāturmāsyāḥ somās triṣu parvasthāneṣu pārṣṭhikāni pṛṣṭhyo vihṛta iti śruteḥ //
meaning: चातुर्मास्याः सोमास् त्रिषु पर्वस्थानेषु पार्ष्ठिकानि पृष्ठ्यो विहृत इति श्रुतेः //
text_mt: The soma rites of the Cāturmāsyas consist of the Pṛṣṭhya [days] distributed at three seasonal joints, because of the śruti: 'The Pṛṣṭhya is distributed.'
In place of the Vaiśvadeva [parvan] is the first.
And the preparation of the high altar is omitted.
The animal is tied to an enclosing stick.
In the second [parvan] is a two-day rite named Dvidiva.
Some say the first is an Agniṣṭoma.
In the third [parvan] is a three-day rite; the last day is an Atirātra.
Some say the first is an Agniṣṭoma.
A Jyotiṣṭoma takes the place of the Śunāsīrīya [parvan].
At five [soma pressings], the pressing animals are those for the Viśvedevas, Varuṇa, the Maruts, Agni, and Indra-Agni.

sanskrit_iast: pañcāśataṃpañcāśataṃ pratyahaṃ dadāty uttame dvādaśam̐ śatam //

text_mt: He gives fifty [cows] each day; on the last day, one hundred and twelve.
Or fifty calves born according to the season.
Between the joints, he wears an unwashed garment.
The barren cows (anūbandhyā) are dedicated to Bṛhaspati, Mitra-Varuṇa, Sūrya, and the Aśvins respectively, according to each concluding bath.
[Namely, for] the Agnyādheya, Punarādheya, Agnihotra, New- and Full-Moon sacrifices, Dākṣāyaṇa, and Āgrayaṇa rites.
Some say the animal sacrifice is an Ukthya.
In the morning, he pours out the oblations following the pressing animals.
The savanīya [offerings] have as their first the deity of the final offering, [namely] the anūbandhyā [cow].
The unexpressed Upahavya is for one desiring a domain.
Or for one falsely accused [of a grave sin].

meaning: श्यावो ऽश्वो दक्षिणा तं ब्रह्मणे ददाति //
text_mt: A dark horse is the sacrificial gift; he gives it to the Brahman priest.
The Ṛtapeya is for one desiring heaven.
or in both cases there is a count of twelve, on account of being an auxiliary [specification].

sanskrit_iast: camasaṃ pūrṇam aṅguliparvaṇā maulyena sarvataḥ pramitam ādyāyām upasadi //

text_mt: On the first Upasad day, a full cup measured all around by the joint of a finger as the purchase-price.
About to consume [the soma], they should speak the truth.
A soma cup made of udumbara wood is to be given as the sacrificial gift to a Brahman priest of the same gotra.
[It is filled] from the pūtabhṛt [vat], because it serves all purposes.

sanskrit_iast: am̐śucamasam eke tena sa yajeteti śruteḥ //
meaning: अम्̐शुचमसम् एके तेन स यजेतेति श्रुतेः //
text_mt: Some [prescribe] an am̐śu cup, because of the Vedic text: 'With that he should sacrifice.'
The Dvināmottara, the Bahuhiraṇya, and the Dūṇāśa [follow].
At the dīkṣaṇīyā offering he gives gold of twelve measures.
And at each subsequent [rite], double the previous one:
at the prāyaṇīyā, atithyā, and the Upasads;
at the end of the omentum of the animal [sacrifice], and when the savanamukhīya [cups] are deposited at each pressing;
at the udayanīyā, at the anūbandhyā, and at the udavasānīyā, and a garland to the Udgātṛ priest;
a golden ornament to the Hotṛ priest, and a hundred oxen to all [the priests] at the proper time.
The Vaiśyastoma is for a Vaiśya and for one desiring cattle.
At the morning pressing, the mixture is made with freshly drawn milk;
The sacrificial gifts are five-year-old spotted young bulls.

sanskrit_iast: vatsataryaś ca trihāyaṇyo 'pravītāḥ pañcavarṇā rājīvapṛśnayo navanītaprāśnayo 'ruṇāḥ piśaṅgyaḥ sāraṅgya iti //
meaning: वत्सतर्यश् च त्रिहायण्यो ऽप्रवीताः पञ्चवर्णा राजीवपृश्नयो नवनीतप्राश्नयो ऽरुणाः पिशङ्ग्यः सारङ्ग्य इति //
text_mt: And heifers, three years old, unbred, five-coloured: striped-spotted, butter-eating, reddish, yellowish-brown, and speckled.
A thousand of both, or one hundred and twelve.
The Tīvrasut is an Ukthya for one excessively purged by soma;
or for those suffering from chronic disease, desiring a domain, desiring offspring, or desiring cattle.
They milk a hundred cows for the admixture.
Consuming [takes place] during the individual portions of the Achāvāka;

sanskrit_iast: teṣv evonnayanam abhyabhi somān unnayantīti śruteḥ //
meaning: तेष्व् एवोन्नयनम् अभ्यभि सोमान् उन्नयन्तीति श्रुतेः //
text_mt: Drawing [the soma] takes place into those [cups] alone, because of the Vedic text: 'They draw the soma portions over and over.'

sanskrit_iast: adhvaryū camasādhvaryavaś ca sarve pratigṛṇanty achāvākāya //
meaning: अध्वर्यू चमसाध्वर्यवश् च सर्वे प्रतिगृणन्त्य् अछावाकाय //
text_mt: The Adhvaryu and all the Camasādhvaryus respond to the Achāvāka.
The first of the paired rites is the Rāṭ, for a noble desiring kingship.
He should give according to his ability groups of twenty-one [cows].
A bull for Indra is the supplementary animal sacrifice.
He should give according to his ability groups of ten [cows].
An animal for Agni is the supplementary animal sacrifice.
The Aupaśada is for one desiring procreation.
The sacrificial gift is one hundred and twenty-four [cows].
An animal for the Viśvedevas is the supplementary animal sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast: bahu pratigṛhya garagīriva yo manyeta tasya punastoma ukthyaḥ //

text_mt: For one who, having accepted many gifts, considers himself as if he had swallowed poison, his [sacrifice] is the Punastoma, an Ukthya.
The sacrificial gift is twelve pairs, and of [cows] having returned [to milk], according to ability.
The two sacrifices for one desiring cattle are Catuṣṭomas.

sanskrit_iast: pūrvasmin yathāśakty ekaśaphān dadyād ubhayān uttarasmin //

text_mt: At the first, he should give single-hoofed animals according to his ability; at the second, both [single-hoofed and cloven-hoofed].
And the Udbhid and Balabhid are connected rites bringing [their fruits].
Having sacrificed with the first, [he] necessarily [sacrifices] with the second.
Between these two there is an Iṣu offering, [which is] a cake on eight potsherds for Agni.
The enclosing sticks are tipped with arrows.
For half a month, a month, or a year [between them].
The sacrificial gift consists of groups of twenty-four according to the Gāyatrī measure, or according to ability.
For one desirous of honor, there are the two Apaciti rites.
The sacrificial gift is a horse chariot yoked with four horses on both [sides].
They are accompanied by the piling of the fire altar, are Agniṣṭomas, and have the consecration of the Sarvajit.
The first has wings; the second is the Jyotis.
The sacrificial gifts are four cartloads of grain each.
For the first, [wagons drawn by] six oxen; for the second, [wagons drawn by] four oxen.
The sacrificial gift is a thousand bulls, or one hundred and twelve.
The Gosava is an Ukthya with a sacrificial gift of ten thousand [cows].

text_mt: One whom the subjects together with their kings place at their head should sacrifice with this.
With warm fresh milk to the south of the Āhavanīya fire.
They should address him as 'Sthapati' (Chief).

sanskrit_iast: vaiśyastomadakṣiṇāliṅgo marutstomo gaṇayajño bhrātṝṇām̐ sakhīnāṃ vā //
meaning: वैश्यस्तोमदक्षिणालिङ्गो मरुत्स्तोमो गणयज्ञो भ्रातॄणाम्̐ सखीनां वा //
text_mt: The Marutstoma, having the sacrificial gift characteristic of the Vaiśyastoma, is a collective sacrifice for brothers or friends.
For one desirous of offspring or cattle, there is the Aindrāgnakulāya, whose sacrificial gift is a herd.
It is a dual sacrifice for two brothers or two friends.
The Indrastoma is a sacrifice for a king.
For one desirous of the office of family priest, there is the Indrāgnyoḥ Stoma.
Or for a king and a family priest sacrificing together.
The sacrificial gift conforms to the Gāyatrī for a Brāhmaṇa.
[The gifts] conform to the Bṛhatī for one desirous of cattle.
For one practicing sorcery, they are well-known.
The Saṃdaṃśa and the Vajra are for one practicing sorcery.
A cow whose horns are trimmed or red-eared is the soma-purchasing cow of the Ṣoḍaśin.
He should practice sorcery against a single king with the first.
Or he may employ the two alternately.

text_mt: Having appeased or slain [the enemy], he should sacrifice with the Jyotiṣṭoma for the purpose of expiation.
Ahīna sacrifices have twelve Upasad days and are completed within a month.
The consecrations occupy the remainder of the soma-pressing and Upasad days.
They begin with two-day rites and extend up to twelve-day rites.
Some hold that Atirātras also [are included] on account of being mentioned there.
The days of the Ten-Day rite [are used] in the two-day rites and so on with an increase of one [each time], because their qualities are observed.
In the four-day rites and beyond, [it is] more.
He gives them equally divided each day.
The first four are without the Ṣoḍaśin.
The Navasaptadaśa [Atirātra] is for one desiring progeny.
The Viṣuvant is for the eldest son of an eldest wife.
The Āyuḥ is for one desiring heaven, or for one who is chronically ill.
The Jyotiṣṭoma, Viśvajit, Trivṛt, Pañcadaśa, Saptadaśa, and Ekavim̐śa [Atirātras] are respectively for those desiring prosperity, livestock, sacred luster, vigor, food, and stability.
The Aptoryāma is for one from whom livestock are about to perish entirely.
The Abhijit is for one having rivals.
The Sarvastoma is for one desiring to become prosperous.
The Atirātras of the latter two are without the Ṣoḍaśin.
[They are] the Āṅgirasa, Caitraratha, and Kāpivana.
Some [teachers hold that] the second has an Ukthya preceding [the Atirātra].

sanskrit_iast: prathamena yajeta yaḥ pauṇyo hīna iva syāt //

text_mt: He who is lacking in merit, as it were, should sacrifice with the first.
One desiring heaven or one desiring livestock [should sacrifice] with the third.
There are five three-day rites: the Garga, Baida, Chandoma, Antarvasu, and Parāka.
In the second, all the Atirātras are nine-versed.
The Antarvasu is for one desiring livestock.
The Parāka is for one desiring heaven.
The Atri-caturvīra, Jāmadagnya, Vasiṣṭha-sam̐sarpa, and Viśvāmitra.
The Jāmadagnya has twenty consecrations, [and is] for one desiring nourishment.
Its Upasad rites are provided with cake offerings.
[The offering has] the characteristics of clarified butter, because of taking its place;
or it has the characteristics of vegetable food, on account of the common substance.

At each Upasad, with an increase of one potsherd, beginning from a single-potsherd [cake, there are cakes] for Agni, the Aśvins, Viṣṇu, Soma, Savitṛ, Dhātṛ, the Maruts, Bṛhaspati, Mitra-Varuṇa, Indra, and the Viśvedevas.

sanskrit_iast: teṣām̐ homaḥ agne ver hotraṃ ver adhvaram \ ā pitaraṃ vaiśvānaram avase kar \ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \ devāv aśvinau madhukaśayādyemaṃ yajñaṃ yajamānāya mimikṣatam \ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \ deva viṣṇa urv adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāyādhi vikramasva \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \ deva soma retodhā adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāyaidhi \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \ deva savitaḥ susāvitram adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāyāsuvasva \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \ deva dhātaḥ sudhātādyāsmin yajñe yajamānāyaidhi \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \ devā grāvāṇo madhumatīm adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāya vācaṃ vadata \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \ devy anumate 'nv adyemaṃ yajñaṃ yajamānāya manyasva \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \ devy adite svādityam adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāyāsuvasva \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \ devya āpo naṃnamyadhvam adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāya \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \ sadaḥsadaḥ prajāvān ṛbhur juṣāṇas \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \ deva tvaṣṭaḥ suretodhā adyāsmin yajñe yajamānāyaidhi \\ indrāya devebhyo juhutā haviḥ svāhā \\ iti //
meaning: तेषाम्̐ होमः अग्ने वेर् होत्रं वेर् अध्वरम् \ आ पितरं वैश्वानरम् अवसे कर् \ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \ देवाव् अश्विनौ मधुकशयाद्येमं यज्ञं यजमानाय मिमिक्षतम् \ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \ देव विष्ण उर्व् अद्यास्मिन् यज्ञे यजमानायाधि विक्रमस्व \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \ देव सोम रेतोधा अद्यास्मिन् यज्ञे यजमानायैधि \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \ देव सवितः सुसावित्रम् अद्यास्मिन् यज्ञे यजमानायासुवस्व \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \ देव धातः सुधाताद्यास्मिन् यज्ञे यजमानायैधि \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \ देवा ग्रावाणो मधुमतीम् अद्यास्मिन् यज्ञे यजमानाय वाचं वदत \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \ देव्य् अनुमते ऽन्व् अद्येमं यज्ञं यजमानाय मन्यस्व \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \ देव्य् अदिते स्वादित्यम् अद्यास्मिन् यज्ञे यजमानायासुवस्व \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \ देव्य आपो नंनम्यध्वम् अद्यास्मिन् यज्ञे यजमानाय \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \ सदःसदः प्रजावान् ऋभुर् जुषाणस् \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \ देव त्वष्टः सुरेतोधा अद्यास्मिन् यज्ञे यजमानायैधि \\ इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुहुता हविः स्वाहा \\ इति //
text_mt: Their offering [formulae are]: 'Agni, foster the office of Hotṛ, foster the sacrifice; take father Vaiśvānara for help! For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!' 'Divine Aśvins, moisten today this sacrifice for the sacrificer with your honey-whip! For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!' 'Divine Viṣṇu, stride widely today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer! For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!' 'Divine Soma, be the placer of seed today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer! For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!' 'Divine Savitṛ, impel good impulsion today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer! For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!' 'Divine Dhātṛ, be a good supporter today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer! For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!' 'Divine pressing-stones, speak honeyed speech today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer! For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!' 'Divine Anumati, approve today this sacrifice for the sacrificer! For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!' 'Divine Aditi, grant freedom from injury today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer! For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!' 'Divine Waters, bend low today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer! For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!' 'Delighting at every place, possessing progeny, Ṛbhu... For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!' 'Divine Tvaṣṭṛ, be the placer of good seed today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer! For Indra, for the gods, offer the oblation, svāhā!'—thus.
With these, at the end of the pressing, he sacrifices for twelve days in reverse order, with one [oblation] each day.
The second is the Pañcaśāradīya.

sanskrit_iast: tena yakṣyamāṇaḥ pañca varṣāṇy āśvayujīśukleṣu catustrim̐śataṃ paśūn ālabhate mārutān //
meaning: तेन यक्ष्यमाणः पञ्च वर्षाण्य् आश्वयुजीशुक्लेषु चतुस्त्रिम्̐शतं पशून् आलभते मारुतान् //
text_mt: Intending to sacrifice with this, for five years during the bright fortnights of the month of Āśvayuja, he seizes thirty-four animal victims for the Maruts,
having the marks of the sacrificial gifts of the Vaiśyastoma;
bulls and heifers, in order of color.
Having carried fire around them, they release the bulls, and conclude [the rite] with the heifers.
In this manner, they tether the bulls for five years.

meaning: षष्ठे सवनीया भवन्ति त्रयस्त्रयो ऽन्वहम् ऐन्द्रामारुताः //
text_mt: In the sixth year, they become the pressing animals, three each day for Indra and the Maruts.

sanskrit_iast: yaḥ kāmayeta bahuḥ syām iti sa etena yajeta //
meaning: यः कामयेत बहुः स्याम् इति स एतेन यजेत //
text_mt: One who desires, 'May I become manifold,' should sacrifice with this.
one to Bṛhaspati if it loses a horn, has deformed horns, or is one-eyed;
to Agni accompanied by Rudra, if it is afflicted by Rudra;
if it is crushed, a single-potsherd cake to the Earth;
if it is carried off by force, [a cake] to Indra the Forceful;
if it dies when it is fit for food, a twelve-potsherd cake to Prajāpati.
He should feed the dead animal to Brahmins.
Throwing into water or depositing [the food takes place], because it is spoiled.
Elsewhere too, because of the connection with a defect.
[The days are] Jyotis, Go, Mahāvrata, Go, and Āyus.
The Ahīna sacrifices have the [Mahā]vrata and have the Sarvajit consecrations.
There are three six-day rites; the first is for the seasons.
In the second, there is a five-day rite having the Bṛhadrathantara-pṛṣṭha, named Pṛṣṭhyāvalamba.
In the third, after three [days], there are the Trikadruka days.
There are seven seven-day rites; the first four have the [Mahā]vrata as the final [day].
From the second onward, there are six one-day rites.
[In] the seven-day rite of Janaka, after four [days], there are the Viśvajit and the Mahāvrata.
In the final [seven-day rite], there is a six-day rite having the Bṛhadrathantara-pṛṣṭha, named Pṛṣṭhyastoma.
In the eight-day rite, the Mahāvrata follows the six-day rite.
In the nine-day rite, there are the Trikadruka days.
The second [nine-day rite consists of] the Pṛṣṭhyāvalamba after the Trikadruka days.
An Ukthya having Agniṣṭoma wings is repeated thrice.
There are three Trivṛt Agniṣṭomas,
The Pūrdaśarātra is for one against whom black magic is being practiced.
It has an Ukthya with Agniṣṭoma wings,
The Chandomadaśāha is for one desiring cattle.
Following the Pṛṣṭhyāvalamba, there are four Chandomas.
The Pauṇḍarīka is for one desiring all prosperity.
It is a ten-day rite without rising from a sacrificial session.
The duty of the Adhvaryu is identical in the Atirātras, except for the Viśvajit.
The night sacrificial sessions begin with the twelve-day rite.
They end with forty [days], increasing by one.
When [the number] is not filled out, the ten-day rite is subsequent.
In rites prescribed according to the archetype, the Mahāvrata follows the ten-day rite when there is need for a one-day rite.
When there is need for a five-day rite, its first five [days are used].

sanskrit_iast: tryahārthe jyotir gaur āyur iti trikadrukāḥ //
meaning: त्र्यहार्थे ज्योतिर् गौर् आयुर् इति त्रिकद्रुकाः //
text_mt: When there is need for a three-day rite, the Trikadrukas, namely Jyotis, Go, and Āyus [are used].
When there is need for a four-day rite, [these] and the [Mahā]vrata as prescribed [are used].
The interval between the Atirātras is the place for insertion.
Among those that are brought together by insertion, the smaller and smaller [rite comes] first.
There are two thirteen-day rites: after the Pṛṣṭhya, there is a Sarvastoma Atirātra.
The second is prescribed according to the archetype.
There are three fourteen-day rites.
In the middle one, the Trikadruka days are on both sides of the Pṛṣṭhya.
This rite is for those whose marriage, water offerings, or bed-sharing are in dispute.
The third is enjoined according to the archetype rite.
There are four fifteen-day rites.
The first two are explained by the two fourteen-day rites.
Between the two Pṛṣṭhya [six-day periods] is the Mahāvrata.
After the Atirātra, the Agniṣṭut of the second [rite is performed].
That [Agniṣṭut] is the opening rite of the third.
Prior to the twenty-day rite, [the multi-day rites] are enjoined according to the archetype rite.
In the twenty-day rite, there are an Abhiplava [six-day period], and the Abhijit and Viśvajit.
In the two twenty-one-day rites, the two Atirātras are without the Ṣoḍaśin.
There are three Abhiplavas; after the first, there is an Atirātra.
The second [twenty-one-day rite is performed] in summer for those who desire spiritual luster.

sanskrit_iast: trayastrayaḥ svarasāmāno viṣuvantam abhitaḥ pṛṣṭhyau ca //
meaning: त्रयस्त्रयः स्वरसामानो विषुवन्तम् अभितः पृष्ठ्यौ च //
text_mt: There are three Svarasāman days on each side of the central day, and two Pṛṣṭhya [six-day periods].
[The victim] dedicated to Soma and Pūṣan is to be offered.
Up to the thirty-two-day rite, [the rites] are enjoined according to the archetype rite.
The twenty-two-day rite is for those who desire food.
The twenty-three-day rite is for those who desire a firm standing.
The former twenty-four-day rite is for those who desire offspring or desire cattle.
The three subsequent Pṛṣṭhya days are in reverse and direct order.
On either side of it are two unexpressed Agniṣṭomas.
From that [follow] two unexpressed Agniṣṭomas.

sanskrit_iast: pañcavim̐śatirātram annādyakāmānām̐ ṣaḍvim̐śatirātraṃ pratiṣṭhākāmānām̐ saptavim̐śatirātram ṛddhikāmānām aṣṭāvim̐śatirātraṃ prajākāmānāṃ paśukāmānāṃ vā //
meaning: पञ्चविम्̐शतिरात्रम् अन्नाद्यकामानाम्̐ षड्विम्̐शतिरात्रं प्रतिष्ठाकामानाम्̐ सप्तविम्̐शतिरात्रम् ऋद्धिकामानाम् अष्टाविम्̐शतिरात्रं प्रजाकामानां पशुकामानां वा //
text_mt: The twenty-five-day rite is for those who desire food; the twenty-six-day rite is for those who desire a firm standing; the twenty-seven-day rite is for those who desire prosperity; the twenty-eight-day rite is for those who desire offspring or desire cattle.
There are three thirty-three-day rites.
After three [five-day periods], there is an Atirātra; [the other day is] the Viśvajit.
The second [thirty-three-day rite] contains the Vrata and three Abhiplavas.
In the intervals between the Abhiplavas, there are two Atirātras.
In the third, there are three five-day periods on each side of the Viśvajit.
Up to the forty-day rite, [the rites] are enjoined according to the archetype rite.
The thirty-four-day rite is for those who desire food.
The thirty-six-day rite is for those who desire a firm standing.
The thirty-seven-day rite is for those who desire prosperity.
The thirty-eight-day rite is for those who desire offspring or desire cattle.
The subsequent rites contain the Vrata, with the exception of the first and the third; there are seven forty-nine-day rites.
The first three-day period is the Kausurubinda.
And on either side of the Pṛṣṭhya [six-day period] there are twelve [days] each.
In the intervals between the groups, there are Atirātras.
There are two Abhiplavas, the Go and Āyus days, and two Atirātras.
There are two Abhiplavas, the Abhijit and Viśvajit, and two Atirātras.
There is an Abhiplava, an all-stoma [rite], nine [chants], seventeen [chants], and two Atirātras.
In the Āñjanābhyañjanīya, there are six Abhiplavas.
After four [Abhiplavas], there is an all-stoma Atirātra.

sanskrit_iast: tasminn upasatsu sarpir vipaceyur gārhapatye gulgulusugandhitejanapītudārubhiḥ //
meaning: तस्मिन्न् उपसत्सु सर्पिर् विपचेयुर् गार्हपत्ये गुल्गुलुसुगन्धितेजनपीतुदारुभिः //
text_mt: During the Upasads of that [rite], they should boil clarified butter on the Gārhapatya fire with bdellium, fragrant reed-grass, and cedar wood.

sanskrit_iast: yathāsavanaṃ taiḥ savaneṣv āñjanābhyañjane kurvīrann āgnīdhre 'harahaḥ //
meaning: यथासवनं तैः सवनेष्व् आञ्जनाभ्यञ्जने कुर्वीरन्न् आग्नीध्रे ऽहरहः //
text_mt: According to the soma pressing, they should day after day perform eye-salving and body-anointing with those [substances] at the soma pressings in the Agnīdhra [shed].
Or when about to consume [the soma] at the start of the soma pressings.

sanskrit_iast: ya ātmānaṃ naiva jānīraṃs teṣām etat //
meaning: य आत्मानं नैव जानीरंस् तेषाम् एतत् //
text_mt: This belongs to those who do not know themselves.
In the [sacrifice] measuring a year, [there is] the twenty-fourth day.
After three [Abhiplavas], there is a nine-day period having the central day in its middle.
In the sixty-one-day rite, there is a Pṛṣṭhya [six-day period] on both sides of the nine-day period.
The first, seventh, and final [days] of the nine-day groups are Agniṣṭomas; the others are Ukthyas.
After four [days] of the preceding [rite], there is the Mahāvrata.
A hundred-day rite is prescribed like the archetype rite, [comprising] fourteen Abhiplavas and a four-day period.
The Sadas and the Havirdhāna sheds possess wheels.
They press [soma] while moving forward, without encroaching on the [successive] places.
Day after day during the Abhiplavas, or during the Trikadrukas.
The completion is by repeating the Abhiplava.
The ten-day period is employed only once.
The rites containing the Mahāvrata have the consecrations of the Sarvajit.

sanskrit_iast: saptadaśarātrādīni trim̐śadantāny eka ekānnapañcāśadrātre cāṣṭādaśadīkṣāṇi paurṇamāsīprakramāṇi //
meaning: सप्तदशरात्रादीनि त्रिम्̐शदन्तान्य् एक एकान्नपञ्चाशद्रात्रे चाष्टादशदीक्षाणि पौर्णमासीप्रक्रमाणि //
text_mt: [The rites] beginning with the seventeen-day period and ending with the thirty-day period, and in one forty-nine-day period, have eighteen consecrations and begin on the full-moon day.
In the hundred-day Atirātra, the days [are taken from the archetype] because of similarity to the hundred-day rite.
Or [they are modeled on] the first [rites] of the twelve-day sacrifice, because of its being their archetype rite.
And likewise in the hundred-day Agniṣṭoma and hundred-day Ukthya.

sanskrit_iast: āśvinasyāgneyānte pratiprasthātā vyutkrāmatādi kṛtvā maitrāvaruṇāya prātaranuvākam upākṛtyāntaryāmam̐ hutvā prapīḍya pavitraṃ droṇakalaśe nidadhāti //
meaning: आश्विनस्याग्नेयान्ते प्रतिप्रस्थाता व्युत्क्रामतादि कृत्वा मैत्रावरुणाय प्रातरनुवाकम् उपाकृत्यान्तर्यामम्̐ हुत्वा प्रपीड्य पवित्रं द्रोणकलशे निदधाति //
text_mt: At the end of the Āgneya cup of the Āśvina [graha], the Pratiprasthātṛ, having performed [the actions] beginning with stepping out, having initiated the morning recitation for the Maitrāvaruṇa, and having offered the Antaryāma cup, squeezes [the strainer] and places the filter in the Droṇakalaśa.
He performs [the rites] beginning with the Tiro’ahnya [grahas] of the preceding day.
Having performed [the rites] beginning with drawing the cups up to the drops-offering,
he offers the continuity-of-pressing oblation with: 'Agni at the morning pressing...'
[The rites] beginning with the year have the Gavāmayana as their archetype rite, because of the appearance of its characteristics.
In the Ādityānāmayana, the Abhiplavas have the Trivṛt and Pañcadaśa stomas.
The Bṛhaspatisava takes the place of the Abhijit.
The Indrastoma takes the place of the Viśvajit.

sanskrit_iast: viśvajitaḥ pare ye trayo 'bhiplavās teṣām uttarayo sthāne trivṛto 'gniṣṭomā daśa //
meaning: विश्वजितः परे ये त्रयो ऽभिप्लवास् तेषाम् उत्तरयो स्थाने त्रिवृतो ऽग्निष्टोमा दश //
text_mt: In place of the latter two of the three Abhiplavas following the Viśvajit, there are ten Trivṛt Agniṣṭomas,
At the beginning of the sixth month, in the middle position, there is a Pṛṣṭhya.
In place of the ten-day period, there is the ten-day Chandoma period.
The Aṅgirasāmayana is like the Ādityānāmayana.
The months begin with the Pṛṣṭhya in the first half [of the year], and are reversed in the latter [half].
The Pṛṣṭhya which is in the middle of the Abhiplava is the last.
The Go and Āyus [days] are reversed, and also the ten-day Chandoma period.
The Dṛtivātavatorayana has month after month with a single Pṛṣṭhya-stoma.
Or they are distinct days, because of the collective designation.
The second half is in reverse order.
The Kuṇḍapāyināmayana has its consecration on the full-moon day.
Or on the fourth day of the dark fortnight.

sanskrit_iast: somam upanahya sutyāsthāneṣu māsam agnihotraṃ juhvati //
meaning: सोमम् उपनह्य सुत्यास्थानेषु मासम् अग्निहोत्रं जुह्वति //
text_mt: Having tied up the soma, they offer the Agnihotra for a month at the places of soma-pressing.
[They sacrifice] with the New- and Full-Moon sacrifices for a month.
Whatever oblation belongs to the beginning of the fortnight is [offered] on every [day].
Or [they are performed] as a common procedure, because they are enjoined collectively.
The months [are offered] separately with the seasonal periods of the Four-Month sacrifices.
The Sākamedha offerings are like the New- and Full-Moon sacrifices.
The session of Dṛti and Vātavant [proceeds] for six months with the first half of the course.
In the last [month], there are three Abhiplavas, the ten-day period, and the Mahāvrata.
An Atirātra takes place at the end.
Some [prescribe] an Atirātra after the Haviryajñas, lest it interrupt the soma rites.
The cups are handleless and shaped like bowls.
Five officiating priests should perform three duties each.
The Hotṛ [performs] the duties of the Adhvaryu and of the Potṛ.
The Udgātṛ [performs] those of the Neṣṭṛ and the Acchāvāka.
The Maitrāvaruṇa [performs] the office of Brahman and that of the Pratihartṛ.
The Prastotṛ [performs] those of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin and the Grāvastut.
The Pratiprasthātṛ [performs] those of the Agnīdh and the Unnetṛ.
From their primary seats, they glide along to the others.
The Sarpasattra [consists of] alternation, the Virāj, and the second Kausurubinda.
Or it is a Gavāmayana, because of the Vedic text regarding the Abhigara chant.

sanskrit_iast: tāpaścitam dīkṣāḥ saṃvatsaramupasadaś ca tathā sutyāḥ //
meaning: तापश्चितम् दीक्षाः संवत्सरमुपसदश् च तथा सुत्याः //
text_mt: The Tāpaścita [consists of] consecrations for a year, Upasads [for a year], and soma pressings likewise.
They should proceed according to the Gavāmayana.
Or with each one of the Sarvajit, Abhijit, and Viśvajit.
The Mahātāpaścita has Upasads for three years.
In the Kṣullakatāpaścita, the consecration, Upasads, and soma pressings last four months each.
On either side of the central day, [there are] the first and the last [six months] of the halves of the Gavāmayana.
[It consists of] one hundred and sixty-four Abhiplava [six-day periods] and a four-day rite.
It lasts three years, with sixty days of consecration.
The Āditya [session consists of] three years of soma pressing.
A fourth part, a fourth part of each [is performed] with the stomas of the Jyotiṣṭoma.

sanskrit_iast: teṣv atirātraviṣuvantaḥ syur vā na vā //
meaning: तेष्व् अतिरात्रविषुवन्तः स्युर् वा न वा //
text_mt: In them, the Atirātras and central days may or may not take place.
Or two Atirātras at the beginning and end, and the central day in the middle.
The twelve-year session belongs to Prajāpati.
The thirty-six-year session belongs to the Śāktyas; [its] cake offerings are made of meat.
Or [only] the pressing cakes, because of the frequent scriptural mention.
The hundred-year session belongs to the Sādhyas.
The thousand-year session belongs to the Viśvasṛjs.
The Sarasvatī sacrificial sessions are traveling sessions.
The Sadas, the Havirdhāna, and the Āgnīdhra [sheds] have wheels.
The sacrificial post, having a mortar-shaped base, is to be dragged along.
They release one hundred pregnant heifers, with one bull in addition, to make up a thousand.
They strew [soil] over the places of the Uparavas; they do not dig.
The consecration takes place on the seventh day of the bright fortnight at the Vinaśana of the Sarasvatī.
The consecration and Upasads are like those of the twelve-day sacrifice.
The introductory Atirātra takes place right there.

sanskrit_iast: sam̐sthite 'dhvaryur āhavanīyasamīpe sthitvābhyadhvam̐ śamyāṃ prāsyati tad gārhapatyasya sthānam //
meaning: सम्̐स्थिते ऽध्वर्युर् आहवनीयसमीपे स्थित्वाभ्यध्वम्̐ शम्यां प्रास्यति तद् गार्हपत्यस्य स्थानम् //
text_mt: When it has concluded, the Adhvaryu, standing near the Āhavanīya fire, throws the yoke-pin along the path: that is the site of the Gārhapatya fire.
The Āhavanīya is [established] as previously prescribed.
They carry the utensils of the sacrifice according to how they stood.
Taking the earth of the mounds, they pour it out in the corresponding place.
On the two days of offering, the Go and Āyus [rites are performed].
At the intervals between the seasonal nodes, the New- and Full-Moon sacrifices [are performed].

sanskrit_iast: śamyāprāseśamyāprāse vasanto yajamānāś ca yanti dakṣiṇena tīreṇa //
meaning: शम्याप्रासेशम्याप्रासे वसन्तो यजमानाश् च यन्ति दक्षिणेन तीरेण //
text_mt: Halting at each throw of the yoke-pin, the sacrificers go along the southern bank.
At the confluence with the Dṛṣadvatī, there is a caru for Apāṁ Napāt.
At Plakṣa Prāsravaṇa, there is an iṣṭi for Agni Kāma.
At it they should give a mare and a woman with young.
And according to some, [they give] the remaining equipment of the sacrifice at the end of the udayanīyā rite.
They descend for the avabhṛtha into the Yamunā opposite Kārapacava.
Or [the offering] for Agni Kāma is before the avabhṛtha.
They should disperse according to their purpose.
The Sarasvatī [sessions] do not have the pṛṣṭha-pacification.
Their mid-terminations are three, with Atirātras:
completion of a thousand, death of the householder, and loss of all property.
At the loss of all property, [the day is] the Viśvajit.
Or [it is] the Jyotiṣṭoma for all [three].
The avabhṛtha is not in the Sarasvatī.
In the second [session], the course of Dṛti and Vātavant, the days between the parvan days alternately have the trivṛt and pañcadaśa stomas.

sanskrit_iast: tayoś ced asamāptayor āgached yajanīyakālas tam upetya śeṣam anusamāpayeyuḥ //
meaning: तयोश् चेद् असमाप्तयोर् आगछेद् यजनीयकालस् तम् उपेत्य शेषम् अनुसमापयेयुः //
text_mt: If the time for sacrifice arrives before those two are completed, they should approach it and finish the remainder [later].

sanskrit_iast: śuklapakṣaś cet trivṛd agniṣṭoma ity eke //
meaning: शुक्लपक्षश् चेत् त्रिवृद् अग्निष्टोम इत्य् एके //
text_mt: According to some, if it is the bright fortnight, [it is] a trivṛt Agniṣṭoma.
In the dark [fortnight], [it is] a pañcadaśa Ukthya.
In the third [session], on the two sacrifice days, there are the Abhijit and Viśvajit.
Between the parvan days are the Trikadruka rites.
The completion is as before.

sanskrit_iast: dārṣadvatam ṛtvigācāryayor anyatarasya gā rakṣet saṃvatsaram //
meaning: दार्षद्वतम् ऋत्विगाचार्ययोर् अन्यतरस्य गा रक्षेत् संवत्सरम् //
text_mt: [For] the Dārṣadvata [session], one should guard the cows of either the officiating priest or the teacher for a year.
Another [view]: one should kindle the fire at Vyarṇa on the Naitandhava.

meaning: कुरुक्षेत्रे परिणहि स्थले ऽग्न्याधेयम् अन्वारम्भणीयान्तं भवति //
text_mt: At Pariṇah, an elevated place in Kurukṣetra, the agnyādheya takes place, ending with the anvārambhaṇīyā rite.
Or ending with the New- and Full-Moon sacrifices.

meaning: आहिताग्निश् चेद् व्यर्णे ऽग्निहोत्रम् एव जुहुयात् //
text_mt: If one has already set up the fires, one should offer only the agnihotra at Vyarṇa.
There is a cake for Agni; sacrificing with that, [it proceeds] as before.
And having gone along the bank of the Dṛṣadvatī,
they descend for the avabhṛtha into the Yamunā opposite Triplakṣāvaharaṇa.
Having stepped out, one should sacrifice with this very iṣṭi.
The Turāyaṇa begins on the fifth [tithi] of the bright half of Vaiśākha.
At the end of the morning offering, uninitiated, he puts on the emblems of consecration.

sanskrit_iast: havīm̐ṣi nirvapaty āgneyam aindraṃ vaiśvadevaṃ carum̐ savanakāleṣv ekaikam //
meaning: हवीम्̐षि निर्वपत्य् आग्नेयम् ऐन्द्रं वैश्वदेवं चरुम्̐ सवनकालेष्व् एकैकम् //
text_mt: He pours out the oblations: the Āgneya, the Aindra, and the Vaiśvadeva caru, one at each soma pressing time.
The avabhṛtha and subsequent rites are like the Dārṣadvata, without a specified body of water.
The Bharata-dvādaśāha has all Agniṣṭoma days.
In the Saṅkrama-dvādaśāha, the first days of the three-day periods of the Daśarātra form the first three-day period.

sanskrit_iast: tryahadvitīyāni dvitīyas tryahas tryahatṛtīyāni tṛtīyas tryahaḥ //
meaning: त्र्यहद्वितीयानि द्वितीयस् त्र्यहस् त्र्यहतृतीयानि तृतीयस् त्र्यहः //
text_mt: The second days of the three-day periods form the second three-day period; the third days of the three-day periods form the third three-day period.
Or [it is performed] with each one of the Agniṣṭut, Indrastut, Sūryastut, and Vaiśvadevastut.
Or with the Trikadruka rites, or with each one of the ahīna and ekāha rites, except the Aptoryāma and Rājasūya.
When repetition is not possible, the Jyotiṣṭoma serves as the filler.

sanskrit_iast: yathoktasya stotram̐ stotriyaṃ varcaṃ vā sāma vā yajur vāhar vānyat kṛtvā yajeta //
meaning: यथोक्तस्य स्तोत्रम्̐ स्तोत्रियं वर्चं वा साम वा यजुर् वाहर् वान्यत् कृत्वा यजेत //
text_mt: Having changed the stotra, the stotriya verse, the ṛc, the sāman, the yajus, or the day of the prescribed [rite], he should sacrifice.
For those who omit [days during] the course, there are modifications of the Gavāmayana.

sanskrit_iast: pañcokthyāṃs trīn abhiplavān upetya caturthaṃ caturukthyam upayanti //
meaning: पञ्चोक्थ्यांस् त्रीन् अभिप्लवान् उपेत्य चतुर्थं चतुरुक्थ्यम् उपयन्ति //
text_mt: Having undertaken three Abhiplavas with five Ukthyas, they undertake the fourth with four Ukthyas.
Or there is the omission of the stoma of a single day.
Or the performance of the rite of pressing of the animal [sacrifice].

sanskrit_iast: ayam eva prāyaṇīyo 'tirātraḥ sarvam̐ sattram̐ syāt //
meaning: अयम् एव प्रायणीयो ऽतिरात्रः सर्वम्̐ सत्त्रम्̐ स्यात् //
text_mt: This opening Atirātra itself may constitute the entire sacrificial session.

meaning: ज्योतिष्टोमाश् चत्वारो ऽभिजित् तैः षण् मासान् //
text_mt: Four Jyotiṣṭomas [and] an Abhijit: with these [they proceed for] six months.
A Viśvajit [and] four Jyotiṣṭomas: with these [they proceed for] the latter [six months].
This is the highest [sattra], of Nārāyaṇa Puruṣa.
Upon a failure in the ritual action, an expiation is to be performed at that very time.
When [a specific expiation is] unprescribed, an oblation with the Mahāvyāhṛtis [is offered].
In the case of [an error in] the Hotṛ's office, [an oblation is offered] in the Gārhapatya fire with [the word] "bhūḥ".
In the case of the Adhvaryu's office, in the Dakṣiṇa fire with "bhuvaḥ".
In the case of the Udgātṛ's office, in the Āhavanīya fire with "svaḥ".
These [oblations] consist everywhere of four ladlings [of ghee].
And the universal expiation [is performed] with five verses, stanza by stanza:

sanskrit_iast: tvaṃ no agne \\ iti dvābhyām ayāś cāgne 'sy anabhiśastiś ca \ satyam it tvam ayā asi \ ayā no yajñaṃ vahāsi \\ ayā no dhehi bheṣajam̐ svāhā \ ye te śataṃ varuṇa ye sahasram \\ yajñiyāḥ pāśā vitatā mahāntaḥ \ tebhir no adya savitota viṣṇur \ viśve muñcantu marutaḥ svarkāḥ svāhā \\ ud uttamam iti ca //
meaning: त्वं नो अग्ने \\ इति द्वाभ्याम् अयाश् चाग्ने ऽस्य् अनभिशस्तिश् च \ सत्यम् इत् त्वम् अया असि \ अया नो यज्ञं वहासि \\ अया नो धेहि भेषजम्̐ स्वाहा \ ये ते शतं वरुण ये सहस्रम् \\ यज्ञियाः पाशा वितता महान्तः \ तेभिर् नो अद्य सवितोत विष्णुर् \ विश्वे मुञ्चन्तु मरुतः स्वर्काः स्वाहा \\ उद् उत्तमम् इति च //
text_mt: with the two [stanzas beginning], "O Agni, do thou unto us...", [with the stanza] "And art thou, Agni, unassailable and free from curses, in truth art thou unassailable; unassailable, bear our sacrifice unto us, unassailable, grant us medicine, svāhā!", [with the stanza] "What hundred, O Varuṇa, what thousand sacrificial nooses of thine are stretched out wide, through these may Savitṛ and Viṣṇu and all the well-praising Maruts release us today, svāhā!", and with [the stanza] "The highest...";
when [the error is] unknown, [an oblation is offered] with each Mahāvyāhṛti, and a fourth with all [three combined],

sanskrit_iast: agnihotrī ced duhānopaviśed yajuṣotthāpanam eke \\ udasthād devy aditir \ āyur yajñapatāv adhāt \\ indrāya krṇvatī bhāgam \\ mitrāya varuṇāya ca \\ iti //
meaning: अग्निहोत्री चेद् दुहानोपविशेद् यजुषोत्थापनम् एके \\ उदस्थाद् देव्य् अदितिर् \ आयुर् यज्ञपताव् अधात् \\ इन्द्राय क्र्ण्वती भागम् \\ मित्राय वरुणाय च \\ इति //
text_mt: If the Agnihotra cow sits down while being milked, according to some [teachers] she is raised up with the yajus: "The divine Aditi has stood up; she has placed life in the lord of sacrifice, making a portion for Indra, and for Mitra and Varuṇa."

sanskrit_iast: dugdhvā brāhmaṇāyaināṃ dadyād yam anabhyāgamiṣyant syāt //
meaning: दुग्ध्वा ब्राह्मणायैनां दद्याद् यम् अनभ्यागमिष्यन्त् स्यात् //
text_mt: Having milked her, he should give her to a Brahmin whom he will not approach again.
Or having stroked her with a stick and raised her up, the milking [proceeds],

sanskrit_iast: vāśyeta cet tṛṇāny ālupya grāsayet sūyavasād bhagavati hi bhūyās \\ atho vayaṃ bhagavantaḥ syāma \ addhi tṛṇam aghnye viśvadānīm \\ piba śuddham udakam ācarantī \\ iti //
meaning: वाश्येत चेत् तृणान्य् आलुप्य ग्रासयेत् सूयवसाद् भगवति हि भूयास् \\ अथो वयं भगवन्तः स्याम \ अद्धि तृणम् अघ्न्ये विश्वदानीम् \\ पिब शुद्धम् उदकम् आचरन्ती \\ इति //
text_mt: If she bellows, he should pluck grass and feed her, [saying]: "Mayest thou be rich in pasture, O fortunate one; and may we also be fortunate. Eat grass, O inviolable cow, at all times; drink pure water as thou wanderest."

sanskrit_iast: lohitadohe dakṣiṇāgniṃ pariśritya vyutkrāmata \\ ity uktvoṣṇe bhasmani rudrāya hutvā pūrvavaddānam //
meaning: लोहितदोहे दक्षिणाग्निं परिश्रित्य व्युत्क्रामत \\ इत्य् उक्त्वोष्णे भस्मनि रुद्राय हुत्वा पूर्ववद्दानम् //
text_mt: If she yields red [bloody] milk, having enclosed the Dakṣiṇa fire, said: "Step aside!", and offered [the milk] on hot ashes to Rudra, he gives [the cow] away as before.

sanskrit_iast: haumyaṃ gavi sad raudram upasṛṣṭaṃ vāyavyam duhyamānam āśvinam dugdham̐ saumyam adhiśritaṃ vāruṇam udantaṃ pauṣṇam viṣyandamānaṃ mārutam bindumat sārasvatam̐ śāntaṃ maitram udvāsyamānam̐ savitur udvāsitam aditer unnīyamānaṃ vaiśvadevam unnītaṃ bārhaspatyam prahriyamāṇaṃ dhātram prahṛtaṃ vaiśvakarmaṇam antarāgnī vaiśvānarāyopasannaṃ dyāvāpṛthivyoḥ pūrvāhutir indrāgnyor uttarā prajāpater hutam aindram //
meaning: हौम्यं गवि सद् रौद्रम् उपसृष्टं वायव्यम् दुह्यमानम् आश्विनम् दुग्धम्̐ सौम्यम् अधिश्रितं वारुणम् उदन्तं पौष्णम् विष्यन्दमानं मारुतम् बिन्दुमत् सारस्वतम्̐ शान्तं मैत्रम् उद्वास्यमानम्̐ सवितुर् उद्वासितम् अदितेर् उन्नीयमानं वैश्वदेवम् उन्नीतं बार्हस्पत्यम् प्रह्रियमाणं धात्रम् प्रहृतं वैश्वकर्मणम् अन्तराग्नी वैश्वानरायोपसन्नं द्यावापृथिव्योः पूर्वाहुतिर् इन्द्राग्न्योर् उत्तरा प्रजापतेर् हुतम् ऐन्द्रम् //
text_mt: The [milk] fit for oblation, while in the cow, belongs to Rudra; when [the calf is] driven up to her, to Vāyu; while being milked, to the Aśvins; milked, to Soma; put on the fire, to Varuṇa; bubbling up, to Pūṣan; overflowing, to the Maruts; marked with drops, to Sarasvatī; quieted down, to Mitra; being taken off [the fire], to Savitṛ; taken off, to Aditi; being ladled out, to the Viśvedevas; ladled out, to Bṛhaspati; being carried forward, to Dhātṛ; carried forward, to Viśvakarman; between the two fires, to Vaiśvānara; placed near [the fire], to Heaven and Earth; the first oblation belongs to Indrāgnī; the second to Prajāpati; the [portion] offered belongs to Indra.

sanskrit_iast: yathākālopapāte taddevate taddaivatam̐ hutvā tad vātidiśyānyena juhyāt //
meaning: यथाकालोपपाते तद्देवते तद्दैवतम्̐ हुत्वा तद् वातिदिश्यान्येन जुह्यात् //
text_mt: Upon an error occurring at a particular time, having offered to that deity [governing that stage], or having transferred it [mentally], he should offer with another [milk].

sanskrit_iast: skandec cet \\ askann adhita prājani \\ ity abhimṛśya śeṣeṇa juhuyāt //
meaning: स्कन्देच् चेत् \\ अस्कन्न् अधित प्राजनि \\ इत्य् अभिमृश्य शेषेण जुहुयात् //
text_mt: If [the oblation] spills, having touched it with [the mantra], "It was not spilled, it was placed, it was generated...", he should offer with what remains.

sanskrit_iast: bhidyeta ced avāpadyeta skannaprāyaścittenābhimṛśya vyāhṛtibhiś cādbhir upaninīya kapālāni bhasmodvāpe kuryāt //
meaning: भिद्येत चेद् अवापद्येत स्कन्नप्रायश्चित्तेनाभिमृश्य व्याहृतिभिश् चाद्भिर् उपनिनीय कपालानि भस्मोद्वापे कुर्यात् //
text_mt: If [the vessel] breaks or falls down, having touched it with the expiation for spilling, poured water over it with the Vyāhṛtis, he should dispose of the potsherds in the place where the ashes are removed.
In a haviryajña, [he touches the spilt oblation with the formula], "To the lord of the earth...";
in a soma sacrifice, with "They have gone to the gods, to heaven";
or he should sprinkle it with water with [the formula], "By the might of which two..."
In the case of a total spilling of what was ladled out, or the breaking of the ladle, the [priest's] sitting remains right there.

meaning: अन्यद् उन्नीयान्यो ऽस्मै प्रयछेत् तेन होमः //
text_mt: Another person, having ladled out another [portion], hands it to him; with that the oblation is made.

sanskrit_iast: pūrvāhutau hutāyāṃ ced āhavanīyo 'nugachet tad uktam //
meaning: पूर्वाहुतौ हुतायां चेद् आहवनीयो ऽनुगछेत् तद् उक्तम् //
text_mt: If the Āhavanīya fire goes out after the first oblation has been offered, that has already been stated.
He should offer over a piece of wood or gold, because of the scriptural statement.

sanskrit_iast: triruddhṛtaś ced āhavanīyo 'nugached udaksthānāny upalipya nirmathya sakṛduddhṛte tasmint sāyamprātarhomam eke //
meaning: त्रिरुद्धृतश् चेद् आहवनीयो ऽनुगछेद् उदक्स्थानान्य् उपलिप्य निर्मथ्य सकृदुद्धृते तस्मिन्त् सायम्प्रातर्होमम् एके //
text_mt: If the Āhavanīya goes out when it has been brought out three times, having smeared the northern spots [with cow dung] and churned [out new fire], according to some [teachers] the evening and morning oblation [is offered] in that [fire] once it has been brought out once.
When the Gārhapatya has gone out, the churning [is done] after touching the two churning sticks with ashes.
Or, if the Āhavanīya is awake [burning], the bringing out [of the fire is done] from that itself;

sanskrit_iast: samārohyāsamārohya vā pūrvam upaśamayya pūrvavad dhomaḥ //
meaning: समारोह्यासमारोह्य वा पूर्वम् उपशमय्य पूर्ववद् धोमः //
text_mt: Having caused [the fires] to ascend [into the churning sticks] or without causing them to ascend, and having extinguished the former [fire], the oblation is performed as before.

sanskrit_iast: trirāhṛto dakṣiṇāgnir anugachec cet anāharaṇam asya tadahar eke //
meaning: त्रिराहृतो दक्षिणाग्निर् अनुगछेच् चेत् अनाहरणम् अस्य तदहर् एके //
text_mt: If the Dakṣiṇa fire, brought three times, goes out, according to some [teachers] it is not brought again on that day.

sanskrit_iast: jāgratam āhavanīyam abhyuddharec cet tad uktam //
meaning: जाग्रतम् आहवनीयम् अभ्युद्धरेच् चेत् तद् उक्तम् //
text_mt: If one brings out [fire] over the burning Āhavanīya fire, that has already been stated.

sanskrit_iast: paścān nidhāya purastād vobhayatra homam eke //
meaning: पश्चान् निधाय पुरस्ताद् वोभयत्र होमम् एके //
text_mt: Having placed [the new fire] behind or in front, according to some [teachers] the oblation is made in both places.
When [a fire] is placed over [another burning fire], a puroḍāśa is offered to Agni Agnimat.
Or there is an attendance [upon the fires] with the two verses [beginning with], "United..."

sanskrit_iast: gṛhītānugamane ca \\ anv agnir ity āhṛtya //
meaning: गृहीतानुगमने च \\ अन्व् अग्निर् इत्य् आहृत्य //
text_mt: And when the taken fire goes out, having brought it with [the verse beginning], "After Agni..."
Where no [specific offering] is specified, it is everywhere a cake.

sanskrit_iast: anuddhṛtābhyastamaye kuśabaddhe hiraṇye paścād dhriyamāṇa idhmenoddhared ārṣeyo brāhmaṇaḥ //
meaning: अनुद्धृताभ्यस्तमये कुशबद्धे हिरण्ये पश्चाद् ध्रियमाण इध्मेनोद्धरेद् आर्षेयो ब्राह्मणः //
text_mt: If the sun sets before [the fire] has been taken out, a brāhmaṇa of ṛṣi descent should take it out with the fuel bundle, while a piece of gold tied in kuśa grass is held behind.
To Viṣṇu and to Agni Sūryavat.
If [the sun] rises upon [the unextracted fire], silver is held in front, [and there is] an oblation to the Viśvedevas.
Or in both cases [the offering is] to the Viśvedevas, without a cake.
If both [fires] go out, there may be re-establishment [of the fires].

sanskrit_iast: mathyamānaś cen na jāyeta yam adūrāt parāpaśyet tam āhṛtyābhijuhuyāt //
meaning: मथ्यमानश् चेन् न जायेत यम् अदूरात् परापश्येत् तम् आहृत्याभिजुहुयात् //
text_mt: If [the fire] being churned should not be produced, he should bring whatever [fire] he sees nearby and offer upon it.
Because of the Vedic text: 'One should not feel disgust toward water.'
If [the sun] rises when [the oblation] is scooped up but not yet offered, he should sit [holding it] until he is exhausted.
Having offered, [the recitation of] the subsequent mantra is: 'Bhūḥ'.

sanskrit_iast: sarvanāśe haviṣāṃ doṣe vā tad uktam //
meaning: सर्वनाशे हविषां दोषे वा तद् उक्तम् //
text_mt: In the event of total loss of the oblations or their corruption, that has been stated.
Or worship of the deities [takes place] by counting them over with clarified butter.
In the case of a breach, because of the occurrence of misarrangement.
If [someone] walks between [the fires], he should not pay heed.
In the case of a dog, a ram, or a boar, [he pours] a stream of water toward the east with: 'This Viṣṇu...'.
When a cart [crosses between], and when a known iṣṭi has lapsed.
Because the Vedic text refers to lapses among the regular [rites].
In case of confusion regarding a chant or a recitation.
[It applies] to one's own kinsman, through the force of the occasion.

meaning: अग्नये व्रतपतये व्रत्ये ऽहनि मैथुनमाम्̐सभोजनं चेत् //
text_mt: [An offering is made] to Agni Vratapati if copulation or eating of meat [occurs] on a day of vow.
[An offering is made] to Agni Vratabhṛt if tears of distress are shed by the one who has established the sacred fires.

meaning: अनुक्रोशे ऽग्नये सम्̐सर्गायाहुतिर् वा ग्रामाग्निना चेत् //
text_mt: Out of remorse, or an oblation to Agni Saṃsarga if it is with a village fire.
To Agni Vivici if [the sacred fires mingle] with one another.
To Agni Saṃvarga if [it mingles] with a forest fire.
To Agni Apsumat if [it mingles] with lightning fire.
To Agni Śuci if [it mingles with fire] from a pure locus.
Upon the birth of twins among wives or cows, he should apportion [a cake] on thirteen potsherds to the Maruts.
When a house burns, [there is] a cake for Agni Kṣāmavat.
If the moon rises upon [him] beforehand on the New Moon day, he should observe that vow.
He should deposit the curds as the curdling agent for the oblation.
Having released the calves, [there is] their separation once again.

sanskrit_iast: nirupte vratāśaktau vā traidhaṃ taṇḍulān vibhajya madhyamān agnaye dātre sthaviṣṭhān indrāya pradātre dadhani carum aṇiṣṭhān viṣṇave śipiviṣṭāya śṛte carum //
meaning: निरुप्ते व्रताशक्तौ वा त्रैधं तण्डुलान् विभज्य मध्यमान् अग्नये दात्रे स्थविष्ठान् इन्द्राय प्रदात्रे दधनि चरुम् अणिष्ठान् विष्णवे शिपिविष्टाय शृते चरुम् //
text_mt: If [the grains] are already measured out, or if he is unable to keep the vow, he should divide the rice grains into three parts: the middle ones [as a cake] for Agni Dātṛ; the largest ones as boiled rice in curds for Indra Pradātṛ; the finest ones as boiled rice in boiled milk for Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa.
Because of the textual statement regarding the removal of its rice grains.

sanskrit_iast: paścādabhyuddṛṣṭa āmāvāsyeneṣṭvā tadahar vaiva śvo vāgnaye pathikṛta indrāya vṛtraghna ekādaśakapālo vaiśvānaraś ca //
meaning: पश्चादभ्युद्दृष्ट आमावास्येनेष्ट्वा तदहर् वैव श्वो वाग्नये पथिकृत इन्द्राय वृत्रघ्न एकादशकपालो वैश्वानरश् च //
text_mt: If [the moon] is seen to rise afterward, having sacrificed with the New Moon sacrifice, on that very day or the next day [he offers] to Agni Pathikṛt, [a cake] on eleven potsherds to Indra Vṛtrahan, and [a cake] to Vaiśvānara.
A bow with three arrows is the sacrificial gift.
Also for one desirous of cattle upon whom [the sun] has not risen.
If a potsherd is lost while being removed, [there is an offering] to the Aśvins.

sanskrit_iast: sāyamprātardohārtāvaindraṃ pañcaśarāvam odanaṃ nirvapet puroḍāśaṃ vā //
meaning: सायम्प्रातर्दोहार्तावैन्द्रं पञ्चशरावम् ओदनं निर्वपेत् पुरोडाशं वा //
text_mt: If the evening or morning milking is spoiled, one should apportion a five-cup mess of boiled rice or a cake for Indra.
Or an expiation, because the deity is explicitly prescribed by scripture.
Or a cake in place of the evening milking.
Disposal of spoiled sacrificial substance into water [takes place].
Spoiled is that which is forbidden from consumption by the cultured.
Or the combined rites belong to it.
If a sacrificial substance is omitted, having remembered before the primary offering, he should bring it up.
Or before the samiṣṭayajus, because of the scriptural statement regarding the conclusion [of the rite].

sanskrit_iast: hutaṃ cet sam̐sthāpya tad eva punar nirvapet //
meaning: हुतं चेत् सम्̐स्थाप्य तद् एव पुनर् निर्वपेत् //
text_mt: If [the primary offering] has been made, having concluded [the sacrifice], he should apportion that very [substance] again.
In case of transposition of deities, having given an abundant [gift], he performs [them] in proper sequence.
And [the same applies] in the case of portions, and yājyā and anuvākyā verses.
If that in the ladle is spoiled, taking [it] again [is done].

sanskrit_iast: dhruvāyā vā tato yajñaḥ prabhavatīti śruteḥ //
meaning: ध्रुवाया वा ततो यज्ञः प्रभवतीति श्रुतेः //
text_mt: Or from the dhruvā ladle, because of the scriptural text: 'The sacrifice originates from it.'

sanskrit_iast: adoṣo vā na vai devāḥ kasmāc cana bībhatsanta iti śruteḥ //
meaning: अदोषो वा न वै देवाः कस्माच् चन बीभत्सन्त इति श्रुतेः //
text_mt: Or there is no defect, because of the scriptural text: 'The gods indeed shrink not from anything.'
Having apportioned an excess [amount], he should sacrifice that as well.

sanskrit_iast: aitu rājā varuṇo revatībhir \ asmint sthāne tiṣṭhatu modamānaḥ \ ariṣṭā asmākaṃ vīrās \\ mā parāseci matpayas \\ iti praṇītā skannā abhimṛśet //
meaning: ऐतु राजा वरुणो रेवतीभिर् \ अस्मिन्त् स्थाने तिष्ठतु मोदमानः \ अरिष्टा अस्माकं वीरास् \\ मा परासेचि मत्पयस् \\ इति प्रणीता स्कन्ना अभिमृशेत् //
text_mt: With 'May King Varuṇa come with the wealthy ones; may he remain rejoicing in this place; uninjured be our heroes; let not my milk be spilled away,' he should touch the spilled praṇītā water.

sanskrit_iast: bhūmir bhūmim avāgāt \\ mātā mātaram apyagāt \ bhūyāma putraiḥ paśubhir \ yo no dveṣṭi sa bhidyatām iti mṛnmayaṃ bhinnam abhimṛśet //
meaning: भूमिर् भूमिम् अवागात् \\ माता मातरम् अप्यगात् \ भूयाम पुत्रैः पशुभिर् \ यो नो द्वेष्टि स भिद्यताम् इति मृन्मयं भिन्नम् अभिमृशेत् //
text_mt: With 'Earth has gone to earth; the mother has joined the mother; may we abound with sons and cattle; he who hates us, let him be shattered,' he should touch a shattered earthen vessel.

sanskrit_iast: ya ṛte cid abhiśriṣaḥ \ purā jatrubhya ātṛdaḥ \ saṃdhātā saṃdhiṃ maghavā purūvasur \ iṣkartā vihrutaṃ punar iti ca gharmyam //
meaning: य ऋते चिद् अभिश्रिषः \ पुरा जत्रुभ्य आतृदः \ संधाता संधिं मघवा पुरूवसुर् \ इष्कर्ता विह्रुतं पुनर् इति च घर्म्यम् //
text_mt: And [with] 'Who even without bindings, before the collar-bones are pierced, Maghavan of many riches is the joiner of the joint, the repairer again of what is broken,' [he touches] the earthen pot for the gharma.
And he offers thirty-four [oblations] beginning with Parameṣṭhin.
Also when the milk-cow for the gharma stumbles and when there is failure to yield milk.
In the milking-place of the northern [cow], [he milks] another [cow].
Or in front of the sacrificial shed, in that of the eastern [cow].
Having offered to the right bone of the tail-stalk, he should cause [her] to be milked.
And some [prescribe this] upon spilling of the clotted butter.

sanskrit_iast: somejyopapāte caikaikāṃ yathākālam̐ hutvā yajñasya dohas \\ iti vācayati //
meaning: सोमेज्योपपाते चैकैकां यथाकालम्̐ हुत्वा यज्ञस्य दोहस् \\ इति वाचयति //
text_mt: And upon the occurrence of a Soma sacrifice, having offered each at its proper time, he causes [the sacrificer] to recite: 'The milking of the sacrifice...'

sanskrit_iast: ā pavasva hiraṇyavad ity udgātṛhomo dhvāṅkṣarohaṇe yūpasya //
meaning: आ पवस्व हिरण्यवद् इत्य् उद्गातृहोमो ध्वाङ्क्षरोहणे यूपस्य //
text_mt: An offering by the Udgātṛ priest with 'Flow clear, possessing gold...' is performed upon a crow mounting the sacrificial post.

sanskrit_iast: pṛṣadājyaskandane juhyāt \\ ayā viṣṭhā janayan karvarāṇi \ sa hi ghṛṇir urur varāya gātuḥ \ sa pratyudaid dharuṇo mṛdhvo agram \\ svāyāṃ yat tanvāṃ tanūm airayata svāhā \\ iti //
meaning: पृषदाज्यस्कन्दने जुह्यात् \\ अया विष्ठा जनयन् कर्वराणि \ स हि घृणिर् उरुर् वराय गातुः \ स प्रत्युदैद् धरुणो मृध्वो अग्रम् \\ स्वायां यत् तन्वां तनूम् ऐरयत स्वाहा \\ इति //
text_mt: Upon spilling of the clotted butter, he should offer with: 'Producing variegated forms through this distribution; for he is the heat, a broad path for the blessing; that upholder rose against the front of the adversaries, when in his own body he set his form, svāhā.'

sanskrit_iast: gharmadhukśārdūlahatā cet spṛtor juhuyāt \\ candrāt te mana spṛṇomi svāhā \ sūryāt te cakṣu spṛṇomi svāhā \ vātāt te prāṇānt spṛṇomi svāhā \ digbhyas te śrotram̐ spṛṇomi svāhā \\ adbhyas te lohitam̐ spṛṇomi svāhā \ pṛthivyai te śarīram̐ spṛṇomi svāhā \\ iti //
meaning: घर्मधुक्शार्दूलहता चेत् स्पृतोर् जुहुयात् \\ चन्द्रात् ते मन स्पृणोमि स्वाहा \ सूर्यात् ते चक्षु स्पृणोमि स्वाहा \ वातात् ते प्राणान्त् स्पृणोमि स्वाहा \ दिग्भ्यस् ते श्रोत्रम्̐ स्पृणोमि स्वाहा \\ अद्भ्यस् ते लोहितम्̐ स्पृणोमि स्वाहा \ पृथिव्यै ते शरीरम्̐ स्पृणोमि स्वाहा \\ इति //
text_mt: If the milk-cow for the gharma is killed by a tiger, he should offer the two deliverance-oblations with: 'From the moon I deliver thy mind, svāhā; from the sun I deliver thine eye, svāhā; from the wind I deliver thy breathings, svāhā; from the quarters I deliver thine hearing, svāhā; from the waters I deliver thy blood, svāhā; from the earth I deliver thy body, svāhā.'
Having offered, he should say: 'Drive another [cow] near.'
One who offers by himself, if incapacitated, should sit nearby.
If incapacitated from approaching, sitting below [is prescribed].

sanskrit_iast: sāyamāhutyām̐ hutāyāṃ ced durbalaḥ syāt tadaiva prātarāhutis tat sam̐sthāśruter agnihotrasya //
meaning: सायमाहुत्याम्̐ हुतायां चेद् दुर्बलः स्यात् तदैव प्रातराहुतिस् तत् सम्̐स्थाश्रुतेर् अग्निहोत्रस्य //
text_mt: If he becomes weak after the evening oblation has been offered, the morning oblation [is offered] right then, because of the scriptural text concerning the conclusion of that Agnihotra.
And at the end of the Full-Moon sacrifice, [he performs] the New-Moon sacrifice, like the Agnihotra.

sanskrit_iast: haviṣyeṣu ced āhriyamāṇeṣu maraṇam dakṣiṇāgnāv enānt saṃdahet //
meaning: हविष्येषु चेद् आह्रियमाणेषु मरणम् दक्षिणाग्नाव् एनान्त् संदहेत् //
text_mt: If death occurs while the sacrificial materials are being brought, he should burn them together in the Dakṣiṇa fire.
[The rites] from the taking up onwards prior to setting down [are performed] in the Gārhapatya.
Or it is to be brought to conclusion, because it has been prepared.
They place the cauldrons on the fire with kindling.

sanskrit_iast: saṃtāpajān agnīn ādāya saśarīrā dakṣiṇā gachanti //
meaning: संतापजान् अग्नीन् आदाय सशरीरा दक्षिणा गछन्ति //
text_mt: Having taken the fires produced by heat, accompanied by the body, they go to the south.

sanskrit_iast: vitānam̐ sādhayitvā same bahulatṛṇe 'ntarāgnī citiṃ cinoti //
meaning: वितानम्̐ साधयित्वा समे बहुलतृणे ऽन्तराग्नी चितिं चिनोति //
text_mt: Having arranged the fire enclosure on level [ground] with abundant grass, he piles the funeral pyre between the fires.
having uprooted milky plants bearing human names,
and Viśākhaśara, Aśmagnandhā, Pṛśniparṇī, and Adhyāṇḍā.
Having cut the hair of his head, beard, nails, and body hair, and desiring [the body to be] free of feces,

sanskrit_iast: keśādi nikhāya sarpiṣāntar aktvā citāv enam ādadhāti kṛṣṇājinam āstīrya prākśirasam //
meaning: केशादि निखाय सर्पिषान्तर् अक्त्वा चिताव् एनम् आदधाति कृष्णाजिनम् आस्तीर्य प्राक्शिरसम् //
text_mt: having buried the hair and the like, [and] having anointed [him] inside with clarified butter, he places him on the funeral pyre after spreading a black antelope skin, with his head facing east.

sanskrit_iast: saptasu prāṇāyataneṣu sapta hiraṇyaśakalān prāsyati mukhe prathamam //
meaning: सप्तसु प्राणायतनेषु सप्त हिरण्यशकलान् प्रास्यति मुखे प्रथमम् //
text_mt: He throws seven gold pieces into the seven vital seats, first in the mouth.
In the right hand he places the Juhū ladle filled with clarified butter,
the Agnihotra ladle on the mouth;
the two Prāśitra vessels on the ears; the cup used for bringing forward the Praṇītā water on the head;

sanskrit_iast: udare pātrīm̐ samavattadhānīṃ pṛṣadājyavatīm̐ śiśne śamyām araṇī vṛṣaṇayoḥ //
meaning: उदरे पात्रीम्̐ समवत्तधानीं पृषदाज्यवतीम्̐ शिश्ने शम्याम् अरणी वृषणयोः //
text_mt: the vessel for holding the portions containing clotted butter on the belly; the sacrificial pin on the penis; the two kindling sticks on the testicles;
the other sacrificial vessels between the thighs.
Throwing into the waters is [prescribed] for earthenware and stone vessels.
Or he should give the metal vessels to a Brahmin.

sanskrit_iast: anustaraṇī cet paścāt karṇam āhatya hastayor vṛkau //
meaning: अनुस्तरणी चेत् पश्चात् कर्णम् आहत्य हस्तयोर् वृकौ //
text_mt: If there is a covering animal, having severed [its] ear from behind, [he places] the two kidneys in the hands;
"Limb to limbs," says Jātūkarṇya.
Having covered the face with the omentum, they kindle [the pyre] with the fires.

sanskrit_iast: āhutiṃ juhoti putro bhrātānyo vā brāhmaṇo asmāt tvam adhi jāto 'si \ tvad ayaṃ jāyatāṃ punaḥ \ asau svargāya lokāya svāhā \\ iti //
meaning: आहुतिं जुहोति पुत्रो भ्रातान्यो वा ब्राह्मणो अस्मात् त्वम् अधि जातो ऽसि \ त्वद् अयं जायतां पुनः \ असौ स्वर्गाय लोकाय स्वाहा \\ इति //
text_mt: The son, a brother, or another Brahmin offers an oblation with the formula: "From him you were born; from you may he be born again, so-and-so, for the heavenly world, svāhā!"
Coming away without looking back, they touch water.

sanskrit_iast: saṃcayanaṃ caturthyām ayugmān brāhmaṇān bhojayitvā palāśavṛntenāsthīni parivartyaparivartyāṅguṣṭhakaniṣṭhikābhyām ādāya palāśapuṭe prāsyati //
meaning: संचयनं चतुर्थ्याम् अयुग्मान् ब्राह्मणान् भोजयित्वा पलाशवृन्तेनास्थीनि परिवर्त्यपरिवर्त्याङ्गुष्ठकनिष्ठिकाभ्याम् आदाय पलाशपुटे प्रास्यति //
text_mt: On the fourth day, the gathering of bones takes place: having fed an uneven number of Brahmins, turning the bones over and over with a Palāśa stalk, [and] taking them with the thumb and little finger, he casts them into a Palāśa cup.
[There are] Śamī-bark, Avakā plants, and mud at the cemetery.

sanskrit_iast: aktvāsthīni sarvasurabhimiśrāṇi dakṣiṇapūrvāyatāṃ karṣūṃ khātvā kuśān āstīrya vastrāvṛkṛttaṃ ca hāridraṃ vāk \\ iti nivapaty asmin //
meaning: अक्त्वास्थीनि सर्वसुरभिमिश्राणि दक्षिणपूर्वायतां कर्षूं खात्वा कुशान् आस्तीर्य वस्त्रावृकृत्तं च हारिद्रं वाक् \\ इति निवपत्य् अस्मिन् //
text_mt: Having anointed the bones mixed with all fragrant substances, having dug a furrow extending south-east, having strewn Kuśa grass, and [spreading] an uncut yellow garment, he deposits [them] in this with the formula: "Speech!"

sanskrit_iast: tvā manasānārtena vācā brahmaṇā trayyā vidyayā pṛthivyāmakṣikāyāmapām̐ rase nivapāmyasāviti //
meaning: त्वा मनसानार्तेन वाचा ब्रह्मणा त्रय्या विद्यया पृथिव्यामक्षिकायामपाम्̐ रसे निवपाम्यसाविति //
text_mt: "Thee, with a sound mind, with voice, with the Brahman, with the threefold knowledge, do I deposit, so-and-so, in the earth, in the fly, in the sap of the waters!"
For one who intends to erect a sepulchral mound, the gathering of bones is into an urn,

sanskrit_iast: proṣitaś cet preyāt prācīnāvītī nivānyāṃ dugdhvā dakṣiṇato 'dhiśrayaṇodvāsane //
meaning: प्रोषितश् चेत् प्रेयात् प्राचीनावीती निवान्यां दुग्ध्वा दक्षिणतो ऽधिश्रयणोद्वासने //
text_mt: If he dies while abroad, having put on the sacred thread over the right shoulder, having milked [a cow whose calf was reared by another] into a Nivānyā pot, the heating and removal are on the south side;
holding a firestick underneath,
having made Kuśa grass whose tips point north point south,
or having strewn once as in rites for the Fathers.

sanskrit_iast: śarīrāṇy āhṛtya kṛṣṇājine puruṣavidhiṃ vidhāyorṇābhiḥ prachādyājyenābhighārya pūrvavaddāhaḥ //
meaning: शरीराण्य् आहृत्य कृष्णाजिने पुरुषविधिं विधायोर्णाभिः प्रछाद्याज्येनाभिघार्य पूर्ववद्दाहः //
text_mt: Having brought the bones, having arranged the human form on a black antelope skin, having covered it with wool, [and] having basted it with clarified butter, the burning takes place as before.

sanskrit_iast: śarīranāśe trīṇi ṣaṣṭiśatāni palāśavṛntānāṃ kṛṣṇājine pūrvavat //
meaning: शरीरनाशे त्रीणि षष्टिशतानि पलाशवृन्तानां कृष्णाजिने पूर्ववत् //
text_mt: In case of the loss of the bones, [he arranges] three hundred and sixty Palāśa leaf-stalks on a black antelope skin as before.

sanskrit_iast: aniṣṭvāgrayaṇena navasyāśnīyāt patitasya bhuktvā pratigṛhya vidviṣāṇayor vāyājyaṃ yājayitvāviṃ pratigṛhyobhayādad vā yasyāgnibhir anyaṃ yājayeyur yo vā yajeta vaiśvānaraṃ nirvapet //
meaning: अनिष्ट्वाग्रयणेन नवस्याश्नीयात् पतितस्य भुक्त्वा प्रतिगृह्य विद्विषाणयोर् वायाज्यं याजयित्वाविं प्रतिगृह्योभयादद् वा यस्याग्निभिर् अन्यं याजयेयुर् यो वा यजेत वैश्वानरं निर्वपेत् //
text_mt: If one should eat of the new grain without having offered the Āgrayaṇa sacrifice, or having eaten the food of an outcaste, or having accepted a gift [from him], or having officiated at a sacrifice for two mutual enemies, or having accepted a sheep or an animal with two rows of teeth, or if another should sacrifice with his fires, or if he should sacrifice [for another with them], he should offer an oblation to Vaiśvānara.

sanskrit_iast: puroḍāśe kṣāme 'vaśiṣṭam̐ samāpya tad eva punar nirvapet //
meaning: पुरोडाशे क्षामे ऽवशिष्टम्̐ समाप्य तद् एव पुनर् निर्वपेत् //
text_mt: If the sacrificial cake is scorched, having finished [the rite] with what remains, he should offer that same oblation again.
Even if only a portion is burnt, [it is replaced] because of its association [with the whole offering],

sanskrit_iast: paśuś ced upākṛtaḥ palāyeta vāyave tam anudiśyānyaṃ tadvarṇaṃ tadvayasam ālabheta //
meaning: पशुश् चेद् उपाकृतः पलायेत वायवे तम् अनुदिश्यान्यं तद्वर्णं तद्वयसम् आलभेत //
text_mt: If the victim that has been dedicated should run away, having assigned it to Vāyu, he should immolate another of the same color and the same age.

sanskrit_iast: prāk prayājebhyaś cen niyukto mriyetānyam ālabheta //
meaning: प्राक् प्रयाजेभ्यश् चेन् नियुक्तो म्रियेतान्यम् आलभेत //
text_mt: If it dies after being bound, before the fore-offerings, he should immolate another.
He should offer the omentum of the former victim in the Dakṣiṇa fire;

sanskrit_iast: somaś cen mārjālīye ya ījānāḥ pitaro ye pitāmahās \\ ye 'nījānā yajñiyāḥ somapāsas \ teṣām eṣa paśur ālabdho 'gnau \ svāhā devebhyaḥ suhuto yamāya \\ iti //
meaning: सोमश् चेन् मार्जालीये य ईजानाः पितरो ये पितामहास् \\ ये ऽनीजाना यज्ञियाः सोमपासस् \ तेषाम् एष पशुर् आलब्धो ऽग्नौ \ स्वाहा देवेभ्यः सुहुतो यमाय \\ इति //
text_mt: if it is a Soma sacrifice, in the Mārjālīya fire with: "The fathers who have sacrificed, the grandfathers who have sacrificed, those who have not sacrificed, worthy of worship, Soma-drinkers—for them this animal has been immolated in the fire; svāhā to the gods, well-offered to Yama!"
Or there should be no removal [of the carcass], because it is not spoiled.
In case of the loss of an apportioned cutting, he should not pay heed to it.

sanskrit_iast: hṛdayanāśe tv anyam ālabhetety eke hṛdayaṃ paśur iti śruteḥ //
meaning: हृदयनाशे त्व् अन्यम् आलभेतेत्य् एके हृदयं पशुर् इति श्रुतेः //
text_mt: In case of the loss of the heart, however, some say he should immolate another, because of the Vedic text: "The heart is the animal."
Or he should sacrifice with clarified butter for all [missing portions].
The statement about the animal is merely an explanatory commendation.

sanskrit_iast: saṃjñapyamānaś ced vāśyetāhutiṃ juhuyāt yat paśur māyum akṛta \\ uro vā padbhir āhate \ agnir mā tasmād enasas \\ viśvān muñcatv am̐hasas \\ iti //
meaning: संज्ञप्यमानश् चेद् वाश्येताहुतिं जुहुयात् यत् पशुर् मायुम् अकृत \\ उरो वा पद्भिर् आहते \ अग्निर् मा तस्माद् एनसस् \\ विश्वान् मुञ्चत्व् अम्̐हसस् \\ इति //
text_mt: If it bleats while being quieted, he should offer an oblation with: "When the animal made a cry, or struck its chest with its feet, may Agni release me from that guilt, from all distress!"

sanskrit_iast: imaṃ me varuṇa \\ iti ca pratyṛcaṃ dvābhyām //
meaning: इमं मे वरुण \\ इति च प्रत्यृचं द्वाभ्याम् //
text_mt: And with the two verses beginning: "This of mine, O Varuṇa...", verse by verse.

sanskrit_iast: paśūkhā cet sravet sāṃnāyyokhā vā tām abhimantrayeta \\ ukhām̐ sravantīm agadām aganma \ tvaṣṭā vāyuḥ pṛthivy antarikṣam \ yata ścutad dhutam agnau tad astu \ na tat prāpnoti nirṛtiḥ parastāt \\ iti //
meaning: पशूखा चेत् स्रवेत् सांनाय्योखा वा ताम् अभिमन्त्रयेत \\ उखाम्̐ स्रवन्तीम् अगदाम् अगन्म \ त्वष्टा वायुः पृथिव्य् अन्तरिक्षम् \ यत श्चुतद् धुतम् अग्नौ तद् अस्तु \ न तत् प्राप्नोति निरृतिः परस्तात् \\ इति //
text_mt: If the pot of the animal [offering] or the pot of the Sāṃnāyya curd-and-milk should leak, he should recite over it: "We have approached the leaking pot made whole; Tvaṣṭṛ, Vāyu, Earth, Atmosphere; whatever dripped, may that be offered in the fire; Nirṛti does not reach that from beyond."
If a sprout grows on the sacrificial post, [the expiation takes place] within the common procedure on the completed day.
He should seize [an animal] of many forms dedicated to Tvaṣṭṛ.

sanskrit_iast: anūbandhyāyai vapām utkhidyānumarśaṃ garbham eṣṭavai brūyāt //
meaning: अनूबन्ध्यायै वपाम् उत्खिद्यानुमर्शं गर्भम् एष्टवै ब्रूयात् //
text_mt: Having extracted the omentum of the anūbandhyā cow, feeling [inside], he should direct [the assistant] to search for an embryo.
Upon seeing [it], he should direct [him] to prepare an earthen pot and a turban.

sanskrit_iast: vapānte 'napekṣam adhvaryuḥ preṣyati nirūhaitaṃ garbham iti virujya śroṇī pratyañcaṃ nirūhitavai brūyāt //
meaning: वपान्ते ऽनपेक्षम् अध्वर्युः प्रेष्यति निरूहैतं गर्भम् इति विरुज्य श्रोणी प्रत्यञ्चं निरूहितवै ब्रूयात् //
text_mt: At the conclusion of the omentum rite, without looking back, the Adhvaryu commands: "Extract this embryo!" Having broken the hip-bones, he should tell him to drag it out toward the west.

sanskrit_iast: niruhyamāṇam abhimantrayate \\ ejatu daśamāsyas \\ iti paśuvad avadānaṃ garbhasya //
meaning: निरुह्यमाणम् अभिमन्त्रयते \\ एजतु दशमास्यस् \\ इति पशुवद् अवदानं गर्भस्य //
text_mt: While it is being dragged out, he addresses it with: "May the ten-month-old move..." The taking of sacrificial portions of the embryo is like that of an animal.
Or, having slit the throat, the draining of the fat into the pot [takes place].

sanskrit_iast: avadānasahitam adhiśrityoṣṇīṣaveṣṭitaṃ garbhaṃ pārśvato nidadhāty anabhighāritam avadānavad dhṛtvā dakṣiṇato medhaṃ nidadhāti //
meaning: अवदानसहितम् अधिश्रित्योष्णीषवेष्टितं गर्भं पार्श्वतो निदधात्य् अनभिघारितम् अवदानवद् धृत्वा दक्षिणतो मेधं निदधाति //
text_mt: Having placed [the pot] on the fire along with the sacrificial portions, he deposits the embryo wrapped in the turban to the side unbasted [with clarified butter]; having held [the pot] like the portions, he places the fat to the south.
At the time of taking portions from the barren cow, the Pratiprasthātṛ takes portions of the fat into the pracaraṇī spoon.

sanskrit_iast: avadānāny anu juhoti yasyai te \\ iti //
meaning: अवदानान्य् अनु जुहोति यस्यै ते \\ इति //
text_mt: After the portions, he offers with: "For her whose..."

sanskrit_iast: aṅgāny ahrutā yasya yasyā iti yathāliṅgam //
meaning: अङ्गान्य् अह्रुता यस्य यस्या इति यथालिङ्गम् //
text_mt: According to the gender marker: "The limbs uninjured of whom [masculine]..." or "of whom [feminine]..."

sanskrit_iast: sviṣṭakṛdvanaspatyantare pratyetya pratiprasthātā pracaraṇyām̐ sarvaṃ medham avadyati //
meaning: स्विष्टकृद्वनस्पत्यन्तरे प्रत्येत्य प्रतिप्रस्थाता प्रचरण्याम्̐ सर्वं मेधम् अवद्यति //
text_mt: Between the Sviṣṭakṛt and Vanaspati [offerings], having returned, the Pratiprasthātṛ cuts all the fat into the pracaraṇī spoon.
After the Sviṣṭakṛt offering, he offers with: "Doing many wondrous deeds..."

sanskrit_iast: sviṣṭakṛdanta uṣṇīṣaveṣṭitasya vṛkṣāsañjanaṃ vāpsv avaharaṇaṃ vākhūtkaropakiraṇaṃ vā //
meaning: स्विष्टकृदन्त उष्णीषवेष्टितस्य वृक्षासञ्जनं वाप्स्व् अवहरणं वाखूत्करोपकिरणं वा //
text_mt: At the end of the Sviṣṭakṛt offering, the hanging of [the embryo] wrapped in the turban onto a tree, or casting [it] into water, or covering it with an earthworm-heap [takes place].
However, in these [methods], there is the danger of imprecation.

sanskrit_iast: samiṣṭayajurante śāmitra eva juhuyāt tiṣṭhan marutas \\ ity asvāhākṛtya mahī dyaur ity aṅgārair abhyūhati //
meaning: समिष्टयजुरन्ते शामित्र एव जुहुयात् तिष्ठन् मरुतस् \\ इत्य् अस्वाहाकृत्य मही द्यौर् इत्य् अङ्गारैर् अभ्यूहति //
text_mt: At the end of the samiṣṭayajus formulas, standing right at the slaughtering place, he should offer with: "O Maruts..." without pronouncing "svāhā", [and] he covers [it] with coals, reciting: "Great Heaven..."

sanskrit_iast: agnihotra āsanneṣu cet pātreṣv āhavanīyo 'nugached gārhapatye juhuyāt prāṇa udānam apyagāt \\ iti //
meaning: अग्निहोत्र आसन्नेषु चेत् पात्रेष्व् आहवनीयो ऽनुगछेद् गार्हपत्ये जुहुयात् प्राण उदानम् अप्यगात् \\ इति //
text_mt: In the Agnihotra, if the Āhavanīya fire should go out when the vessels are set down, he should offer in the Gārhapatya fire with: "The out-breath has merged into the up-breath."

sanskrit_iast: gārhapatyaś ced āhavanīye \\ udānaḥ prāṇam apyagāt \\ iti //
meaning: गार्हपत्यश् चेद् आहवनीये \\ उदानः प्राणम् अप्यगात् \\ इति //
text_mt: If the Gārhapatya fire [goes out], [he offers] in the Āhavanīya fire with: "The up-breath has merged into the out-breath."

sanskrit_iast: dakṣiṇāgniś ced gārhapatye vyāna udānam apyagāt \\ iti //
meaning: दक्षिणाग्निश् चेद् गार्हपत्ये व्यान उदानम् अप्यगात् \\ इति //
text_mt: If the Dakṣiṇa fire [goes out], [he offers] in the Gārhapatya fire with: "The cross-breath has merged into the up-breath."

sanskrit_iast: sarve cet tūrṇaṃ mathitvā prativātam uddhṛtya vāyavyām āhutim̐ hutvā yathānupūrvyakaraṇam //
meaning: सर्वे चेत् तूर्णं मथित्वा प्रतिवातम् उद्धृत्य वायव्याम् आहुतिम्̐ हुत्वा यथानुपूर्व्यकरणम् //
text_mt: If all [go out], having churned [fire] swiftly, having carried it out against the wind, [and] having offered an oblation to Vāyu, the performance is according to regular sequence.

sanskrit_iast: nivātaṃ cet pūrvavan mathitvā prāñcam uddhṛtya gārhapatye saṃskṛtya paścād āhavanīyasya svayaṃ pānam //
meaning: निवातं चेत् पूर्ववन् मथित्वा प्राञ्चम् उद्धृत्य गार्हपत्ये संस्कृत्य पश्चाद् आहवनीयस्य स्वयं पानम् //
text_mt: If [the fire goes out] sheltered from the wind, having churned as before, having carried it forward, [and] having consecrated [the milk] on the Gārhapatya fire, the drinking [of it] by himself [takes place] behind the Āhavanīya fire.

sanskrit_iast: agnihotrātipattāv āhutiṃ juhuyāt \\ mano jyotir juṣatām ājyasya \ vichinnaṃ yajñam̐ sam imaṃ dadhātu \ yā iṣṭā uṣaso yā aniṣṭās \ tāḥ saṃtanomi haviṣā ghṛtena svāhā \\ iti //
meaning: अग्निहोत्रातिपत्ताव् आहुतिं जुहुयात् \\ मनो ज्योतिर् जुषताम् आज्यस्य \ विछिन्नं यज्ञम्̐ सम् इमं दधातु \ या इष्टा उषसो या अनिष्टास् \ ताः संतनोमि हविषा घृतेन स्वाहा \\ इति //
text_mt: Upon the omission of the Agnihotra, he should offer an oblation with: "May Mind, the light, partake of the clarified butter; may it reunite this severed sacrifice. Whatever dawns have been sacrificed to, whatever have not been sacrificed to, them do I unite with oblation, with clarified butter, svāhā!"
If one has resolved upon a sacrificial session and is unable [to perform it], he should sacrifice with the Viśvajit Atirātra.
Or it is a subsidiary rite of the sacrificial session, because only the resolution is heard [in the text].

sanskrit_iast: dīkṣitānāṃ cet sāmyutthānaṃ jāyeta somaṃ vibhajya tenaiva sarvavedasena sarvapṛṣṭhena yajeran //
meaning: दीक्षितानां चेत् साम्युत्थानं जायेत सोमं विभज्य तेनैव सर्ववेदसेन सर्वपृष्ठेन यजेरन् //
text_mt: If mid-way abandonment should occur for the consecrated performers, having divided the soma, they should sacrifice with that very [soma] in a rite where all one's possessions are given as dakṣiṇā and with all Pṛṣṭha stotras.
The division [is prescribed] because it is a qualification of the action.

meaning: अनीतासु चेद् दक्षिणासूद्गात्रपछेदो ऽदक्षिणम्̐ सम्̐स्थाप्य पुनराहारः //
text_mt: If the interruption of the Udgātṛ's chant occurs before the sacrificial gifts are led forward, having brought the rite to completion without sacrificial gifts, there is repetition [of the sacrifice].

sanskrit_iast: prastotā ced brahmaṇe varaṃ dattvā punarvaraṇam //
meaning: प्रस्तोता चेद् ब्रह्मणे वरं दत्त्वा पुनर्वरणम् //
text_mt: If the Prastotṛ [causes the interruption], having given a choice gift to the Brahman, there is a re-election [of the priests].
If the Pratihartṛ [causes the interruption], all one's possessions are to be given [as sacrificial gift].
If simultaneously, there is an option due to the conflict.
In a temporal sequence, the earlier is weaker, as in the archetype rite.
On whichever day the interruption of the Udgātṛ's chant occurs in a multi-day sacrifice, there is repetition of that [day].

sanskrit_iast: patny udakyā dīkṣārūpāṇi nidhāya sikatāsv āsītopasravaṇāt //
meaning: पत्न्य् उदक्या दीक्षारूपाणि निधाय सिकतास्व् आसीतोपस्रवणात् //
text_mt: If the wife is menstruating, having laid aside the marks of consecration, she should sit on sand until the discharge ceases.
She should stand at the two twilight times.

sanskrit_iast: trirātrānte gomūtramiśreṇodakena snāpayitvā paridhānādi karoti sāṃnipātikam //
meaning: त्रिरात्रान्ते गोमूत्रमिश्रेणोदकेन स्नापयित्वा परिधानादि करोति सांनिपातिकम् //
text_mt: At the end of three nights, having bathed her with water mixed with cow's urine, he performs the putting on of garments and the like, which are associated rites.
And for a woman who has given birth, the bathing and other rites [take place] after ten nights.
